## About Assets in AEM

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/about-assets-aem
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Remediate for AEM > About Assets in AEM
- Last modified: 2026-04-12T07:06Z
- Summary: Information on the Assets page in the Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) application of the SecOps platform.

The Assets page provides a centralized view of your organization's assets in the Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) app.Each asset represents a single asset in your environment, unified (i.e., merged) and enriched with information from multiple sources. On this page, you can explore asset details and statuses, view the sources and records from which it was merged, view the findings it contains, and view the tickets it's related to.

The Assets page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Access and organize assets using system-saved views, filters, grouping options, and customizable table columns to focus on specific scenarios.
- Explore detailed information about each asset, including associated tickets and findings, risk scores, ownership, and the sources that the assets were detected on.
- Understand how the asset was merged from multiple sources into a unified entity.

## About the Assets Page

On the Assets page (Assets > Assets), you can do the following:

1. Select from system-saved views, or views [you previously saved](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/creating-managing-saved-views).
  - List of System-Saved Views
2. Search for specific assets by entering keywords in the search bar.
3. [Save your view](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/creating-managing-saved-views) for quick access after making adjustments to it (e.g., applying filters, adjusting columns, or grouping).
4. [Filter](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/using-filters) assets by **Asset Is Crown Jewel, State**, **Owner ID**, or **Source**.
5. Explore the **Overview**charts to gain high-level insights into the assets and their risk level in your environment. The charts are adjusted by the selected view and filters.
  - **Number of Assets by Risk Score**: Displays the number of assets in the different risk score ranges (in increments of 0.5). The X-axis represents the max severity score of active findings related to the asset, and the colors represent the risk category. You can hover over the bars to view the number of assets and the exact score range.
  - **Asset Count by Type**: Presents the asset count categorized by asset type, displaying the 5 most frequently occurring types.
  - **Asset Count by Operating System**: Displays the number of assets categorized by operating system, displaying the 5 most frequently occurring types.
6. [Group assets](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/grouping-data-entity-pages) by fields such as **Asset State**, **Asset ID**, or **Asset Owner ID**.
7. Refresh the page to reflect the most current information.
8. Export the list of assets and their associated details as a CSV file.
9. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/managing-table-columns)
10. Select all assets on the page.
11. Click an asset to open individual asset drawers. When the default **Active**saved view is selected, you can see the following details for each asset:
  - **ID**: The asset's ID on the in the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform.
  - **Type**: The asset type (e.g., **Windows Workstation**, **Web Application**, **Container Image**).
  - **Name**: The asset's name.
  - **Risk Score**: The risk level of findings associated with the asset. The risk score is initially set by the default [reconciliation function](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/attribute-reconciliation-default-functions), and reflects the highest severity score among the findings. The default can be customized through [Data Unification](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/what-data-unification).
  - **Risk Mass**: The sum of all severity scores of the active findings associated with the asset.
  - **Owner ID**: The unit in the organization assigned to handling the asset.
  - **Sources**: The sources that the information on the asset is retrieved from.
  - **Is Crown** **Jewel**: A boolean field with values of **TRUE**or **FALSE**indicating whether the asset is defined as a crown jewel asset (i.e., one of your organization's most valuable assets).
  - **Site**: The site that the asset is located on.
  - **First Seen**: The earliest date on which a finding on the asset was first detected.
  - **Last Seen**: The latest date on which a finding on the asset was detected.
  - **Total Findings**: The sum of the active findings per severity.
  - **Tags**: Tags pulled from your sources that include information about the asset that can be [extracted](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/configuring-field-unification) and used to enrich the asset data.

[Image: about assets operational view]

The Assets page includes system views with predefined filter selections, providing quick access to common data scopes:

- **Active**: All active assets (i.e., all assets ingested into the account from your sources that have not been aged yet). This is the default view.
- **Vulnerable**: All active assets that have at least one active finding.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Policy Violations

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/about-policy-violations
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Remediate for AEM > About Policy Violations
- Last modified: 2025-11-19T14:58Z
- Summary: Information on the Policy Violations page in the Asset Exposure Management (AEM) application in the SecOps platform.

The Policy Violations page provides a centralized overview of all policy violations within your organization's AEM app. Each policy violation represents a deviation from established security policies detected on an asset and aggregated with additional contextual information such as severity, violation origins, and affected asset types. On this page, you can explore policy violation details, analyze their impact, prioritize remediation actions, and streamline workflows using risk-driven insights.

The Policy Violations page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Access and organize policy violations using system-saved views, filters, grouping options, and customizable table columns to focus on specific scenarios or issues.
- Dive into detailed information about each policy violation to prioritize actions effectively.
- Dispatch policy violations to external platforms (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow) to streamline workflows and remediation processes.

## About the Policy Violations Page

On the Policy Violations page (Assets > Policy Violations), you can do the following:

1. Select from system-saved views, or views [you previously saved](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-managing-saved-views). System-saved views with predefined filter selections include:
  - **Active Violations**: All active policy violations.
  - **Active Critical and High Violations**: Active policy violations with critical or high severity.
  - **CMDB Hygiene Policy Violations**: Policy violations generated by the CMDB Hygiene policy.
  - **Coverage Policy Violations**: Policy violations generated by the Tool Coverage policy.
2. Search for specific violations by entering keywords in the search bar.
3. [Save your view](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-managing-saved-views) for quick access after making adjustments to it (e.g., applying filters, adjusting columns, or grouping).
4. [Filter](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/using-filters) policy violations by **Severity**, **Policy Name**, **State**, or **Asset Type**.
5. Explore the **Overview**charts to gain high-level insights into policy violations and their risk levels in your environment. The charts are adjusted based on the selected view and filters:
  - **Policy violations by severity**: Displays a breakdown of violations grouped by their severity level.
  - **Policy violations by policy name**: Displays a breakdown of violations grouped by the policy they were generated from.
  - **Policy violations by asset type**: Highlights the affected asset types, such as Applications or Windows Workloads.
6. Apply actions to multiple policy violations:
  - **Update**: Update the details of a group of selected violations (e.g., resolution SLA, assignment).
  - **Create 3rd party Issue**: Dispatch selected violations to external work management systems (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow).
7. [Group policy violations](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/grouping-operational-views-group) by fields such as **Severity**, **Asset Type**, **Policy Name**, or **Assignee**.
8. Refresh the page to reflect the most current information.
9. Export the list of policy violations and their associated details as a CSV file for offline analysis or reporting.
10. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/managing-table-columns)
11. Select all policy violations on the page.
12. Click a policy violation to open individual [policy violation drawers](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/managing-policy-violations-aem). When the default **Active Violations**saved view is selected, you can see the following details for each policy violation:
  - **ID**: The unique AEM policy violation ID.
  - **Severity Score**: The severity score assigned to the policy violation in the [configured policy](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/configuring-asset-compliance-policies).
  - **Title**: The name or description of the policy violation.
  - **Asset Type**: The category or classification of the asset related to the policy violation (e.g., server, application, device).
  - **First Seen**: The date the policy violation was generated.
  - **Last Seen**: The most recent date that the policy violation was still detected.

[Image: about policy violations operational view]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Violation Tickets

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/about-violation-tickets
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Remediate for AEM > About Violation Tickets
- Last modified: 2025-11-11T13:49Z
- Summary: Information on the Violation Tickets page in the Asset Exposure Management (AEM) application in the SecOps platform.

The Violation Tickets page provides a centralized overview of your organization's compliance-related tickets in AEM. Each violation ticket aggregates related policy violations into a single work item, helping you streamline actions needed to address compliance and operational risks. On this page, you can explore violation ticket details and statuses, assign tickets, and dispatch tasks to external platforms (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow).

The Violation Tickets page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Access and organize violation tickets using system-saved views, filters, grouping options, and customizable table columns to focus on specific scenarios.
- Dive into detailed violation ticket information to prioritize actions, assign owners, and understand associated policies and affected assets.
- Dispatch violation tickets to external platforms (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow) to streamline workflows and remediation processes.

## About the Violation Tickets Page

On the Violation Tickets page (Assets > Violation Tickets), you can do the following:

1. Select from system-saved views, or views [you previously saved](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-managing-saved-views). The Active view is the system default, which displays all violation tickets with at least one active policy violation.
2. Search for specific tickets by entering keywords in the search bar.
3. [Save your view](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-managing-saved-views) for quick access after making adjustments to it (e.g., applying filters, adjusting columns, or grouping).
4. [Filter](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/using-filters) violation tickets by **Severity**, **State**, **Assignee**, or **Policy Violation Count**.
5. Apply actions to multiple violation tickets:
  - **Update**: Update the details of a group of selected violation tickets.
  - **Merge**: Merge multiple selected tickets into one violation ticket.
  - **Create 3rd party Issue**: Dispatch a group of selected violation tickets to external work management systems.
6. [Group violation tickets](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/grouping-operational-views-group) by fields such as **Policy**, **Severity**, or **Assignee**.
7. Refresh the page to reflect the most current information.
8. Export the list of violation tickets and their associated details as a CSV file.
9. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/managing-table-columns)
10. Select multiple violations.
11. Click a violation ticket to open individual [violation ticket drawers](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/managing-violation-tickets-aem). When the default **Active**saved view is selected, you can see the following details for each violation ticket:
  - **ID**: The unique AEM violation ticket ID.
  - **Severity Score**: The severity score assigned to the violation ticket, calculated based on the severity scores of the policy violations within the violation ticket (e.g., using the highest score or the average score).
  - **Title**: The violation ticket title.
  - **SLA**: The service-level agreement (SLA) deadline for the violation ticket.
  - **Assignee**: The remediation owner assigned to remediate the ticket.
  - **Status**: The current status of the ticket.
  - **Remediation**: The percentage of policy violations resolved within the violation ticket.
  - **Policy Violation Count**: The total number of policy violations in the ticket.
  - **Asset Count**: The number of affected assets linked to the ticket.

[Image: about violation tickets operational view]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Configuring Asset Compliance Policies

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/configuring-asset-compliance-policies
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Settings for AEM > Configuring Asset Compliance Policies
- Last modified: 2025-11-11T14:07Z
- Summary: How to configure asset compliance policies in Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM).

Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) allows organizations to collect and manage asset data from various sources to track and manage asset inventory and coverage. With AEM, you can create policies that ensure asset compliance across your organization's assets.

Two primary benefits include:

- Ensuring your organization's Configuration Management Database (CMDB) contains a comprehensive and accurate inventory of assets.
- Identifying and tracking tool coverage gaps.

Policy rules are designed to generate policy violations on assets that are out of compliance with a given security standard in your organization. Policy violations can then be assigned to a designated owner, tracked against a specific SLA deadline, and prioritized with a severity score. When assigned, these violations can be dispatched to relevant team members for prompt action. Automatically alerting you to policy violations helps organizations operationalize efforts to drive compliance with asset-related policies.

## Creating Policies

Creating new policies for tracking asset compliance involves selecting the policy category, defining the asset population that the policy applies to, and setting the policy scenario (i.e., the conditions that generate a policy violation).

For access to Policies, your assigned role must include the Read, Create, Edit permissions under the Assets App > Policy Rule resource. To learn more, see [Creating Custom Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-custom-roles) and [Assigning Roles to Users](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/assigning-roles-users). The Asset Admin can create and manage policies, but can't delete them.

To create a new policy:

1. Go to **Assets**> **Policies**.
2. Click **Create**. See image. The **Create New Policy**page appears.
3. On the **Create New Policy**page, configure the following sections:
  - Details
  - Policy Criteria
  - Formatting Rule
  - Trigger Settings
  - Policy Violation Findings
4. Click **Preview**to test and adjust the policy configuration. This displays the top 50 policy violations generated by the policy.

After creating and saving a policy, assets that violate the policy automatically generate policy violations, which can be viewed and monitored on the [Policy Violations](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/about-policy-violations-operational-view-aem) page. The policy violations are aggregated into violation tickets that can be tracked on the [Violation Tickets](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/about-violation-tickets-operational-view-aem) page.

You can manage and adjust the policy's settings and criteria in the Policies table. To learn more, see [Managing Asset Compliance Policies](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/managing-asset-compliance-policies).

### Save & Run Ruleset

After creating the policy, save the policy to complete the process in one of the following ways:

- Click **Save**to save the policy. The policy will apply the next time data is ingested into your account.
- In the **Save**drop-down menu, click **Save & Run**to save the policy and immediately run it.

To set the policy's basic details:

- **Title**: Enter a name that reflects the policy violations it generates.
- **Description**: (Optional) Enter a brief description of the policy violations.
- **Category**: Select one of the following options: The selected category modifies the available configuration options in the **Policy Criteria**settings.
  - **CMDB Hygiene**: Flag assets with incomplete, inaccurate, or inconsistent data in your CMDB. This maintains a reliable, accurate, and comprehensive asset inventory. To learn more, see [Using the CMDB Hygiene Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/using-cmdb-hygiene-policy).
  - **Tool Coverage**: Flag assets that lack coverage from a specific tool used in your security stack, such as EDR tools. This ensures your assets are covered by the necessary security tools required by your organization. To learn more, see [Using the Tool Coverage Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/using-tool-coverage-policy).
  - **OS End of Life**: Flag assets running operating systems that have reached the end of their supported lifecycle. This mitigates potential security vulnerabilities stemming from outdated OS and strengthens compliance with industry regulations. To learn more, see [Using the OS End of Life Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/using-os-end-life-policy).
  - **Custom**: Create a custom policy tailored to your organization's specific needs. For example, detect and manage assets with outdated tool coverage or assets with conflicting values in key fields, and optionally restrict access until the issue is resolved.
- **Severity**: Set a severity score for the policy violations (this adjusts the severity category accordingly). The severity is reflected in the policy violations, and consequently in the reports and dashboards within your AEM application. The severity indicates the level of risk or impact associated with noncompliant assets identified by the policy, and provides a baseline for efficient prioritization of exposure.

See image.

[Image: create policies button]

[Image: aem policy details section]

In the **Policy Criteria**section, define the asset population for the policy, and then set the conditions that constitute a violation of the policy.

This step defines the Policy Scenario for the relevant Asset Population:

- **Asset Population**: A group of assets that the policy applies to (e.g., Workstations, Cloud Resources). Assets not included in the population criteria are not evaluated for violations.
- **Policy Scenario**: The set of conditions that constitute a policy violation (e.g., the asset is running an outdated software version, or missing an asset owner). See image.

To set the policy criteria:

1. Under **Asset Population**, set the conditions to filter the assets that the policy applies to:
  1. Select a field that the condition should be based on.
  2. Select an operator (e.g., **Equals**, **Contains**). Available operators vary depending on the field type, indicated to the left of the field name.
  3. Enter the value that the rule should apply to.
  4. (Optional) Use **AND**/**OR**logic to define compound rules:
    - **AND**includes assets only if they meet all conditions in the rule.
    - **OR**includes assets if they meet any of the conditions in the rule.
2. Under **Policy Scenario**, set the conditions that constitute a violation of the policy based on the policy category selected in the **Details**section.
  - To configure policy scenarios for system policies using predefined templates (i.e., the Simple setup), see the available system policies:
    - [CMDB Hygiene](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/using-cmdb-hygiene-policy)
    - [Tool Coverage](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/using-tool-coverage-policy)
    - [OS End-of-Life](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/using-os-end-life-policy)
  - To configure policy scenarios for custom policies, or to configure advanced conditions for system policies:
    1. Select the source of the value being evaluated (i.e., **Original Source Value**or**Merged Entity Value**). To learn more, see [Understanding Original Source and Merged Entity Values](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/understanding-original-source-and-merged-entity-values).
    2. Set the conditions for the policy scenario:
      1. Select a field that the condition should be based on.
      2. Select an operator (e.g., **Equals**, **Contains**). Available operators vary depending on the field type, indicated to the left of the field name.
      3. Enter the value that the rule should apply to.
      4. (Optional) Use **AND**/**OR**logic to define compound rules:
        - **AND**applies only if all conditions are met.
        - **OR**applies if any of the conditions are met.

[Image: aem policy criteria]

In the **Formatting Rule**section, set a benchmark formatting rule to display your policy's compliance levels using percentage thresholds. This helps you easily identify and report compliance rates. You can either select an existing formatting rule that applies to the current policy, or create a new rule for the policy. To learn more, see [Creating Formatting Rules](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-formatting-rules).

To create a new formatting rule for the policy:

1. Click **New Rule**. The **Create Formatting Rule**drawer appears.
2. In the **Create Formatting Rule**drawer: See image.
  1. **Name**: Enter a name (e.g., `Policy Compliance Threshold`).
  2. Define the conditions:
    1. Select an operator (e.g., **>**, **<**, **=**, **Between**). If you select **Between**, set both start and end values for the range.
    2. Enter a value for the condition.
    3. Assign a color for the condition (e.g., red for <25%). Green typically represents satisfactory rates, and red represents unsatisfactory rates.
    4. **Fallback Formatting Rule Logic**: Assign a default color to display when no other condition applies to a value.
  3. Click **Done**.

[Image: policy formatting rule drawer]

In the **Trigger Settings**section, set the frequency and time that the policy is run.

To set the trigger settings:

1. In the **Frequency** drop-down menu, select a trigger option:
  - **Daily**: Triggers a policy run at a specified time every day.
  - **Weekly**: Triggers a policy run on a specific day of the week at a specified time.
  - **Monthly**: Triggers a policy run on a specific day of the month at a specified time.
  - **Custom**: Triggers a policy run at a specified interval (e.g., every x hours).
2. Select the time or day as necessary.

See image.

[Image: Policy trigger settings.]

In the **Policy Violation Findings**section, set the title and description of the policy violations.

1. Click the **Title** box. An editor window appears.
2. Select a method for populating the title and the description fields: See image.
  - **Smart Text**: Use free text, or create a template using a combination of free text and field values. To insert field values into the text, enclose the field name in double curly brackets (e.g., `{{Asset Name}}`). The field's display name automatically translates to its system name (e.g., Asset Name → `asset.name`).
  - **Value**: Enter a fixed value for the policy violation title or the policy violation description. This option is static text that is used for all policy violations generated by the policy. A fixed value is useful if you have a standard title or description that applies to all violations of the policy.
  - **Field**: Select a field to dynamically populate the policy violation title or policy violation description with a value from a specific field. For example, select the **Asset Name**field to insert the name of the affected asset in the policy violation title or description.
3. Repeat this procedure for the **Description** box.

[Image: policy title description text editor]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Configuring Discovery Settings

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/configuring-discovery-settings
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > External Attack Surface Management for AEM > Configuring Discovery Settings
- Last modified: 2026-05-17T07:06Z
- Summary: How to configure asset discovery settings in Zscaler's AEM and UVM apps to identify and manage your internet-exposed assets using Zscaler's External Attack Surface Management (EASM) capabilities.

Zscaler's External Attack Surface Management (EASM) capabilities require you to create discovery profiles and configure seeds to initiate the discovery process for internet-exposed assets. A seed is a known, legitimate asset belonging to your organization—such as a domain, IP address, or IP address block—that can be used to discover other assets linked with your organization. You can also use an organization's name as a seed to find related domains by performing a reverse domain lookup.

You can create a discovery profile by including or excluding specific seeds across different asset types. This discovery profile is used to scan for asset connections that are associated with the seeds. Discovery profiles add a layer of granularity to tracking and managing your attack surface by grouping relevant seeds. For example, you can create distinct discovery profiles for different business entities (e.g., parent company, subsidiaries) to individually manage the corresponding attack surfaces.

When you configure and activate your discovery profile, the discovery engine starts scanning the internet for asset connections using seeds to map your organization's attack surface and build an inventory of the internet-exposed assets. After the scan is completed, you can view the unified asset inventory in Asset Exposure Management (AEM), and the risks identified for the assets and enriched security insights in Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM). The asset scan is performed weekly, and the asset and findings data in AEM and UVM is updated to reflect the latest information. In addition, when seeds within a discovery profile are modified, a new scan is triggered to update the asset inventory based on the new set of seeds. Outdated or irrelevant assets are identified and marked inactive depending on your [asset aging](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/aging-assets) configuration.

- To access Zscaler's EASM capabilities, your organization must have either AEM or UVM, or both. EASM functionalities vary between these apps, with AEM focusing on asset inventory and policy coverage to reduce overall risk, and UVM simplifying the management of associated vulnerabilities and remediating risks from a centralized platform.
- To configure and manage EASM Discovery Settings, your assigned role must include Read, Create, Edit, and Delete permissions for the EASM Configuration resource. To learn more, see [Creating Custom Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-managing-role-permissions) and [Assigning Roles to Users](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/assigning-roles-users).

The following section explains how you can configure and manage EASM discovery settings. To learn more about EASM capabilities, see [Understanding Zscaler EASM Capabilities](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/understanding-zscaler-easm-capabilities) and [Understanding Asset Discovery with Zscaler EASM](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/understanding-asset-discovery-zscaler-easm).

## Creating a Discovery Profile

To create a discovery profile:

1. In the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform, go to **Configure**> **EASM Settings**. See image. You can also access this page from **Assets** > **Settings** in AEM, or **Vulnerabilities** > **Settings** in UVM.
2. If you are configuring your first discovery profile, click **Create a profile**. If one or more profiles already exist, click **New Profile**. The **Create Profile** window appears.
3. In the **Create Profile** window:
  1. **Name**: Enter a name for the discovery profile.
  2. **Scan Frequency**: Scanning frequency is automatically set to **Weekly** and cannot be changed.
  3. Select the type of seed asset you want to configure: A discovery profile can have a maximum of 100 seeds across the seed types.
    - Domains
    - IP Addresses
    - IP Blocks
    - Organizations
4. Click **Save**. The discovery profile is saved and displayed on the **EASM Settings** page. On this page, you can view your configured discovery profiles along with their name, individual counts of included and excluded seeds, last scan timestamp, and scan status. The scanning process typically takes a few hours, and you can track the scan status, including progress, successful completion, and failure, under the **Status** column. See image.

After scanning is completed, you can view the ingested assets on the [Assets](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/about-assets-uvm) page and the associated risk detections on the [Findings](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/about-findings-operational-view-uvm) page.

1. Select **Included Domains** or **Excluded Domains**to include or exclude specific domains from scanning, respectively. To exclude specific domains, you must first include at least one seed (of any type) to define the target for initiating scanning.
2. You can either upload a CSV file containing the domain names or manually enter them: Domains, subdomains, top-level domains, and punycode extensions are supported. You can use the search option to locate specific domains within include or exclude lists. To remove an entry, click the **Delete** icon displayed for the field. See image.
  - To use a CSV file, click **Upload .CSV File** and select the required file. Ensure that the file contains valid domains, with each entry listed in a separate row. A header row is not required.
  - To manually enter the domain names:
    1. Click **Add Domains**. The **Add Domains** drawer appears.
    2. In the **Add Domains** drawer, enter the domain name or subdomain (e.g., `acme.com` or `support.acme.com`) in the text field. To add multiple entries, click **Add More**.
    3. Click **Done**. See image.
3. Click **Save**.

1. Select **Included IP Addresses** or **Excluded IP Addresses** to include or exclude specific IP addresses from scanning, respectively. To exclude specific IP addresses, you must first include at least one seed (of any type) to define the target for initiating scanning.
2. You can either upload a CSV file containing the IP addresses or manually enter them: The IP address must be a strictly formatted IPv4 address (e.g., `192.0.2.2`). Subnet mask, port number, and CIDR notation (e.g., appending `/24` is invalid) are not supported. IPv6 addresses are also not supported. You can use the search option to locate specific IP addresses within include or exclude lists. To remove an entry, click the **Delete** icon displayed for the field. See image.
  - To use a CSV file, click **Upload .CSV File** and select the required file. Ensure that the file contains valid IP addresses, with each entry listed in a separate row. A header row is not required.
  - To manually enter the IP addresses:
    1. Click **Add IP Addresses**. The **Add IP Addresses** drawer appears.
    2. In the **Add IP Addresses**drawer, enter the IP address (e.g., `192.0.2.24`) in the text field. To add multiple entries, click **Add More**.
    3. Click **Done**. See image.
3. Click **Save**.

1. Select **Included IP Blocks**or **Excluded IP Blocks**to include or exclude specific IP address blocks from scanning, respectively. To exclude specific IP address blocks, you must first include at least one seed (of any type) to define the target for initiating scanning.
2. You can either upload a CSV file containing the IP address blocks or manually enter them: Ensure that the IP address blocks are valid and meet specific, predefined conditions. See validation criteria. You can use the search option to locate specific IP address blocks within include or exclude lists. To remove an entry, click the **Delete** icon displayed for the field. See image.
  - To use a CSV file, click **Upload .CSV File** and select the required file. Ensure that the file contains valid IP address blocks, with each entry listed in a separate row. A header row is not required.
  - To manually enter the IP address blocks:
    1. Click **Add IP Blocks**. The **Add IP Blocks**drawer appears.
    2. In the **Add IP Blocks**drawer, enter the IP address block (e.g., `192.0.2.0/32`) in the text field. To add multiple entries, click **Add More**.
    3. Click **Done**. See image.
3. Click **Save**.

1. Select **Included Organizations**or **Excluded Organizations**to include or exclude specific organizations from scanning, respectively. To exclude specific organizations from scanning, you must first include at least one seed (of any type) to define the target for initiating scanning.
2. Click **Add Organizations**. The **Add Organizations**drawer appears. You can use the search option to locate specific organizations within include or exclude lists. To remove an entry, click the **Delete** icon displayed for the field. See image.
  1. In the **Add Organizations**drawer:
    1. Enter the organization name (e.g., `Acme Inc.`) in the text field. The organization name must have a minimum length of 4 characters. To add multiple entries, click **Add More**.
    2. Click **Done**. See image.
3. Click **Save**.

- The IP address block must be formatted as a valid IP address followed immediately by a forward slash (`/`) and then a routing prefix (i.e., subnet mask).
- The IP address portion must strictly adhere to the formatting rules for IPv4 addresses.
- The subnet mask portion must be a valid, unsigned integer. Explicit positive or negative signs (e.g., `+24` or `-24`) are not allowed.
- The subnet mask must be between `20` and `32`, inclusive of these numbers (e.g., `192.0.2.0/32`). Subnet masks between `0` and `19`, including these numbers, are not allowed.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/configuring-grouping-rules-aem","lastmod":"2026-02-17T06:06Z","nid":"1534045"} -->
## Configuring Grouping Rules in AEM

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/configuring-grouping-rules-aem
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Settings for AEM > Configuring Grouping Rules in AEM
- Last modified: 2026-02-17T06:06Z
- Summary: How to configure grouping rules in the Assets app.

You can configure grouping rules to aggregate policy violations into a single violation ticket, for a focused and streamlined workflow. During the initial setup, a default rule set based on best practices is created based on the policy name and policy assignee. You can create and modify a grouping rule to align with your organization's requirements.

You can create a rule set in the following ways:

- Create a new grouping rule set: Add a new rule set, activate, and run the rule set to reaggregate policy violations into violation tickets. Activating the new rule set deactivates the existing rule set.
- Clone and edit the default rule set: Clone and edit the default rule set. Run the edited rule set to reaggregate policy violations into violation tickets based on the newly configured grouping logic.

## Configuring a New Grouping Rule Set

A grouping rule set is a collection of individual rules that group similar policy violations into violation tickets based on specific conditions. While you can create multiple rule sets within an account, only one rule set can be active at a time.

To configure a grouping rule set:

1. In the SecOps platform, click **Assets**in the top navigation bar.
2. Go to **Settings**> **Grouping Rules**. The **Grouping Rule Sets** page appears. See image.
3. Click **New Rule Set**. The **Create New Rule** **Set**page appears.
4. Enter a name for the rule set.
5. Click **New Rule**. The **Create Rule** page appears. See image.
6. On the **Create Rule** page:
  1. **Name**: Enter a name for the rule.
  2. **If**: Define the condition that determines which policy violations the rule applies to.
  3. **Then**: Select an action from the **Group By** drop-down menu that must be implemented when the conditions are met.
  4. **Define Violation Ticket Title By**: Select a title format for the violation tickets.
    - **Smart Text**: Use a combination of free text and field names as tokens for the title. For example, you can enter the name of the team based on the business application associated with the violation ticket. To add fields as tokens, enter the field name within double curly brackets. The field's display name automatically translates to the field's system name (e.g., Application Name → `application.name`).
    - **Expression**: Set a violation ticket title using an expression to apply custom value transformations and standardize formats. Supported functions, operators, and references, along with examples, are displayed when clicking the Expression text box.
7. (Optional) Click **Preview**to validate the rule's logic.
8. Click **Save**. To activate the new rule, click **Save & Activate**from the **Save**drop-down menu.
9. Click **Save**. This saves the rule but doesn't aggregate violation tickets based on the rule set's rules. To aggregate policy violations into a violation ticket based on the new logic, activate and run the new rule set. If you only activate but don't run the new rule set, it will run on the next data ingestion in your account.

Every rule set includes a default fallback rule, which provides a default aggregation method for policy violations that don't match any conditions. The fallback rule can be edited, but can't be removed or deleted.

[Image: The Grouping Rule Sets page]

[Image: Adding a new ruleset]

## Configuring Rules in a Default Rule Set

Within a grouping rule set, you can create individual rules that define how policy violations must be aggregated into violation tickets. Every new rule set must include at least one rule in addition to the default fallback rule.

A grouping rule consists of three key components:

- If condition: Determines which policy violations the rule applies to.
- Then action: Aggregates policy violations into a single violation ticket if they have matching values in all selected fields.
- Define Ticket Title By: The title format for violation tickets that are created based on the rule.

To create a grouping rule in a rule set:

1. In the relevant rule set, click **New Rule**. The **Create Rule** page appears. See image.
2. On the **Create Rule**page:
  1. **Name**: Enter a name for the rule.
  2. **If**: Define the rule condition that determines which policy violations must be aggregated into a single violation ticket.
    1. Select a field on which the condition should be based.
    2. Select an operator (**Contains**, **Is Not Empty**, **Is Empty**, **Equals**). The available operators vary depending on the field type.
    3. Enter the value to which the rule should apply.
    4. (Optional) Use **AND**/**OR**logic to define compound rules.
      - **AND**aggregates policy violations only if they meet all conditions.
      - **OR**aggregates policy violations if they meet any of the conditions.
  3. **Then**: Select at least one field from the **Group By**drop-down menu according to which the policy violations that meet the conditions should be aggregated. All policy violations with the same value are merged into a single violation ticket.
  4. **Define Ticket Title By**: Select a method to set the violation ticket title.
    - **Smart Text**: Use a combination of free text and field names as tokens to set the violation ticket title. For example, you can enter the name of the team based on the business application associated with the violation ticket. To add fields as tokens, enter the field name within double curly brackets. The field's display name automatically translates to the field's system name (e.g., Application Name → `application.name`).
    - **Expression**: Set a violation ticket title using an expression to apply custom value transformations and standardize formats. Supported functions, operators, and references, along with examples, are displayed when clicking the **Expression**text box.
3. Click **Preview**to validate your rule's logic. The preview displays policy violations that match the rule and their relevant fields according to the fields specified in the rule. This can indicate whether the rule's filters apply to the policy violations you intend to group into violation tickets. If no policy violations match the filter condition displayed in the preview, you might need to adjust the rule's configured filters. Alternatively, a previous rule might be applicable to the relevant policy violations, as grouping is dependent on rule order.
4. Click **Save** to add the rule to the rule set.
5. After adding all the required rules to the rule set, choose an option to save the rule set to complete the process:
  - Click **Save**. This saves the rules from the rule set but doesn't reaggregate into violation tickets based on the rule set's rules.
    - If the rule set is active, the new rule set will take effect either when you click **Run**or the next time data is processed in the account (e.g., when a data source runs).
    - If the rule set is inactive, no changes will apply to the grouping of policy violations in the account until the rule set is activated and runs.
  - From the **Save**drop-down menu, click **Save & Activate**to save the rule set and immediately apply the rules to the data in your account.

You can repeat the process to add as many grouping rules as required.

[Image: Rule to define how findings are aggregated]

## Order of Rules in a Grouping Rule Set

The rules within a grouping rule set are run sequentially by their order of appearance. A policy violation is aggregated into a violation ticket according to the first rule that applies to it. If no rule applies to the policy violation, it's aggregated by the default fallback rule. You can adjust the order of rules by dragging the rules to your desired order. After rearranging the rule order, click **Save**to apply your changes.

[Image: Order of rules within a grouping rule set]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Configuring Violation Ticket Workflows

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/configuring-violation-ticket-workflows
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Settings for AEM > Configuring Violation Ticket Workflows
- Last modified: 2026-05-22T07:06Z
- Summary: How to configure ticket workflows in AEM.

The Violation Ticket Lifecycle page in the Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) app enables you to fully configure the ticket lifecycle to accommodate your organization's specific operational needs, providing full transparency and control over how violation tickets are managed. By customizing your ticket lifecycle, you can create a streamlined, efficient, and tailored workflow. You can define violation ticket status transitions, set up workflows to automatically open new violation tickets or aggregate them within existing violation tickets, define conditions to trigger automatic dispatch to third-party vendors, and set rules to automatically lock a violation ticket.

The Violation Ticket Lifecycle page includes:

- **V****iolation****Ticket Statuses**: Set the status of a violation ticket within the violation ticket workflow. You can also create custom ticket statuses that allow you to tailor your ticketing system to specific business requirements. To learn more, see [Managing Violation Ticket Statuses in AEM](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/managing-violation-ticket-statuses-aem).
- **V****iolation****Ticket Workflows**: Configure automated rules for managing violation tickets. Violation ticket workflow categories include the following rule sets:
  - **Violation Ticket Status Management**: Define the rules to update the status of a violation ticket.
  - **Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers**: Define the rules to lock a violation ticket.
  - **Auto-Dispatch to External Systems**: Automate the creation of third-party work management items and alerts.

To learn more, see [About Violation Tickets](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/about-violation-tickets) and[Viewing Violation Tickets in AEM](https://help.zscaler.com/aem/viewing-violation-tickets-aem).

## Configuring Violation Ticket Workflow Rule Sets

To configure violation ticket workflow rule sets:

1. Go to the AEM app (**Assets**).
2. In the left-side navigation, click **Settings**> **Violation Ticket Lifecycle**. The **Violation Ticket Lifecycle** page appears.
3. Click **Violation Ticket Workflows**. See image. The **Violation Ticket Workflows**page appears. See image.
4. On the **Violation Ticket Workflows**page, configure rules for the following workflow categories:
  - Violation Ticket Status Management
  - Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers
  - Auto-Dispatch to External Systems
5. Click **Done.**

You can view the activity log for all these actions on a ticket's **Activity**tab.

[Image: Violation Ticket Lifecycle page]

[Image: Ticket Workflows with Workflow Category, Condition, and Action]

To configure automated rules for violation tickets:

1. Click **Violation Ticket Status Management**. The **Violation Ticket Status Management**drawer appears.
2. Click **Unlink & Override**to enable rule creation. See image.
3. Click **Create a New Rule.** The **Violation Ticket Status Management**drawer appears.
4. In the **Violation Ticket Status Management** drawer, enter the following details: See image.
  - **NAME**: Enter a name for the rule.
  - **CATEGORY**: Select one of the following options:
    - Automatic Violation Ticket Closure
    - Resurface Policy Violation - Create New Violation Ticket
    - Resurface Policy Violation - Reopen Violation Ticket
    - Custom Status Transition
5. (Optional) Click **New Rule** to add a new rule.
6. Save the rule set in one of the following ways: See image.
  - Click **Save** for rules take effect when new data is ingested into your account.
  - Click **Save & Run** to save the rule set and immediately apply the rules on the tickets.

Set the conditions to close a violation ticket.

Set the criteria:

- **IF**:
  - **Violation Ticket status is**: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
  - **A third-party work management item is attached**: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
  - (Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
- **THEN**: From the **Update violation ticket status to** drop-down menu, select the action that should be taken for violation tickets that meet the IF condition.

See image.

Create a new violation ticket if a previously detected policy violation resurfaces.

Set the criteria:

- **IF**:
  - **Violation Ticket status is**: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
  - **At least one policy violation is active for**: Enter the number of days. The rule is triggered even if one policy violation is active for the specified period.
  - **A third-party work management item is attached**: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
  - (Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
- **THEN**: A new violation ticket is created with the resurfaced policy violation. This option is displayed by default.

See image.

Reopen the violation ticket if a previously detected policy violation resurfaces.

Set the criteria:

- **IF**:
  - **Violation Ticket status is**: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
  - **At least one policy violation is active for**: Enter the number of days. The rule is triggered even if one policy violation is active for the specified period.
  - **A third-party work management item is attached**: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
  - (Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
- **THEN**: From the **Move violation ticket to status** drop-down menu, select the action that should be taken for violation tickets that meet the IF condition.

See image.

Define custom conditions for the violation ticket status transition.

Set the criteria:

- **IF**:
  - **Violation Ticket status is**: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
  - **A third-party work management item is attached**: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
  - (Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
- **THEN**: From the **Move violation ticket to status** drop-down menu, select the action that should be taken for violation tickets that meet the IF condition.

See image.

To configure automated rules to lock a violation ticket:

1. Click **Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers**. The **Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers**drawer appears.
2. Click **Unlink & Override**to enable rule creation. See image.
3. Click **Create a New Rule.** The **Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers**drawer appears.
4. In the**Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers** drawer, enter the following details: See image.
  - **NAME**: Enter a name for the rule.
  - Set the criteria:
    - **IF**:
      - **Violation Ticket is manually split or merged**: This checkbox is selected by default.
      - **Violation Ticket status is**: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
      - **A third-party work management item is attached**: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
      - (Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
    - **THEN**: The violation ticket is locked. This option is displayed by default.
5. (Optional) Click **New Rule** to add a new rule.
6. Save the rule set in one of the following ways: See image.
  - Click **Save** for rules to take effect when new data is ingested into your account.
  - Click **Save & Run** to save the rule set and immediately apply the rules on the tickets.

To configure automated rules for creating third-party work management items and alerts:

1. Click **Auto-Dispatch to External Systems**. The **Auto-Dispatch to External Systems**drawer appears. See image.
2. Click **Create a New Rule**. The **Auto-Dispatch to External Systems**drawer appears.
3. In the **Auto-Dispatch to External Systems** drawer, enter the following details: See image.
  - **NAME**: Enter a name for the rule.
  - Set the criteria:
    - **IF**:
      - **Violation Ticket status is**: Select the checkbox to add the violation ticket status to which the rule should be applied.
      - **Violation Ticket severity is**: Select the checkbox to add the violation ticket severity to which the rule should be applied.
      - **Violation Ticket assignee is**: Select the checkbox to add the assignee of the violation ticket on which the rule should be applied.
      - (Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
    - **THEN**:
      - **Create a third-party item on**: Select a value from the drop-down menu.
      - **Create New Outegration**: Click to configure an outegration for the third-party value selected previously.
4. (Optional) Click **New Rule** to add a new rule.
5. Save the rule set in one of the following ways: See image.
  - Click **Save** for rules to take effect when new data is ingested into your account.
  - Click **Save & Run** to save the rule set and immediately apply the rules on the tickets.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/exporting-reports-discovery-profiles","lastmod":"2026-05-22T07:06Z","nid":"1538690"} -->
## Exporting Reports for Discovery Profiles

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/exporting-reports-discovery-profiles
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > External Attack Surface Management for AEM > Exporting Reports for Discovery Profiles
- Last modified: 2026-05-22T07:06Z
- Summary: How to generate and export reports for EASM asset discovery profiles, which present key aggregated data and insights into the organization's external security posture.

You can generate and export reports for the [discovery profiles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/configuring-discovery-settings) configured for Zscaler's External Attack Surface Management (EASM) that aggregate key analytic data and security insights into an organization's exposure to cyber risk. The reports are generated in PPTX format, translating real-time technical security data from automated discovery findings into actionable strategic insights for diverse stakeholders.

These reports consolidate critical asset findings along with their mitigation strategies, which help organizations assess the resulting business and financial impact and focus on high-impact risk remediation. The report data varies across discovery profiles depending on the asset and risk information identified. Some key metrics included are known vulnerabilities, exposed servers and public cloud instances, outdated SSL/TLS, domain expiration, and registered lookalike domains highlighting phishing domains for virtual takedown.

These reports can be used in executive- and board-level communication to report on the organization's external posture across dimensions—such as vulnerabilities, exposures, and compliance—aiding in key business decision-making and strategic management and governance. They can also be used in mergers and acquisitions to summarize the inherited risks of a target company, providing visibility into vulnerabilities and misconfigurations without requiring invasive internal scans. These reports also serve auditing purposes to demonstrate continuous monitoring and adherence to regulatory frameworks.

To export reports, your assigned role must include Read permission under the EASM Configuration resource. To learn more, see [Creating Custom Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-managing-role-permissions) and [Assigning Roles to Users](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/assigning-roles-users).

To export a report:

1. In the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform, go to **Configure**> **EASM Settings**.
2. Locate the required discovery profile, and click the **Export Report**icon. See image. You can also click the **Edit** icon for the discovery profile, then click **Export Report** in the top-right corner of the Edit [Discovery Profile] window. See image. The report is generated and downloaded to your system as a PPTX file.

[Image: Exporting report for discovery profile from the EASM Settings page]

[Image: Exporting report for EASM discovery profile]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/managing-asset-compliance-policies","lastmod":"2025-11-11T14:11Z","nid":"1533690"} -->
## Managing Asset Compliance Policies

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/managing-asset-compliance-policies
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Settings for AEM > Managing Asset Compliance Policies
- Last modified: 2025-11-11T14:11Z
- Summary: How to manage configured asset compliance policies in the AEM app of the SecOps platform.

After [creating a policy](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/configuring-asset-compliance-policies), you can manage and adjust its settings and criteria in the Policies table, a centralized view of all policies. To view policies in your account, go to the AEM app and click Policies.

For access to Policies, your assigned role must include the Read, Create, Edit permissions under the Assets App > Policy Rule resource. To learn more, see [Creating Custom Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-custom-roles) and [Assigning Roles to Users](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/assigning-roles-users). Users assigned the Assets Admin role can create and manage policies, but can't delete them.

When managing policies, you can perform the following actions:

- Edit a Policy
- Delete a Policy
- See Runs
- Duplicate a Policy
- Process a Policy Immediately

You can edit a policy to adjust its scope, refine asset filters, update tool coverage requirements, or modify conditions.

Editing a policy automatically updates all existing and future policy violations associated with it. Confirm the changes when prompted.

To edit a policy:

1. Go to **Assets**> **Policies**.
2. Hover over the policy you want to edit, and click the **Edit** icon. The **Edit Policy** page appears.
3. Make the necessary changes.
4. Click **Save**.

You can delete a policy if it is no longer needed, such as when a tool is decommissioned or replaced.

To delete a policy:

1. Go to **Assets** > **Policies**.
2. Choose one of the following options:
  - To delete a single policy, hover over the policy and click the **Delete** icon.
  - To delete multiple policies, select the policies from the table and click **Delete**.
3. Select your preferred option in the warning window:
  - Delete the policy but retain all existing violations.
  - Delete both the policy and all associated violations.
4. Click **Delete**.

Monitor policy runs to track timestamps, statuses, and potential failures. This can be useful for troubleshooting issues.

To see runs:

1. Go to **Assets** > **Policies**.
2. Hover over the policy you want to monitor, and click the **See Runs** icon. The **Policy Runs**page appears.

You can duplicate an existing policy to save time when creating a new policy with similar logic but slight modifications.

To duplicate a policy:

1. Go to **Assets** > **Policies**.
2. Hover over the policy you want to duplicate, and click the **Duplicate** icon. The duplicated policy setup page appears.
3. Edit the policy as needed, including changing its name.
4. Click **Save**.

Policies run automatically upon saving and at their scheduled trigger times. However, you can manually process a policy to sync updates on demand.

To manually process a policy:

1. Go to **Assets**> **Policies**.
2. Choose one of the following options:
  - To process a single policy, hover over the policy and click the **Process Now** icon.
  - To process multiple policies, select the policies from the table and click **Process**. The policy processes and updates the data in your AEM app.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/managing-discovery-profiles","lastmod":"2026-05-17T07:06Z","nid":"1538689"} -->
## Managing Discovery Profiles

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/managing-discovery-profiles
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > External Attack Surface Management for AEM > Managing Discovery Profiles
- Last modified: 2026-05-17T07:06Z
- Summary: How to edit and delete discovery profiles created for Zscaler's External Attack Surface Management (EASM) capabilities.

You can manage the [discovery profiles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/configuring-discovery-settings) configured for Zscaler's External Attack Surface Management (EASM) capabilities, including editing and deleting them. When you add or remove seeds in a discovery profile, a new discovery scan is triggered to update the asset inventory based on the modified profile.

To manage EASM Discovery Settings, your assigned role must include Read, Edit, and Delete permissions for the EASM Configuration resource. To learn more, see [Creating Custom Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/creating-managing-role-permissions) and [Assigning Roles to Users](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/assigning-roles-users).

## Editing a Discovery Profile

To edit a discovery profile:

1. In the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform, go to **Configure**> **EASM Settings**. You can also access this page from **Assets** > **Settings** in AEM, or **Vulnerabilities** > **Settings** in UVM.
2. Locate the required discovery profile, and click the **Edit**icon. You can also click the discovery profile entry in the table to edit details. The **Edit [Discovery Profile]** window appears.
3. In the **Edit [Discovery Profile]** window, you can edit the discovery profile name and make changes to the seed configuration by adding or removing seeds. You cannot edit seeds that are already present in the discovery profile. You can remove them and add new seeds to make changes. To learn more, see [Configuring Discovery Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/uvm/configuring-discovery-settings). See image.
4. Click **Save**.

## Deleting a Discovery Profile

Deleting a discovery profile removes all references to the scan data, including discovered assets and associated risk findings, and can no longer be accessed on the platform.

To delete a discovery profile:

1. Go to **Configure**> **EASM Settings**. You can also access this page from **Assets** > **Settings** in AEM, or **Vulnerabilities** > **Settings** in UVM.
2. Locate the required discovery profile, and click the **Delete**icon.
3. In the confirmation window that appears, click **Continue**.

To delete multiple discovery profiles:

1. Go to **Configure**> **EASM Settings**.
2. Select the discovery profiles you want to delete, and click the **Delete** icon displayed in the top-left of the page.
3. In the confirmation window that appears, click **Continue**.

[Image: Editing EASM discovery profile]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/aem/managing-grouping-rules-aem","lastmod":"2026-01-26T06:06Z","nid":"1534044"} -->
## Managing Grouping Rules in AEM

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/managing-grouping-rules-aem
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Settings for AEM > Managing Grouping Rules in AEM
- Last modified: 2026-01-26T06:06Z
- Summary: How to manage grouping rule sets and rules in the Assets app.

After creating grouping rules, you can manage the rule sets and the rules they contain to refine how policy violations are grouped into violation tickets.

Only one grouping rule set can be active at any given time.

## Managing Grouping Rule Sets

When managing grouping rule sets, you can perform the following actions:

- Activate a Grouping Rule Set
- Clone a Grouping Rule Set
- Edit a Grouping Rule Set
- Delete a Grouping Rule Set

To manage and organize rules effectively, you can create multiple grouping rule sets. This flexibility allows you to develop new rule sets without altering existing ones, ensuring the current setup remains intact. However, keep in mind that only one rule set can be active at a time. The active rule set is clearly identified to help you track which configuration is currently in use.

See image.

To activate an inactive rule set:

1. In the SecOps platform, click **Assets**in the top navigation bar.
2. Go to **Settings**> **Grouping Rules**.
3. Click the **Column Menu**icon on the rule set tile.
4. Click **Set as active**. See image. The **Activate Rule Set**window appears.
5. In the **Activate Rule Set** window, enter the text displayed above the text box into the text box, then click **Continue**. When manually activating a rule set, the previously active rule set becomes inactive.

To immediately apply changes to the grouping in your account, run the newly activated rule set to reaggregate policy violations into violation tickets. To run the rule set, click **Run**on the rule set tile. This reprocesses all data in the account, and applies the new grouping logic to your violation tickets.

You can clone an existing rule set to create a new rule set similar to the existing configuration. This saves time and allows you to modify the cloned rule set to fit your specific needs.

To clone a rule set:

1. In the SecOps platform, click **Assets**in the top navigation bar.
2. Go to **Settings**> **Grouping Rules**.
3. Click the **Column Menu**icon on the rule set tile.
4. Click **Clone**. See image. A copy of the rule set is created with the same name as the original, preceded by the word `clone`.
5. Click the cloned rule set to edit it.
6. Enter a name for the rule set and update the rules as needed.
7. Save the rule set in one of the following ways:
  - Click **Save**to save the rule set. This saves the rules to the rule set but doesn't reaggregate tickets based on the rule set's rules. If the rule set is left inactive, no changes will apply to the grouping of findings in the account until the rule set is activated and run.
  - In the **Save**drop-down menu, click **Save & Activate**to save and set the rule set as active. To apply changes immediately, run the activated rule set to reaggregate findings into tickets; otherwise, changes will take effect during the next data ingestion.

You can edit a rule set to update its name or adjust its logic as needed.

To edit a rule set:

1. In the SecOps platform, click **Assets**in the top navigation bar.
2. Go to **Settings**> **Grouping Rules**.
3. Click the **Edit** icon on the rule set. See image.
4. Make the necessary changes.
5. Save your changes.
  - For the active rule set: Click **Save**to apply the changes during the next data ingestion, or select **Save & Run**from the drop-down menu to immediately apply the changes to the grouping in your account.
  - For inactive rule sets: Click **Save**to update the rule set, or select **Save & Activate**from the drop-down menu to enable the rule set and apply its grouping logic in your account. To apply changes immediately, make sure the rule set is active and then run it.

If a rule set is no longer needed, you can delete it to remove unnecessary configurations from your account. Deleting the active rule set can impact data processing, so ensure another rule set is activated before proceeding.

To delete a rule set:

1. In the SecOps platform, click **Assets**in the top navigation bar.
2. Go to **Settings**> **Grouping Rules**.
3. Click the **Column Menu**icon on the rule set tile.
4. Click **Delete rule set**. See image. The **Confirm Deletion**dialog window appears.
5. In the **Confirm Deletion**dialog window:
  - For the active rule set, enter the text displayed above the text box into the text box, then click **Delete**.
  - For inactive rule sets, click **Delete**.

## Managing Grouping Rules

Manage grouping rules to control how findings are grouped into tickets within a rule set. You can clone or edit rules to adjust their logic, or delete rules you no longer need. Each rule set must include at least one rule in addition to the default fallback rule, which provides a standard grouping method for unmatched findings and cannot be removed.

When managing grouping rules, you can perform the following actions:

- Clone Grouping Rules
- Edit Grouping Rules
- Delete Grouping Rules

Cloning a rule is useful when you need to create multiple rules with similar logic or structure. Instead of building each rule from scratch, you can copy an existing rule and modify only the parts that differ, such as field values, conditions, or grouping criteria.

To clone a grouping rule:

1. In the SecOps platform, click **Assets**in the top navigation bar.
2. Go to **Settings**> **Grouping Rules**.
3. Select the rule set that you want to modify.
4. Hover over the rule you want to clone, and click the **Clone**icon ([Image: clone icon]). A copy of the rule is created with the same name as the original, followed by the word `clone`.
5. Click the cloned rule to edit it.
6. Enter a name for the rule and update the rule's logic as needed.
7. (Optional) Click **Preview**to verify your rule's logic.
8. Click **Save.**

To update an existing rule's grouping logic, you can edit the rule rather than deleting and recreating it.

To edit a rule:

1. In the SecOps platform, click **Assets**in the top navigation bar.
2. Go to **Settings**> **Grouping Rules**.
3. Select the rule set that you want to modify.
4. Hover over the rule you want to edit, and click the **Edit**icon ([Image: edit icon]). The **Edit Rule**drawer appears.
5. Make the necessary changes.
6. Click**Save**.

If your rule is part of an active rule set, it will apply either when the rule set is run manually or during the next data ingestion.

You can remove rules that are outdated or no longer relevant due to changes in data structure or grouping logic.

Deleting a rule doesn't trigger a warning message and deletes the rule immediately.

To delete a rule:

1. In the SecOps platform, click **Assets**in the top navigation bar.
2. Go to **Settings**> **Grouping Rules**.
3. Select a rule set.
4. Hover over the rule you want to delete, and click the **Delete**icon ([Image: delete icon]).

[Image: Rule sets on the Grouping Rule Sets page]

[Image: Set the rule set as active]

[Image: Cloning a rule set]

[Image: Edit a rule set]

[Image: Delete a rule set]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Managing Violation Ticket Statuses in AEM

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/aem/managing-violation-ticket-statuses-aem
- Product: Asset Exposure Management
- Path: Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Help > Settings for AEM > Managing Violation Ticket Statuses in AEM
- Last modified: 2026-05-17T07:06Z
- Summary: How to manage ticket statuses in AEM.

A status bucket is a high-level container that logically groups violation tickets with similar statuses, allowing you to track the progress and manage workflows efficiently. You can manage the status of violation tickets by creating status buckets.

[Image: View the statuses of a violation ticket]

## Creating a Status Bucket

To create a status bucket:

1. Go to the AEM app (**Assets**).
2. In the left-side navigation, go to **Settings > Violation Ticket Lifecycle.** The **Violation Ticket Lifecycle** page appears.
3. Click **Violation Ticket Statuses**. See image. The **Statuses** page appears, displaying the default configuration for statuses and buckets.
4. From the **Entity Type** drop-down menu, select **Violation Ticket**.
5. Click **Add Bucket**. See image.
6. Enter a name for the bucket. See image.
7. (Optional) Select the following checkboxes to add a label to the status bucket: These labels provide insights for metrics and calculations and allow you to view all closed violation tickets.
  - **Closed**: Indicates that the violation ticket is closed.
  - **Remediated**: Indicates that the violation ticket is resolved.
8. Click **Save**. The new status bucket appears on the **Violation Ticket Statuses** page.

## Adding a Status to a Status Bucket

To add a status to a status bucket:

1. Click**Add Status** under the relevant status bucket. See image.
2. Enter a status name.
3. Click **Save**.

[Image: Violation Ticket Lifecycle page]

[Image: The default configuration for buckets and statuses]

[Image: Create a new bucket]

## Editing, Rearranging, and Deleting Status Buckets

To edit a status bucket:

1. Hover over the bucket, and click the **Edit**icon. See image.
2. Edit the bucket name.
3. Add or remove the labels (e.g., **Closed**).
4. Click **Save**.

[Image: Edit a bucket]

Torearrange the order of buckets, hover over the bucket and use the **Grid**icon to drag it to the desired position.

See image.

[Image: Rearrange the order of a bucket]

To delete a bucket, hover over the bucket and click the **Delete Bucket**icon.

See image.

[Image: Delete a bucket]

You can only delete the most recently added bucket.

[Image: Add a status name for the bucket]

## Editing, Rearranging, and Deleting Violation Ticket Statuses

You can only edit a status that is currently not used for a violation ticket.

To edit a violation ticket status:

1. Hover over the violation ticket status in the status bucket, and click the **Edit**icon. See image.
2. Edit the status name.
3. Click **Save**.

[Image: Edit a violation ticket status]

Torearrange the order of violation ticket statuses in a status bucket, hover over the status and use the **Grid**icon to drag it to the desired position.

See image.

[Image: Rearrange the order of a ticket status in a bucket]

To delete a violation ticket status, hover over the status and click the **Delete Status** icon.

See image.

[Image: Delete a status]

You can only delete the most recently added violation ticket status.

## Updating Violation Ticket Status

A status timeline is displayed on the top of each violation ticket, providing a visual cue of the violation ticket's current status. You can manually change the status of the violation ticket by selecting a new one from the drop-down menu.

See image.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->
