## About Scan Settings

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > About Scan Settings
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about configuring the scan settings in the AI Security Admin Portal.

AI Security regularly scans the cloud resources (data stores) such as cloud storage devices, databases, virtual machines. etc., within your cloud accounts and detects sensitive data and vulnerabilities. AI Security performs the scan by leveraging the [local scan orchestrator](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-orchestrator) that is deployed in your AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or On-Premises Data Centers account during the [onboarding process](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts). The resources are scanned against a set of standard [security policies](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-posture-policies) and a scan schedule. In the scan rules, you can select the resources you want to scan, the scan type, and set the scan frequency.

The scan rule provides granular control over scan configurations. You can define custom scan types and schedules for individual data stores based on:

- Account
- Region
- Tags
- Specific resources

When scanning relational databases such as PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, and MySQL, AI Security uses the data sampling technique to scan a subset of data, instead of scanning the entire database. This helps to avoid a full data scan and ensures the database operations are not impacted.

You can create multiple scan rules for supported data stores such as virtual machines, databases, and Snowflake accounts.

- You need to first onboard your cloud accounts before configuring the scan rule. To learn more, see [About Cloud Accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts).
- Although overlapping scan rules are allowed, they can lead to duplicate scans and increased compute costs. AI Security displays warnings during rule creation to help you avoid redundant configurations.
- If a resource is deleted from the account after configuring the scan schedule, then AI Security ignores this resource during the scan.

The scan framework in AI Security provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Use predefined DLP engines to classify sensitive data based on the level of sensitivity and risk.
- Configure the scan rule to scan your accounts and identify sensitive data.
- Regularly monitor your cloud accounts for any vulnerabilities.
- Select the required accounts for scanning and exclude some accounts from scanning.
- Configure the scan frequency and scan type.
- Use data sampling to scan a subset of data.

## Scan Types

AI Security supports the scanning of the following data stores. The scan type varies for each data store.

| Data Store | Scan Type |
| --- | --- |
| Compute | **On-Demand Scan**: Perform an on-demand scan instantly. |
| Storage | **Full Scan**: Scan all the data in the selected data or object stores. This includes both the historic data and the newer data. Newer data scan is prioritized over historic data scan.; **Scan Only New or Modified Files**: Scan only new or modified data or files in the accounts.; **Historical Scan**: Scan data or files over a lookback period in terms of days (max of 365 days). |
| Managed Database | **Full Scan**: Scan all the data in the selected data or object stores. This includes both the historic data and the newer data. Newer data scan is prioritized over historic data scan.; **Data Sampling Scan**: Scan a subset of data. |
| NoSQL Datastore | **Full Scan**: Scan all the data in the selected data or object stores. This includes both the historic data and the newer data. Newer data scan is prioritized over historic data scan.; **Scan Only Recent Data**: Scan only those files that are newly added or modified since the previous scan. This scan type is also applicable for unmanaged databases. |
| Unmanaged Database | **Data Sampling Scan**: Scan a subset of data. |

## About the Scan Settings Page

On the Scan Settings page (Administration > Scan Settings), you can see the following tabs:

- Scan Rules
- Scan Scopes

On the Scan Scopes tab, you can do the following:

1. [Create a new scan scope.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-scope)
2. View the scan scope configurations. For each configuration, you can view the following information:
  - **Scope**: Name of the scan scope. Click the scan scope name to view the following details.
    - Scan Scope Details
  - **Description**: A concise summary of the purpose and objectives of each scan scope.
  - **Scan Rules**: Information on whether the scan scope is linked to any specific scan rule.
  - **Created by**: The user who created the scan scope.
  - **Created on**: The date and time when the scan scope was created
3. [Show or hide the columns on the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
4. Click the **Action** icon to [edit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/editing-or-deleting-scan-scopes) or [delete](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/editing-or-deleting-scan-scopes) the scan scope.

[Image: The Scan Scope page details all scan scopes.]

For each scan scope configuration, you can view:

1. Name of the scan scope.
2. **General Information**: Provides an overview of the scan scope, including:
  - **Created by**: Name of the user who created the scan scope.
  - **Created on**: Date and time the scan scope was created.
  - **Description**: Brief summary of the scope.
3. **Scope Criteria**: Defines the scan scope.
  - **DLP Engines**: List of the DLP engines included in the scan scope.
  - **File Type**: List of the file types included in the scan scope.
  - **ML Categories**: Whether machine learning categories are enabled or disabled for the scan scope.
4. **Scan Rules**: List of scan rules associated with the scan scope.

See image.

[Image: Scan Scope Details]

On the Scan Rule tab, you can do the following:

1. Add new scan rule for AWS, GCP, Azure, On-Premises, or Snowflake data center accounts.
2. View the scan rule configurations for various resources. For each rule configuration, you can view:
  - **Scan Rule**: Name of the scan rule. Click the scan rule name to view the following details.
    - Scan Rule Details
  - **Description**: Optional summary that explains the purpose of the scan rule.
  - **Cloud**: The name of the cloud service (AWS, Azure, GCP, or On-Premises Data Centers).
  - **Resource Type**: The type of resource or data store (cloud storage, database, or virtual machine).
  - **Scan Scope**: Information on whether the scan rule is linked to any specific scan scope.
  - **Scan Status**: The scan status indicates the state of the scanning process. To learn more, see [Understanding Scan Status](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-scan-status).
  - **Scan Enable/Disable**: The enabled or disabled state of the scan setting. By default, the scan setting is disabled. After configuring the scan setting, you must [enable the scan setting](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/enabling-or-disabling-scan-rule) to initiate the scan.
  - **Added By**: Name of the user who created the scan scope.
  - **Added On**: Date and time the scan scope was created.
3. Sort the column data.
4. [Show or hide the columns in the table](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
5. Click the **Action** icon to:
  - [Edit or delete the scan rule](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/editing-or-deleting-scan-rule).
  - [Stop the scan](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/enabling-or-disabling-scan-rule).
  - [Run an on-demand scan](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/running-demand-scan). You can perform an on-demand scan only on databases and virtual machines.

[Image: The Scan Rules page details all scan rules.]

For each scan rule configuration, you can view:

- **Name**: Name of the scan rule.
- **Description**: Optional summary that explains the purpose of the scan rule.
- **Status**: The scan status indicates whether the scan is enabled or disabled.
- **Cloud**: The name of the cloud service (AWS, Azure, GCP, or On-Premises Data Centers).
- **Resource Type**: The type of resource or data store (cloud storage, database, or virtual machine).
- **Scan Scope**: Information on whether the scan rule is linked to any specific scan scope.
- **Scan Type**: The method used to scan the resource.
- **Resources Scanned**: The number of resources discovered and scanned by this scan rule.
- **Added On**: Date and time the scan scope was created.
- **Added By**: Name of the user who created the scan scope.

See image.

[Image: The Scan Settings page details all the scan scopes and rules.]

[Image: View the scan setting details]

## About Scanning AI Models

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scanning-ai-models
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Model Scan Management > About Scanning AI Models
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on AI Model Security Scanning in AI Security.

The use of large language models (LLMs) and other machine learning (ML) models has created new security blind spots. Organizations often download models from public repositories without a reliable way to inspect them for any vulnerabilities. The AI models can contain malicious code, backdoors, or embedded secrets that execute with the host application's privileges, posing a serious risk to data and systems.

AI Security AI model security provides a framework to enforce security on AI models. The AI model scanner is a command-line tool that developers and MLOps engineers can run before deploying AI models to production. You can integrate the scanner into local workflows or CI/CD pipelines to stop threats before they reach sensitive environments and ensure security across all AI model deployments.

The AI model scanner provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- **Threat Detection**: Identify malicious code, backdoors, and vulnerabilities in AI models using YARA rules and the Zscaler ThreatLabz AV engine. This prevents compromised models from entering production.
- **Secret Scanning**: Detect embedded credentials, API keys, and sensitive information across all supported file types to reduce the risk of data breaches and system compromise.
- **Code Extraction**: Extract and analyze embedded code from pickle files and Lambda layers to detect hidden malicious logic.
- **Centralized Visibility and Reporting**: Integrate scan results into the AI Security Admin Portal, providing clear reports with severity levels and remediation steps for centralized scan management, auditing, and governance.
- **Automated Security Integration**: Enable consistent, automated security checks that can be integrated into the devops pipelines.
- Prevent compromised AI models from entering production environments.
- Reduce risk of data breaches and disruption by malicious AI models.
- Enable consistent, automated security checks across development and deployment pipelines.
- Support auditing and governance through centralized reporting.

## About the Model Scan Management Page

On the Model Scan Management Page (Administration > Model Scan Management Page), you can see the following tabs:

- Integration Registration
- Download Model Scanner

[Image: Model Scan Management page showing the Integration Registration and Scanner Download tabs.]

On the **Integration Registration** tab, you can do the following:

1. [Add an integration](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-ai-model-scan-integrations).
2. Search for specific integrations in the searchable columns.
3. View the list of model scan integrations. For each integration, you can view:
  - **Integration Name**: The name of the integration.
  - **Integration ID**: The unique identifier for the integration.
  - **Modified By**: The user who last modified the integration.
  - **Configured On**: The date and time the integration was last configured.
  - **Status**: The current status of the integration (**Enabled** or **Disabled**).
4. Sort the column data.
5. Modify the table and its columns.
6. Click the **Actions** icon to [edit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-ai-model-scan-integrations) or [delete](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-ai-model-scan-integrations) an integration.

[Image: The Integration Registration tab, displaying a list of model scan integrations with their names, IDs, and statuses.]

On the **Download Model Scanner** tab, you can view the list of available AI model scanner binaries. For each scanner binary, you can view:

- **Scanner Name**: The name of the scanner binary. Click on the name to download the scanner file to your local system.
- **Scanner Version**: The version number of the scanner.
- **Operating System**: The operating system the scanner is built for (e.g., Linux, macOS).
- **Architecture**: The processor architecture (e.g., x64, Arm64).
- **Release Date**: The date the scanner binary was released.

[Image: The Scanner Download tab, showing the list of available AI Model Scanner binaries available for different operating systems.]

## About System Logs - AI Infra Scanning

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-system-logs-ai-infra-scanning
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Monitoring & Investigation > About System Logs - AI Infra Scanning
- Last modified: 2026-08-29T07:06Z
- Summary: Information about the System Logs in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The System Logs page with AI Infra Scanning tab in AI Security gives administrators a unified, filterable view of every AI infrastructure scan event generated across their AWS, Azure, and GCP environments. The page displays scan outcomes, including successes, failures, and detailed error messages so administrators can quickly triage scan health, identify misconfigurations, and audit the inventory pipeline over time.

The System Logs Page in AI Security provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- View error events in chronological order across AWS, Azure, and GCP from a single page.
- See inline scan error messages and correlate them to parent resources without leaving the console or engaging support.
- Filter scan activity by cloud environment, region, resource type, severity, resource status, and time range to quickly isolate issues.
- Export filtered scan event logs to CSV files to support compliance requirements, covering up to 30 days of scan history.
- Detect and resolve misconfigurations blocking scans such as missing customer-managed KMS keys independently, without engineering involvement.

## About System Logs - AI Infrastructure Scanning Page

On the System Logs - AI Infrastructure Scanning page (Administration > System Logs - AI Infrastructure Scanning), you can do the following:

1. Search by resource name, resource ID, or message.
2. Filter the report.
3. Export the event results as a CSV file to your default downloads folder. You can also view the downloaded results in the [Report Management](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/downloading-reports) page.
4. Select and hide columns in the table.
5. Show or hide filters.
6. View a list of scan events and for each event you can view:
  - **Timestamp:** The date and time the last full scan was initiated for the resource, formatted as local date and time in the user's time zone.
  - **Event ID:** The unique identifier assigned to the scan event record.
  - **Source ID & Name:**The unique identifier and name of the scanned resource, e.g., an ARN or URN for AWS resources.
  - **Source Type:** The type of cloud resource that was scanned, e.g., AWS::EC2::Volume).
  - **Severity:** The severity level of the scan event, derived from the scan error or resource tag.
  - **Event Details:** A comma-separated list of scan error messages and descriptions associated with the resource's latest scan attempt.
  - **Region:** The cloud region where the resource is deployed.
  - **Environment:** The cloud provider environment in which the resource exists.
  - **Provider Timestamp:** The timestamp of the event as recorded by the cloud service provider.
  - **Source Status:** The current status of the resource.
  - **Parent Source ID:**The unique identifier of the parent resource associated with this event.
  - The following columns are hidden. You can enable the hidden columns by clicking the gear icon and selecting the column names.
    - Account ID
    - Organization ID
    - Scan Status
    - Parent Resource Type
    - First Scanned At
    - Last Scanned At
    - Full Scan Completed At
    - Scan Updated At
    - Discovered
    - Created
    - Updated
    - Is Primary
    - Is Deleted

- Time Range: Filters the results by a predefined time period. Select Last 1 Hour, Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days, or All Time.
- **Environment:** Filters scan events by cloud provider environment. Select **AWS, Azure, GCP, Copilot Studio, GitHub**, or **GitLab** to narrow results to a specific cloud environment.
- **Regions:** Filters scan events by the cloud region where the scanned resource is deployed, e.g., us-east-1.
- **Source:** Filters scan events by the type of cloud resource that was scanned, e.g., AWS::EC2::Volume.
- **Severity:** Filters scan events by the severity level of the scan error. Select **Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, **Low**, or **Unknown**.
- **Source Status:** Filters scan events based on the current status of the scanned resource. Select one or all of the following:
  - **Active:**To view events for existing resources.
  - **Deleted:**To view events for resources that have been removed.

[Image: You can view the logs for the error events in the System Logs Page.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Usage Insights

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-usage-insights
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Monitoring & Investigation > Usage Insights > About Usage Insights
- Last modified: 2026-07-08T07:02Z
- Summary: Information on AI Security's Usage Insights pages and how AI applications are being used across your organization.

On the Usage Insights page, you can view AI application usage across departments, users, locations, and sensitive data.

The Usage Insights pages provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Provide you with actionable insights into an organization's AI usage patterns between users and applications.
- Present usage patterns of the application across an organization.
- Analyze granular details of usage patterns based on segment groups, user groups, and users.
- Review usage patterns to design better access policy rules.
- Quickly drill down on insights with the help of multiple filters and operators available.

## About the Usage Insights Page

On the Usage Insights page (Public AI > Usage Insights), you can view insights for the following tabs:

- Users
- Departments
- Locations
- Sensitive Data

Use this tab to view usage insights for users.

1. Select the time period for which you want to see the data. You can select the **Last 1 Day**, **Last 7 Days**, **Last 15 Days**, **Last Month**, or **Last Quarter**.
2. Filter the data for specific **Departments**, **Application Type**, or Policy Actions (**Allowed**, **Blocked**, or **Isolated**).
3. **Total Volume**: View the total volume of data generated by the users.
4. Search by a specific user.
5. The **Users**column populates the data determined by your selections. Each user tile shows the volume of data generated by them and their percentage contribution to the total incidents generated by the application.
6. Select the User for which you want to view the data.
7. The **Apps**column populates the data determined by your selections. Each apps tile shows the volume of data generated by them and their percentage contribution to the total incidents generated by the application. You can view the total number of apps. You can also search for a specific app.

Use this tab to view usage insights for departments.

1. Select the time period for which you want to see the data. You can select the **Last 1 Day**, **Last 7 Days**, **Last 15 Days**, **Last Month**, or **Last Quarter**.
2. Filter the data for specific Departments, Application Type (Gen AI or Embedded AI), or Policy Actions taken (**Allowed**, **Blocked**, or **Isolated**).
3. **Total Volume**: View the total volume of data generated by the department.
4. The **Departments** column populates the data determined by your selections. Each application tile shows the volume of data generated by them and their percentage contribution to the total incidents generated by the department.
5. Select the department for which you want to view the data.
6. The **Apps**column populates the data determined by your selections. Each apps tile shows the volume of data generated by them and their percentage contribution to the total incidents generated by the application.
7. Select the app for which you want to view the data.
8. The **Users** column is updated for the selected app. Each user tile shows the volume of data geenerated by them and the percentage contribution to the total transactions generated by all the users. You can view the total number of users. You can also search for a specific user.

Use this tab to view usage insights for locations.

1. Select the time period for which you want to see the data. You can select the **Last 1 Day**, **Last 7 Days**, **Last 15 Days**, **Last Month**, or **Last Quarter**.
2. Filter the data for specific Locations, Application Type (Gen AI or Embedded AI), or Policy Actions taken (**Allowed**, **Blocked**, or **Isolated**).
3. **Total Volume**: View the total volume of data generated by the department.
4. The **Locations**column populates the data determined by your selections. Each location tile shows the volume of data generated by them and their percentage contribution to the total incidents generated by the location. You can view the total number of locations. You can also search for a specific location.
5. Select the location for which you want to view the data.
6. The **Apps**column populates the data determined by your selections. Each app tile shows the volume of data generated by them and their percentage contribution to the total incidents generated by the application.
7. Select the app for which you want to view the data.
8. The **Users** column is updated for the selected app. Each user tile shows the volume of data generated by them and the percentage contribution to the total transactions generated by all the users. You can view the total number of users. You can also search for a specific user.

Use this tab to view usage insights for sensitive data.

1. Select the time period for which you want to see the data. You can select the **Last 1 Day**, **Last 7 Days**, **Last 15 Days**, **Last Month**, or **Last Quarter**.
2. Filter the data for specific Policy Actions taken (**Allowed**, **Blocked**, or **Isolated**) or Content Type (**DLP Engine**, **DLP Dictionary**, or **ML Category**).
3. **Number of Transactions**: View the number of transactions.
4. The **Applications**column populates the data determined by your selections. Each application tile shows the number of transactions generated by them and their percentage contribution to the total incidents generated by the application.
5. Select the application for which you want to view the data.
6. The **<Content Type>** column populates the data determined by your selections. Each tile shows the number of transactions and their percentage contribution to the total incidents generated by the application.
7. Select the <Content Type> column for which you want to view the data.
8. The **Users** column is updated for the selected Content Type. Each user tile shows the number of users and the percentage contribution to the total transactions generated by all the users. You can view the total number of users. You can search data for a specific user.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-and-managing-custom-roles","lastmod":"2026-06-05T21:06Z","nid":"1540159"} -->
## Adding and Managing Custom Roles

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-and-managing-custom-roles
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Role Management > Adding and Managing Custom Roles
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about how to add a custom role in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can add or edit custom roles and assign them to users to manage tasks in specific modules or global modules.

## Adding a Custom Role

To add a custom role:

1. Go to **Administration**>**Access Roles**.
2. On the **Access Roles** page, click **Add Role**. See image. The **Add Role** window appears.
3. In the **Add Role** window: See image.
  - **Role Name**: Enter a unique name for the custom role. The role name can include letters, numbers, or special characters (hyphen (-) or underscore (_)).
  - **Permissions:**Assign any of the following permissions: For the Scan Settings module, you need to assign **Access** or **View Only** permissions for Cloud Accounts and permissions to start or stop the scan, or edit the scan settings. See image.
    - **Access**: Select the checkbox for tasks that users can perform in each module or global module.
    - **View Only**: Select to provide view only access to specific modules or global modules.
    - **None**: Select to restrict users from accessing or viewing specific modules or global modules.
4. Click **Save**. The custom role is created and displayed on the [Access Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-access-roles) page.

## Editing a Custom Role

You can edit a custom role and modify the permissions to view, access, or restrict access to specific modules.

You cannot edit or delete predefined roles.

To edit a role:

1. Go to **Administration**>**Access Roles**.
2. On the **Access Roles** page, click the **Edit** icon for the custom role that you want to edit. See image.
3. In the **Edit Role** window, change the **Role Name** or **Permissions**, as required. See image.
4. Click **Update**. A message appears indicating that the role is updated successfully.

## Deleting a Custom Role

To delete a custom role:

1. Go to **Administration**>**Access Roles**.
2. On the **Access Roles** page, click the **Delete**icon for the custom role that you want to delete. See image.
3. In the **Delete Role** window, click **Delete**. See image. The role is deleted from the AI Security Admin Portal.

[Image: The Edit Role window with the Role Name field and list of permissions to be added.]

[Image: The Access Roles page with the list of predefined and custom roles.]

[Image: The Delete Role window]

[Image: The Access Roles page with the list of predefined and custom roles.]

[Image: The Add Role window with Role Name field and permissions list]

[Image: The Access Roles page with the list of predefined and custom roles and annotation around Add Role.]

[Image: The Permissions section with the list of global modules.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-microsoft-entra-tenant-details","lastmod":"2026-06-18T21:06Z","nid":"1540115"} -->
## Adding Microsoft Entra Tenant Details

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-microsoft-entra-tenant-details
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > Adding Microsoft Entra Tenant Details
- Last modified: 2026-06-18T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about adding Microsoft Entra tenant details in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The first step in the [onboarding process](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant) is to provide the Microsoft Entra tenant details. AI Security uses the tenant or management group details to generate a template to connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant.

1. Go to **Administration**> **Account Onboarding**.
2. Click **Add New**.
3. Under **Select Cloud Provider**, click the**Azure** tile.
4. Select **Tenant** or **Management Group**.
5. Click **Next**.
6. In the **Tenant Details** section: The role name and service principal name must contain only alphabetic characters, numbers, hyphens ("-"), and underscores ("_").
  - **Integration Alias:**Enter a user-friendly name for the tenant or management group.
  - **Tenant Name**: Enter the name of the tenant that you want to onboard.
  - **Role Name**: Enter a unique role name. This role name is added as a prefix to all the custom roles that are created during the onboarding process.
  - **Tenant ID**: Enter the Microsoft Entra tenant ID. You can find the tenant ID in the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) in multiple ways. For example:
    1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
    2. On the top right, select your account and then click **Switch directory**.
    3. On the **Portal Settings |** **Directories + subscriptions** page, under **All Directories**, copy the **Directory ID** of the corresponding tenant that you want to onboard.
  - **Service Principal**: Enter a unique name for the service principal (application). AI Security creates a service principal with this name in the Microsoft Entra tenant after deploying the [tree discovery template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-tree-discovery-template). The service principal is used to define the access policy and permissions for AI Security to access specific resources within the tenant. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/app-objects-and-service-principals?tabs=browser).
  - **Management Group ID**: Enter the management group ID. You can include multiple management group IDs to onboard the management groups. This field is visible only if you select the Management Group for onboarding.
  - **Notification Emails** (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded tenant. You can add up to 30 email addresses to receive notifications about the issues. You can also add email addresses after completing the onboarding process.
7. Click **Apply**to continue. Click **Reset** if you want to change the details. If all the details are accurate, you are directed to the [Connect to the Tenant](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-tree-discovery-template) section to deploy the tree discovery template.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-organization-details","lastmod":"2026-06-29T21:06Z","nid":"1539740"} -->
## Adding Organization Details

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-organization-details
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Organization > Adding Organization Details
- Last modified: 2026-06-29T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about adding AWS organization details in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The first step in the [onboarding process](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization) is to provide the AWS organization details. AI Security uses these details to generate a template to connect to the AWS organization.

1. Go to **Administration** > **Account Onboarding**.
2. Click **Add New**.
3. In the **Select Cloud Provider** window:
  - For **Select Cloud Type**, select **AWS**.
  - For **Select Onboarding Type**, select **Organization**.
4. Click **Next**.
5. In the **Add New Organization Configuration** section:
  - **Organization Details**:
    - **Integration Alias**: Enter a user-friendly name for the organization that you want to onboard.
    - **Role Name**: Enter a unique role name. This role name is added as a prefix to all the [roles](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/iam-roles-and-permissions-aws) that are created during the onboarding process.
    - **Management Account Name**: Enter the name of the management account. You can find this in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) under **Organization**.
    - **Management Account ID**: Enter the 12-digit AWS account ID of the management account.
    - **Organization ID**: Enter the organization ID that you want to onboard. You can find this in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) in multiple ways. For example:
      1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
      2. On the top right, select your account and then click **Organization**.
      3. In the left-side navigation, copy the **Organization ID**.
    - **Notification Emails** (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded organization. You can add up to 30 email addresses of recipients. You can also add email addresses after completing the onboarding process.
    - **External ID**: View the optional identifier that is autopopulated. This ID is used in an IAM role trust policy to designate a specific user to assume the IAM role to provide access to the AWS resources. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user_externalid.html).
  - **CloudTrail Details**:
    - **CloudTrail Type**: Select the **OrgCloudTrail** checkbox, if it is an organization CloudTrail. [Organization CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-aws-cloudtrail) shares the CloudTrail events of the management and member accounts of the organization to the same CloudTrail S3 bucket. During initial onboarding, AI Security checks for log files to perform data scan in the following paths: After the onboarding is completed successfully, AI Security checks for log files in each target account.
      | CloudTrail Type | Path |
      | --- | --- |
      | Organization CloudTrail | `prefix/<organization ID>/<management account ID>` |
      | Account CloudTrail | `prefix/<management account ID>` |
    - **CloudTrail Bucket Name**: Enter the S3 bucket name that is associated with CloudTrail. This S3 bucket stores the CloudTrail events.
    - **Prefix**: Enter the prefix specified in the CloudTrail S3 bucket path. If your CloudTrail is part of the AWS Control Tower, enter the organization ID as prefix. You can find this on the **Trails**page, under the **Log file prefix**column in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
    - **Bucket Account ID**: Enter the 12-digit AWS account ID where CloudTrail S3 bucket is present.
6. Click **Apply**to continue. Click **Reset** if you want to change the details.

If all the details are accurate, you are directed to the [Connect to the Organization](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-aws-tree-discovery-template) section to deploy the tree discovery template.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/changing-aws-cloudtrail-details","lastmod":"2026-06-18T21:06Z","nid":"1539953"} -->
## Changing AWS CloudTrail Details

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/changing-aws-cloudtrail-details
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > Cloud Trail > Changing AWS CloudTrail Details
- Last modified: 2026-06-18T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about how to change CloudTrail details in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can change the [CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-aws-cloudtrail) for an organization or a single account within the organization as required.

## Prerequisites

- You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with Edit Cloud Accounts permission.
- To configure a cross-account CloudTrail that stores logs in an S3 bucket located in a different account than the onboarded account (member account), enable the following settings:
  - CloudTrail Permissions for Member Accounts
  - Cross-Account Log Decryption
  - KMS Key ID

## Changing AWS CloudTrail for an Organization

The organization CloudTrail shares the CloudTrail events of the management and member accounts of the organization to the same CloudTrail S3 bucket. When you reset the organization's AWS CloudTrail details, the existing CloudTrail is disabled and all the onboarded accounts move to the [Needs Attention](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-onboarding-status)state until the new CloudTrail is validated successfully.

To change AWS CloudTrail for an organization:

1. Go to **Administration**> **Account Onboarding**.
2. Select the organization account for which you want to change the CloudTrail details.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Manage CloudTrail** from the drop-down menu.
4. In the **Organization CloudTrail** window:
  1. Click **Reset** to edit the existing CloudTrail details and add new details.
  2. **CloudTrail Type**: If it is an [organization CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-aws-cloudtrail), select the **OrgCloudTrail** checkbox.
  3. **CloudTrail Bucket Name**: Enter the S3 bucket name that is associated with the CloudTrail.
  4. **Prefix (Optional)**: Enter the prefix specified in the CloudTrail S3 bucket path, if any.
  5. **Bucket Account ID**: Enter the AWS account ID where the CloudTrail S3 bucket is present.
  6. Click **Apply**. A message appears indicating that the CloudTrail details is saved successfully.
  7. Under **Download and Deploy Template,**select one of the following template types:
    - CloudFormation
    - Terraform
  8. Click **Done**.
5. In the **Overview** tab, under the **CloudTrail** section, click **Validate**. After CloudTrail is validated successfully, the CloudTrail status shows as **Enabled**. If there is any issue found while validating the template, the status of the CloudTrail shows **Failed**. Download the template and run it again, and then validate the CloudTrail.

## Changing AWS CloudTrail for Single or Multiple Accounts

When you update the account's CloudTrail, the existing CloudTrail is disabled only for that account, without affecting the other accounts in the organization. The account moves to the [Needs Attention](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-onboarding-status) state until the new CloudTrail is validated successfully.

To change AWS CloudTrail for single or multiple accounts:

1. Go to **Administration** > **Account Onboarding**.
2. Select the AWS account and then select the **Accounts** tab.
3. Choose one of the following options:
  - To change CloudTrail for a single account: Click the **Actions** icon for the account you want to change the CloudTrail details, then select **Update CloudTrail**.
  - To change CloudTrail for multiple accounts:
    1. Select the checkboxes for the required accounts.
    2. From the **Actions**drop-down menu, select **Update CloudTrail**.
4. In the **Update Account CloudTrail** window: AI Security validates the template deployment by checking the new CloudTrail details provided. If there is any error while validating the template, download and rerun the template. You can see the CloudTrail details of the account in the corresponding account drawer.
  1. Click **Reset** to edit the existing CloudTrail details and add new details.
  2. **CloudTrail Bucket Name**: Enter the S3 bucket name that is associated with CloudTrail.
  3. **Prefix (Optional)**: Enter the prefix specified in the CloudTrail S3 bucket path, if any.
  4. **Bucket Account ID**: Enter the AWS account ID where the CloudTrail S3 bucket is present.
  5. Click **Apply**. A message appears indicating that the CloudTrail details is saved successfully.
  6. Under **Download and Deploy Template,**select one of the following template types:
    - CloudFormation
    - Terraform
  7. Click **Done**.

To update the CloudTrail details using the CloudFormation template:

- i. Download the CloudFormation template.
- ii. Update the stack.

In the **Organization CloudTrail** window, click **Organization CloudTrail** to download the template as a YAML file to your local system.

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) using the root account credentials and go to **CloudFormation**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Stacks**.
3. Identify the stack created while [onboarding an organization](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization) and click the stack name.
4. Click **Update**.
5. On the **Update stack** page:
  - **Prepare template**: Select **Replace current template**.
  - **Specify template**: Select **Upload a template file** and click **Choose file**. Browse your folder and select the downloaded YAML file, then click **Open**.
6. Click **Next**.
7. On the **Specify stack details** page, click **Next**.
8. On the **Configure stack options** page, click **Next**.
9. On the **Review stack** page, review the stack details and then select the **I acknowledge** checkbox to acknowledge AWS CloudFormation's creation of IAM resources with custom names.
10. Click **Submit**. On the **Events** tab, you can view the status of the stack execution.

To update the CloudTrail details using the Terraform template:

- i. Download the Terraform template.
- ii. Copy the access keys of the root account.
- iii. Run the Terraform template.

In the **Organization CloudTrail** window, click **Organization CloudTrail** to download the template as a Terraform file to your local system.

Copy the **Access keys** of the root account. The access keys provide AI Security with administrator access to the root account from the AWS CLI.

To copy the access keys:

1. Sign in to the AWS access portal and select the root account.
2. Click **Access keys**.
3. Select the required tab (macOS/Linux, Windows, PowerShell) based on your operating system.
4. Under **Option 1: Set AWS environment variables**, click **Copy**.

1. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
2. Switch to the directory that contains the downloaded template .tf folder.
3. Paste the access keys you copied earlier and press `Enter`.
4. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the Terraform working directory: ``terraform init``See image.
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: ``terraform plan``
  3. To run the Terraform script: ``terraform apply``Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes`and press `Enter`.

To update the CloudTrail details using the CloudFormation template:

- i. Download the CloudFormation template.
- ii. Create a stack.

In the **Update Account CloudTrail** window, click**CloudTrail** to download the template as a YAML file to your local system.

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) for the account you want to change the CloudTrail, and go to **CloudFormation**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Stacks**.
3. Click **Create stack**.
4. On the **Create stack** page:
  1. **Prepare template**: Select **Choose an existing template**.
  2. **Specify template**: Select **Upload a template file**to upload the template you downloaded from the Zscaler Admin Console.
  3. **Upload a template file**: Click **Choose file**, browse and select template, then click **Open**.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Specify stack details**page, under **Stack name**, enter a unique stack name.
7. Click **Next**.
8. On the **Configure stack options** page, click **Next**.
9. On the **Review and create** page, under **Capabilities**, select the **I acknowledge** checkbox to acknowledge AWS CloudFormation's creation of IAM resources with custom names.
10. Click **Submit**.

To update the CloudTrail details using the Terraform template:

- i. Download the Terraform template.
- ii. Copy the access keys of the account for which you want to change the CloudTrail details.
- iii. Run the Terraform template.

In the **Update Account CloudTrail** window, select **Terraform** and click**CloudTrail** to download the template as a Terraform file to your local system.

The access keys provide AI Security with administrator access to the account from the AWS CLI.

To copy the access keys:

1. Sign in to the AWS access portal and select the account for which you want to change the CloudTrail details.
2. Click **Access keys**.
3. Select the required tab (macOS/Linux, Windows, PowerShell) based on your operating system.
4. Under **Option 1: Set AWS environment variables**, click **Copy**.

1. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
2. Switch to the directory that contains the downloaded template .tf folder.
3. Paste the access keys you copied earlier and press `Enter`.
4. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the Terraform working directory: ``terraform init``See image.
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: ``terraform plan``
  3. To run the Terraform script: ``terraform apply``Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes`and press `Enter`.

1. Sign in to the [AWS account](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) where the S3 bucket that stores CloudTrail logs is available, and go to **CloudTrail**.
2. Under **Trails**, select the required CloudTrail.
3. Under **General details**, click the **Trail log location**.
4. Select the S3 bucket, and then select the **Permissions**tab.
5. Under **Bucket policy**, click **Edit**and add the following permissions to write CloudTrail logs of the member accounts in the S3 bucket: `{ "Sid": "AllowCloudTrailWriteLogsFor*<*CloudTrail account ID*>*", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" }, "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::cross-bucketpolicy/AWSLogs/*<*CloudTrail account ID*>*/*", "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "AWS:SourceArn": "arn:aws:cloudtrail:us-west-2:*<*CloudTrail account ID*>*:trail/cross-trail", "s3:x-amz-acl": "bucket-owner-full-control" } }``{ "Sid": "AllowBucketAccessForMembers", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": [ "arn iam::*<*CloudTrail account ID*>*: root" ] } }`
6. Click **Save changes**.

2. Copy the S3 bucket name of the CloudTrail.
3. Sign in to the member account, and go to **CloudTrail**.
4. Click **Create trail**.
5. On the **Choose trail attributes** page:

9. Under **General**details, click **AWS KMS key** to update the policy and provide access to the S3 bucket where the CloudTrail is present.
10. On the **Key policy** tab, click **Edit**to add the following policies: `"Sid": "Enable IAM User Permissions", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": [ "arn:aws:iam::*<*CloudTrail Account ID*>*:root", "arn:aws:iam::*<*S3 bucket account ID*>*:role/DSPM-Role-org-1stjuly", "arn:aws:sts::*<*CloudTrail Account ID*>*:assumed-role/AWSReservedSSO_AdministratorAccess_2d4e2733faaf72bb/*<userID>*" ] },``{ "Sid": "Enable cross account log decryption", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": [ "arn:aws:iam::*<*S3 bucket account ID*>*:role/DSPM-Role-org-1stjuly-get-data-events", "arn:aws:iam::*<*S3 bucket account ID*>*:role/DSPM-Role-org-1stjuly" ] }, "Action": [ "kms:Decrypt", "kms:ReEncryptFrom" ], "Resource": "*", "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "kms:CallerAccount": "*<*S3 bucket account ID*>*" }, "StringLike": { "kms:EncryptionContext:aws:cloudtrail:arn": "arn:aws:cloudtrail:*:*<*CloudTrail Account ID*>*:trail/*" }`

5. Click **Save**.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/changing-aws-orchestrator-account","lastmod":"2026-07-22T23:57Z","nid":"1539930"} -->
## Changing an AWS Orchestrator Account

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/changing-aws-orchestrator-account
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Organization > Changing an AWS Orchestrator Account
- Last modified: 2026-07-22T23:57Z
- Summary: Information on how to change an orchestrator account to a different one for AWS in the AI Security Admin Portal.

AI Security regularly scans the data stores of the target accounts by leveraging the [orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-orchestrator) deployed in the AWS orchestrator account while onboarding.

After [onboarding an organization](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization), you can change the orchestrator account if the existing orchestrator account is being decommissioned, deleted, or if an incorrect account was selected while onboarding. When you change the orchestrator account, you must run the orchestrator template in the new account. AI Security validates the template deployment and updates the [orchestrator status](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-orchestrator-status) accordingly.

Until the new orchestrator account is successfully validated, the following changes occur:

- The existing orchestrator is disabled.
- The AI Security connection status moves to the Waiting for Connection state and Configuration status moves to the Pending state.
- The data scans are stopped.
- The target accounts move to the Needs Attention state.

## Prerequisites

You must be assigned either an [administrator](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/predefined-ai-security-roles-and-permissions) role or a custom role with the Configure New Orchestrator permission in the AI Security Admin Portal.

## Changing an Orchestrator Account

To change the orchestrator account:

1. Go to **Administration** > **Account Onboarding**.
2. Select the organization for which you want to change the orchestrator account.
3. Click **Manage** and then select **Configure New Orchestrator**.
4. In the **Configure New Orchestrator** window, read the caution and then select the **I understand** checkbox.
5. Click **Continue**.
6. In the **Configure an Orchestrator Account** page, select the account and primary region where you want to deploy the orchestrator template, and then click **Next**. The existing orchestrator account checkbox is disabled.
7. In the **Provide Permissions** page, download and run the templates. Before running the template on the new orchestrator account, purge the template that was previously deployed on the existing orchestrator account. You can do this by deleting the corresponding stackset or running the `terraform destroy` command based on the template type.
  1. [Run the orchestrator template.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization#runorchtemplate)
  2. [Run the monitoring template.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization#runmonitoringscopetemplate)
8. Click **Done**.

AI Security validates the template deployment every hour by checking the roles created and permissions granted.

If there is any issue while deploying the template, an error is displayed. Rerun the templates in the orchestrator account and target accounts.

After the template deployment is validated successfully, the target accounts move to the Successfully Configured state, and AI Security begins the [data scan](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings). The orchestrator status (AI Security Connection and Configuration Status) moves to the Successful state.

You can view the orchestrator details on the [Overview](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-onboarded-account-details) tab.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/changing-azure-orchestrator-subscription","lastmod":"2026-06-26T21:06Z","nid":"1541203"} -->
## Changing an Azure Orchestrator Subscription

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/changing-azure-orchestrator-subscription
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > Changing an Azure Orchestrator Subscription
- Last modified: 2026-06-26T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to change an orchestrator subscription to a different one for Azure in the AI Security Admin Portal.

AI Security uses the [orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-orchestrator) that is deployed on the Azure subscription to scan the data stores.

You can change the orchestrator subscription if the existing orchestrator subscription is being decommissioned, deleted, or if an incorrect subscription was selected while onboarding. When you change the orchestrator subscription, you must run the orchestrator template in the new subscription. AI Security validates the template deployment and updates the [orchestrator status](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-orchestrator-status) accordingly.

Until the new orchestrator subscription is successfully validated, the following changes occur:

- The existing orchestrator is disabled.
- The AI Security connection status moves to the Waiting for Connection state and Configuration status moves to the Pending state.
- The data scans are stopped.
- The target subscriptions move to the Needs Attention state.

## Prerequisites

Make sure the following prerequisites are met:

- Be assigned either an [administrator](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/predefined-ai-security-roles-and-permissions) role or any role with the Configure New Orchestrator permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.
- Before redeploying the orchestrator template, you must add your system's IP address to the [Azure storage account](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=845586) and [Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/azure/key-vault/general/how-to-azure-key-vault-network-security)'s IP networks. This is required when multiple users need to apply Terraform from different IP addresses.

## Changing Orchestrator Subscription

To change the orchestrator subscription:

1. Go to **Administration** > **Account Onboarding**.
2. Select the tenant for which you want to change the orchestrator subscription.
3. Click **Manage** and then select **Configure New Orchestrator**.
4. In the **Configure New Orchestrator** window, read the caution and then select the **I understand** checkbox.
5. Click **Continue**.
6. In the **Configure an Orchestrator subscription** page:
  - Select a subscription on which you want to deploy the AI Security's orchestrator template.
  - **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select a region where you want to deploy the orchestrator.
  - **Storage Account Name**: Enter a unique name for the storage account. This storage account is used to store the activity logs of the target subscriptions. It is created while running the onboarding template. The storage account name cannot exceed 16 characters.
  - Select the **Deploy private endpoint for secure communication** checkbox to establish a private connection between AI Security and Azure resources. This restricts communication over public IP addresses.
7. Click **Next**.
8. On the **Provide Permissions** page, download the template to run it in the Microsoft Entra tenant. Before running the template on the new orchestrator subscription, purge the previously deployed template by running the `terraform destroy` command.; If the resource group is manually deleted:Import the following resources:`terraform import "module.control_plane[\"region\"].module.encryption_key.azurerm_key_vault_key.cmk_key""resourceID"`; `terraform import "module.worker_plane[\"region\"].module.encryption_key.azurerm_key_vault_key.cmk_key""resourceID"`; Purge the secret key vault:Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Key vaults**.; Click **Manage deleted vaults**.; On the **Manage deleted key vaults** page:**Subscription**: Select the existing orchestrator subscription.; Select the secrets key vault check box and click **Purge**.
  - a. Download the orchestrator template.
  - b. Update and run the Terraform files.
9. Click **Done**.

AI Security validates the template deployment every hour by checking the roles that are created and permissions granted.

An error message appears if there is any issue while deploying the template. Rerun the template in the root account.

After the template is successfully deployed, the onboarded subscriptions move to the Successfully Configured state and AI Security begins the [data scan](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings). The AI Security Connection and Configuration Status for the orchestrator are displayed as successful.

You can view the orchestrator details on the [Overview](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-onboarding-status) tab.

Click **Azure Onboarding**to download the template as a ZIP file. Extract the file to your local system and create a new folder to store the extracted files. The ZIP file includes multiple Terraform files that contain policies and permissions required for AI Security to connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant.

Update the following downloaded files:

- **backend.tf**: Enter the name of the storage containers where you want to store the Terraform state files.
- **terraform.tfvars**: Change the random_seed value. Remember this seed value and use the same value when you deploy new templates.

1. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
2. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform files.
3. Run the following commands:
  1. To connect to your Microsoft Entra tenant: `az login --tenant <tenant ID>`You are directed to a web browser to authorize the Microsoft Entra tenant. Select your account to confirm the authorization. The command output returns the subscriptions available within your Microsoft Entra tenant.
  2. To set the subscription where you want to run the Terraform template: `az account set --subscription <subscription ID>`
  3. (Optional) To verify if the subscription is accurately set: `az account show`
  4. To initialize the working directory and apply Terraform configuration: `terraform init`
  5. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`
  6. To run the Terraform script: `terraform apply`Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes` and then press `Enter`.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Changing a GCP Orchestrator Account

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/changing-gcp-orchestrator-account
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > GCP Cloud Accounts > Changing a GCP Orchestrator Account
- Last modified: 2026-08-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to change an orchestrator account to a different one for GCP in the AI Security Admin Portal.

AI Security regularly scans the data stores of the target projects by leveraging the [orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-orchestrator) deployed in the GCP orchestrator project while onboarding.

After [onboarding an organization](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-gcp-organization), you can change the orchestrator project if the existing orchestrator project is being decommissioned, deleted, or if an incorrect project was selected while onboarding. When you change the orchestrator project, you must run the orchestrator template in the new project. ai-security validates the template deployment and updates the [orchestrator status](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-orchestrator-status) accordingly.

Until the new orchestrator project is successfully validated, the following changes occur:

- The existing orchestrator is disabled.
- The AI Security connection status moves to the Waiting for Connection state and Configuration status moves to the Pending state.
- The data scans are stopped.
- The target projects move to the Needs Attention state.

## Prerequisites

Be assigned either an [administrator](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/predefined-ai-security-roles-and-permissions)role or a custom role with the Configure New Orchestrator permission in the AI Security Admin Portal.

## Changing Orchestrator Subscription

To change the orchestrator project:

1. Go to **Administration > Account Onboarding**.
2. Select the organization to which you want to change the orchestrator subscription.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Configure New Orchestrator** from the drop-down menu.
4. In the **New Orchestrator** window, read the caution and then select the **I understand** checkbox.
5. Click **Continue**.
6. In the **Configure an Orchestrator project**page:
  - Select an orchestrator project on which you want to deploy the AI Security's orchestrator template.
  - **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select a region where you want to deploy the orchestrator project.
  - **Log Bucket Name**: Enter a unique name for the log bucket. This log bucket stores the activity logs of the target projects. The log bucket is created while deploying the onboarding template. The name must be unique, otherwise AI Security shows an error message.
7. Click **Next**.
8. In the **Grant Permissions** section, download the GCP onboarding template, which includes policies and permissions to create custom roles in the GCP organization, and deploy it on your cloud account. This template provides AI Security with the permissions to access the organization. Before running the template on the new orchestrator subscription, purge the template that was previously deployed on the existing orchestrator by running the `terraform destroy` command.
  - a. In the AI Security Admin Portal
  - b. On the Local System
9. Click **Done**. AI Security validates the template deployment every hour by checking the roles that are created and permissions granted. An error message appears if there is any issue while deploying the template. Rerun the template in the root account. After the template is successfully deployed, the AI Security begins the [data scan](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings) for the onboarded projects, and you are directed to the [Overview page](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-onboarding-status) to view the status of the onboarded project and orchestrator details.

Click **GCP Onboarding** to download the template as a ZIP file.

Update and run the template in the gcloud using the CLI app:

1. Extract the downloaded ZIP file to a local directory on your system.
2. Locate the `backend.tf` file within the extracted folder and open it in a text editor.
3. Update the file by adding the name of the storage bucket and a preferred prefix where you would like to store the Terraform state files, and then, save and close the `backend.tf` file.
4. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app on your local system.
5. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform file.
6. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the working directory and apply the Terraform configuration: `terraform init`
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`For **Enter a value**, enter the regions where you want AI Security to monitor and scan data in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]`AI Security creates resources required for data scanning only in these specified regions.
  3. To run the Terraform script: `terraform apply`For **Enter a value**, enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]`For **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes` and then press `Enter`.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Configuring the AWS Network

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-aws-network
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Custom Network Configuration > Configuring the AWS Network
- Last modified: 2026-06-25T09:45Z
- Summary: How to configure the AWS network and allow AI Security to scan data in the AWS resources.

AI Security requires a specific network configuration to be able to access the services, scan the data in the resources, compute, and report the findings. You must configure a custom network in your organization by creating the following control plane and worker plane virtual private clouds (VPCs) in the [orchestrator account](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/selecting-aws-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope):

- **Control Plane VPC**: Create this VPC only in the primary region where the orchestrator is going to run.
- **Worker Plane VPC**: Create this VPC in all the regions where the resources exist. For example, if the S3 buckets are stored in US West and US East regions, create the worker plane VPCs in both regions.

Ensure that both control and worker planes do not have overlapping Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR).

## Configure AWS Network

You can configure the AWS network manually or deploy the predefined templates:

- Manual Configuration
- Deploy Predefined Templates

After the control plane and worker plane network components are created, peer the VPCs between the control plane and all worker plane.

## Peer the VPCs

After creating the control and worker plane VPC, you need to peer these VPCs, so they can communicate with each other. This step is common for both manual and template-based configurations.

1. In the [AWS console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/), go to the **Peering Connections** page.
2. Click **Create peering connection**.
3. On the **Create peering connection** page: The peering connection is displayed on the **Peering connections** page, and it is in the **Pending acceptance** state.
  1. **Name**: Enter a name for the VPC peering connection.
  2. **VPC ID (Requestor)**: Select the control plane VPC.
  3. **VPC ID (Accepter)**: Select the worker plane VPC.
  4. Click **Create peering connection**.
4. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Accept request**.
5. Review the details and click **Accept request**.
6. Update the route tables for both control plane and worker plane VPCs to enable traffic flow between the VPCs.
  - Update control plane VPC route table
  - Update worker plane VPC route table
7. Add the private subnets of the control and worker planes.
8. For **NAT Gateway**, add a route with destination `0.0.0.0/0` as needed.
9. Confirm that the route tables reflect the correct peering connections and IP ranges.

Repeat the steps for other target regions.

1. Go to the **Route Tables**, and select the route table associated with the control plane VPC.
2. In the **Routes** tab, click **Edit routes**.
3. Click **Add route** and configure:
  1. **Destination**: Enter the IP address of your worker plane VPC.
  2. **Target**: Select **Peering Connection**, and then choose the appropriate peering connection.
4. Click **Save changes**.

1. Go to the **Route Tables**, and select the route table associated with the worker plane VPC.
2. In the **Routes** tab, click **Edit routes**.
3. Click **Add route** and configure:
  1. **Destination**: Enter the IP address of your control plane VPC.
  2. **Target**: Select **Peering Connection**, and then choose the appropriate peering connection.
4. Click **Save changes**.

- 1. Create the control plane VPC.
- 2. Create the worker plane VPC.
- 3. Create the control plane security group.
- 4. Create the worker plane security group.
- 5. Create the DB subnet group.

To deploy the templates, identify the template type you want to use.

- CloudFormation Template
- Terraform Template

To deploy the Terraform template:

- 1. Download the Terraform template.
- 2. Update and deploy Terraform to create control plane VPC.
- 3. Update and deploy Terraform to create worker plane VPC.

1. Open a file explorer and browse to the location where the downloaded `.zip` file was extracted. Then, open the `control-plane` folder.
2. Locate and open the`backend.tf` file in a text editor.
3. Update the file with the name of the storage services where you want to store the Terraform state files. For example: Replace the placeholders with the actual values for your storage services.
  - `**resource_group_name**: "``<resource_group_name>``"`
  - `**storage_account_name**: "``<storage_account_name>``"`
  - `**container_name**: "``<container_name>``"`
  - `**key**: "``aisec-control-plane-network-configuration.tfstate``"`
4. Save the updated file.
5. Run the following commands: Executing these steps creates the control plane network components.
  1. To initialize the Terraform working directory: `terraform init`
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`
  3. To execute the planned changes to your infrastructure: `terraform apply -auto-approve`The `-auto-approve` flag skips the interactive approval step, automatically applying the changes.

1. Open a file explorer and browse to the location where the downloaded `.zip` file was extracted. Then, open the `worker-plane` folder.
2. Locate and open the`backend.tf` file in a text editor.
3. Update the file with the name of the storage services where you want to store the Terraform state files. For example: Replace the placeholders with the actual values for your storage services.
  - `**resource_group_name**: "``<resource_group_name>``"`
  - `**storage_account_name**: "``<storage_account_name>``"`
  - `**container_name**: "``<container_name>``"`
  - `**key**: "``<name>``.tfstate``"`
4. Save the updated file.
5. Run the following commands: Executing these steps creates the worker plane network components.
  1. To initialize the Terraform working directory: `terraform init`
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`
  3. To execute the planned changes to your infrastructure: `terraform apply -auto-approve`The `-auto-approve` flag skips the interactive approval step, automatically applying the changes.

Download the Terraform templates file as a ZIP file and extract it to a folder on your system.

[Download the Terraform templates](https://help.zscaler.com/downloads/ai-asset-mgmt/cloud-accounts-onboarding/aws-cloud-accounts/aws-account/aws-network-template-tft.zip)

The `.zip` file includes two folders, one for the worker plane and another for the control plane that contain policies and permissions required for AI Security to create required network configurations in the AWS organization.

To deploy the CloudFormation template:

- 1. Download the CloudFormation template.
- 2. Create Stack for control plane VPC in the AWS Management Console.
- 3. Create Stack for worker plane VPC in the AWS Management Console.

Download the CloudFormation templates file as a ZIP file and extract it to a folder on your system.

[Download the CloudFormation templates](https://help.zscaler.com/downloads/ai-asset-mgmt/cloud-accounts-onboarding/aws-cloud-accounts/aws-account/aws-network-template-cft.zip)

The `.zip` file includes two YAML files that contains policies and permissions required for AI Security to create required network configurations in the AWS organization.

1. Sign in to the root account [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **CloudFormation**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Stacks**.
3. Click **Create Stack**, and then select **With new resources (standard)**.
4. On the **Create stack** page:
  - **Prerequisite - Prepare template**: Select **Choose an existing template**.
  - **Specify template**: Select **Upload a template file** and click **Choose file**. Browse to the location where the downloaded .zip file is extracted, select the **aws_worker_plane_network_components_cft.yml** file, and then click **Open**.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Specify Stack Details** page:
  - **Stack name**: Enter a unique name for the Stack.
  - For the **Parameters** section:
    - **Name for the network components**: Enter the name for the network components.
    - **Worker plane VPC CIDR range**: Enter the IPV4 address range for the VPC, preferably `/24`.
    - **Worker plane public subnet A CIDR range**: Enter the IPV4 address range for the first public subnet CIDR, preferably `/24`.
    - **Worker plane public subnet B CIDR range**: Enter the IPV4 address range for the second public subnet CIDR, preferably `/24`.
    - **Worker plane private subnet A CIDR range**: Enter the IPV4 address range for the first private subnet CIDR, preferably `/24`.
    - **Worker plane private subnet B CIDR range**: Enter the IPV4 address range for the second private subnet CIDR, preferably `/24`.
    - **Control plane VPC CIDR range**: Enter the IPv4 address range for the control plane VPC.
7. Click **Next**.
8. On the **Configure Stack options** page, click **Next**.
9. On the **Review and create** page, review the Stack details of worker plane VPC.
10. Click **Submit**.

Repeat steps for all other worker regions.

If you encounter a conflicting S3 bucket error during Stack creation, try deleting the existing bucket and retry the Stack creation. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/delete-bucket.html).

Before creating a new Stack for the new control plane, delete the old control plane's existing infrastructure to avoid conflicts.

1. Sign in to the root account [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **CloudFormation**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Stack**.
3. Click **Create Stack**, and then select **With new resources (standard)**.
4. On the **Choose a template** page:
  - **Prerequisite - Prepare template**: Select **Choose an existing template**.
  - **Specify template**: Select **Upload a template file** and click **Choose file**. Browse to the location where the downloaded .zip file is extracted, select the **aws_control_plane_network_components_cft.yml** file, and then click **Open**.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Specify Stack Details** page:
  - **Stack name**: Enter a unique name for the Stack.
  - For the **Parameters** section:
    - **Name for the network components**: Enter the name for the network components.
    - **Control plane VPC CIDR range**: Enter the IPV4 address range for the VPC, preferably `/24`.
    - **Control plane public subnet CIDR range**: Enter the IPV4 address range for the public subnet CIDR, preferably `/24`.
    - **Control plane private subnet CIDR range**: Enter the IPV4 address range for the private subnet CIDR, preferably `/24`.
7. Click **Next**.
8. On the **Review** page, review the Stack details of control plane VPC.
9. Click **Submit**.

If you encounter a conflicting S3 bucket error during Stack creation, try deleting the existing bucket and retry the Stack creation. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/delete-bucket.html).

1. Sign in to the [AWS console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
2. Go to the **VPC**page and click **Create VPC**.
3. Under **Create VPC**:
  1. **Resources to create**: Select **VPC and more**.
  2. **Name tag auto-generation**: Enter the name tag for the VPC and its associated resources.
  3. **IPV4 CIDR block**: Enter the IPV4 address range for the VPC, preferably `/24`.
  4. **IPv6 CIDR block**: Select **No IPv6 CIDR block**.

  9. **Number of private subnets**: Select **1**.
  10. **Customize subnets CIDR blocks**: Retain the default value.
  11. **NAT Gateways**: Select **In 1AZ**.
  12. **VPC endpoints**: Select **S3 Gateway**.
  13. **DNS options**: Select the **Enable** **DNS hostnames** and **Enable** **DNS resolution** checkboxes.
4. Click **Create VPC**.

1. Sign in to the [AWS console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
2. Go to the **VPC** page and click **Create VPC**.
3. Under **Create VPC**:
  1. **Resources to create**: Select **VPC and more**.
  2. **Name tag auto-generation**: Enter the name tag for the VPC and its associated resources.

The DB subnet group is required for AI Security to be able to scan the RDS databases.

1. In the [AWS console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/), go to the **Subnet group** page.
2. Click **Create DB subnet group**.
3. Enter the **Name** and **Description** for the DB subnet group.
