## Configuring the Azure Network

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-azure-network
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Custom Network Configuration > Configuring the Azure Network
- Last modified: 2026-07-22T20:47Z
- Summary: How to configure the Azure network and allow AI Security to scan data in the Azure resources.

AI Security requires a specific network configuration to be able to access the Azure services, scan the resources, compute, and report the findings. You must configure a custom network in your organization by creating the following virtual networks (VNets) in the [orchestrator](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/selecting-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope) subscription:

- **Control Plane VNet**: Create this VNet only in the primary region where the orchestrator is going to run.
- **Worker Plane VNet**: Create this VNet in all the regions where the resources exist. For example, if the Azure storage accounts are stored in East US and Central US regions, create the worker plane VNet in both regions.

Ensure that both control and worker plane VNets do not have overlapping Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR).

## Configure Azure Network

You can configure the Azure network manually or deploy the predefined templates:

- Manual Configuration
- Deploy Predefined Templates

## Peer the VNets

After creating the control and worker plane VNets, you need to peer these VNets so they can communicate with each other. This step is common for both manual and template-based configurations.

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
2. Go to the **Virtual networks** page.
3. Select the **Control plane VNet**.
4. Go to **Settings** > **Peerings** > **Add**.
5. On the **Add peering** page: After the peering is successfully configured, the **Peering state** is updated to **Connected** and the **Sync status** to **Fully Synchronized**. Repeat the steps for other target regions
  1. **Peering link name**: Enter a name for the peering link.
  2. **Virtual network deployment model**: Retain the default selection.
  3. **Subscription**: Select the orchestrator subscription from the drop-down menu.
  4. **Virtual network**: Select the worker plane VNet from the drop-down menu.
  5. **Remote virtual network peering**: Retain the default value.
  6. **Local virtual network summary**: Enter the peering link name.
  7. **Local virtual network peering** : Retain the default value.
  8. Click **Add**.

To configure the Azure network manually:

- 1. Create the control plane VNet.
- 2. Create the worker plane VNet.
- 3. Configure the control plane network security group.
- 4. Configure the worker plane network security group.
- 5. Configure the network security group for Azure PostgreSQL Server.

A network security group needs to be created and configured to ensure communication with Azure PostgreSQL Server.

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
2. Go to the **Network security groups** page, and click **Create**.
3. On the **Create network security group** page:
  1. **Subscription**: Select the subscription where the custom configuration worker plane is created.
  2. **Resource group**: Select the resource group where the custom configuration worker plane is created.
  3. **Name**: Enter a name for the security group.
  4. **Region**: Select the same region where the worker plane VNet is created.
  5. Click **Review + Create**.
4. Click **Create**.
5. Configure security rules. Add a rule to allow PostgreSQL inbound. Add a rule to deny all inbound communication to the orchestrator. Add a rule to deny internet access.
  1. Open the created security group and go to **Settings** > **Inbound security rules**.
  2. Click **Add**.
  3. On the **Add inbound security rules** page:
    1. **Source**: Select **Service Tag** from the drop-down menu.
    2. **Source service tag**: Select **VirtualNetwork** from the drop-down menu.
    3. **Source port ranges**: Enter an asterisk (*).
    4. **Destination**: Select **Any** from the drop-down menu.
    5. **Service**: Select **PostgresSQL** from the drop-down menu.
    6. **Action**: Select the **Allow**option.
    7. **Priority**: Set **100**.
    8. **Name**: Enter a name for the rule.
  4. Click **Add**.
  1. Open the created security group and go to **Settings** > **Inbound security rules**.
  2. Click **Add**.
  3. On the **Add inbound security rules** page:
    1. **Source**: Select **Any** from the drop-down menu.
    2. **Source port ranges**: Enter an asterisk (*).
    3. **Destination**: Select **Any** from the drop-down menu.
    4. **Service**: Select **Custom**from the drop-down menu.
    5. **Action**: Select the **Deny**option.
    6. **Priority**: Set **2000**.
    7. **Name**: Enter a name for the rule.
  4. Click **Add**.
  1. Open the created security group and go to **Settings** > **Outbound security rules**.
  2. Click **Add**.
  3. On the **Add outbound security rules** page:
    1. **Source**: Select **Any** from the drop-down menu.
    2. **Source port ranges**: Enter an asterisk (*).
    3. **Destination**: Select **Any** from the drop-down menu.
    4. **Destination service tag**: Select **Internet** from the drop-down menu.
    5. **Service**: Select **Custom**from the drop-down menu.
    6. **Destination port ranges**: Enter an asterisk (*).
    7. **Priority**: Set **2010**.
    8. **Name**: Enter a name for the rule.
  4. Click **Add**.

To deploy the templates:

- 1. Create a resource group for the control plane.
- 2. Create a resource group for the worker plane.
- 3. Download and configure the template.
- 4. Initialize the template.
- 5. Deploy the control plane template.
- 6. Deploy the worker plane template.

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and [create a new resource group](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/manage-resource-groups-portal) or select an existing one.
2. On the **Create a resource group** page, on the **Basics** tab, provide the details:
  1. **Subscription**: Select your Azure subscription from the drop-down menu.
  2. **Resource Group**: Enter a name for the resource group.
  3. **Region**: Choose the location where you want to create the resource group from the drop-down menu.
3. Click **Next: Tags >**.
4. In the **Tags**tab, add the following tags: Replace `<tag_name>`, `<tag_value>`, `<your_name>` with appropriate values.
  - Tag 1: **Name** = `<tag_name>`, **Value** = `<tag_value>`.
  - Tag 2: **Name** = `<owner>`, **Value** = `<your_name>`.
5. Click **Next: Review + create >**.
6. In the **Review + create**tab, click **Create**.

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and [create a new resource group](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/manage-resource-groups-portal) or select an existing one.
2. On the **Create a resource group** page, on the **Basics** tab, provide the details:
  1. **Subscription**: Select your Azure subscription from the drop-down menu.
  2. **Resource Group**: Enter a name for the resource group.
  3. **Region**: Choose the location where you want to create the resource group from the drop-down menu.
3. Click **Next: Tags >**.
4. In the **Tags**tab, add the following tag: Replace `<your_name>` with the appropriate value.
  - Tag 1: **Name** = `<owner>`, **Value** = `<your_name>`.
5. Click **Next: Review + create >**.
6. In the **Review + create**tab, click **Create**.

1. Download the Azure Network Configuration template file as a ZIP file and extract it to a folder on your system. [Download the template](https://help.zscaler.com/downloads/ai-asset-mgmt/cloud-accounts-onboarding/microsoft-azure-cloud-accounts/azure-network-template.zip)
2. Open the `control-plane` folder and locate the `backend.tf` file in the folder and open it in a text editor.
3. Update the following details in the `backend.tf` file: For more information on the fields, refer to the `README.md` file.
  1. **resource_group_name**: Update the `<resource_group_name>` with the resource group of the storage account where you want to save the Terraform state files.
  2. **storage_account_name**: Update the `<storage_account_name>` with the name of the storage account.
  3. **container_name**: Update the `<container_name>` with the name of the container.
  4. **key**: unique key for the storage account.
4. Save and close the `backend.tf` file.
5. Open the `worker-plane` folder and locate the `backend.tf` file in the folder and open it in a text editor.
6. Update the following details in the `backend.tf` file: For more information on the fields or region format, refer to the `README.md` file.
  1. **resource_group_name**: Update the `<resource_group_name>` with the resource group of the storage account where you want to save the Terraform state files.
  2. **storage_account_name**: Update the `<storage_account_name>` with the name of the storage account.
  3. **container_name**: Update the `<container_name>` with the name of the container.
  4. **key**: unique key for the storage account, including the region where you want to configure the network.
7. Save and close the `backend.tf` file.

Use any of the following methods:

- Cloud Shell
- Command Prompt

1. Sign in to the Azure portal, and click **Cloud Shell**.
2. In the **Welcome to Azure Cloud Shell** window, select **Bash**or **PowerShell**, as required.
3. In the **Getting started** window:
  1. Select **Mount storage account**.
  2. Select the storage account subscription from the list.
  3. Click **Apply**.
4. In the **Mount storage account** window, select **Select existing storage account**and click **Next**.
5. In the **Select storage account** window:
  1. **Subscription**: Select the subscription where the storage account is created.
  2. **Resource group**: Select the resource group from the list.
  3. **Storage account name**: Select the storage account.
  4. **File share**: Click **Create a file share**and enter a name for the new file.
  5. Click **Select**.
6. Use any of the following:
  - Azure PowerShell
  - Bash

1. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
2. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform file.
3. Connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant by running the following command: `az login --tenant <tenant ID>`You are directed to a web browser to authorize the Microsoft Entra tenant. Select your account to confirm the authorization. The command output returns the subscriptions available.

1. Zip the modified template and upload the folder to the PowerShell environment:
  1. Click **Manage files** and select **Upload**.
  2. Browse for the template and click **Open**.
2. Run the following commands:
  1. To move the `azure_network_components.zip` file from its current location to the `/home/``<user_name>``/clouddrive` folder: `mv azure_network_components.zip /home/<user_name>/clouddrive`Replace `<user_name>` with appropriate values.
  2. To switch to the clouddrive folder: `cd /home/<user_name>/clouddrive`Replace `<user_name>` with appropriate values.
  3. To extract the `azure_network_components.zip` file: `unzip azure_network_components.zip`The `azure_network_components.zip` file contains two folders: `control-plane` and `worker-plane`.
  4. To switch to the extracted template folder: `cd <folder name>`Replace `<folder name>` with `control-plane` or `worker-plane`, depending on the template to deploy.

1. Run the following commands to prepare the Bash environment:
  1. Click **Manage files** and select **Upload**.
  2. Browse for the template and click **Open**.
2. Run the following commands:
  1. To move the `azure_network_components.zip` file from its current location to the `/home/``<user_name>``/clouddrive` folder: `mv azure_network_components.zip /home/<user_name>/clouddrive`Replace `<user_name>` with appropriate values.
  2. To switch to the clouddrive folder: `cd /home/<user_name>/clouddrive`Replace `<user_name>` with appropriate values.
  3. To extract the `azure_network_components.zip` file: `unzip azure_network_components.zip`The `azure_network_components.zip` file contains two folders: `control-plane` and `worker-plane`.
  4. To switch to the extracted template folder: `cd <folder name>`Replace `<folder name>` with `control-plane` or `worker-plane`, depending on the template to deploy.

1. Set the Subscription and Initialize the Terraform Configuration
  1. Open a terminal and run the following command to set the subscription where the storage containers containing the Terraform state files are stored: `az account set --subscription <SUBSCRIPTION-ID>`Replace `<SUBSCRIPTION-ID>` with the actual ID of your subscription.
  2. To initialize the working directory and apply Terraform configuration: `terraform init`
2. Run the following command to deploy the control plane: `terraform apply -auto-approve -var='control_plane_component_name=<CONTROL_PLANE_COMPONENT_NAME>' -var='control_plane_region=<CONTROL_PLANE_REGION>' -var='control_plane_vnet_cidr=["<CONTROL_PLANE_VNET_CIDR>"]' -var='control_plane_vnet_subnet_address_range=["<CONTROL_PLANE_VNET_SUBNET_ADDRESS_RANGE>"]' -var='resource_group=<RESOURCE_GROUP>' -var='scanner_subscription_id=<SCANNER_SUBSCRIPTION_ID>' -var='outbound_ips=["<IP_1>","<IP_2>","<IP_3>","<IP_4>"]'`Replace the placeholders with the actual values:
  - `<CONTROL_PLANE_COMPONENT_NAME>`: The name of the control plane component to be deployed.
  - `<CONTROL_PLANE_REGION>`: The region where the control plane needs to be deployed in a format supported by the cloud provider, such as `centralus` or `eastus`.
  - `<CONTROL_PLANE_VNET_CIDR>`: The CIDR block for the virtual network of the control plane, such as `10.0.0.0/24`.
  - `<CONTROL_PLANE_VNET_SUBNET_ADDRESS_RANGE>`: The address range for subnet within the VNet of the control plane, such as `10.0.0.0/24`.
  - `<RESOURCE_GROUP>`: The name of the resource group where the control plane needs to be deployed.
  - `<SCANNER_SUBSCRIPTION_ID>`: The subscription ID of your cloud environment that will be used by the scanner.
  - `<IP_#>`: The AI Security IP address that needs to be placed on the allowlist, such as `[ "``35.164.218.12``", "``34.208.206.171``", "``52.42.215.70``", "``35.84.226.159``", "``52.40.209.233``", "``54.191.175.18``"]`

1. Run the following command to provide back-end details for the new regions: `terraform apply -auto-approve -var='control_plane_vnet_cidr=["<CONTROL_PLANE_VNET_CIDR>"]' -var='resource_group=<RESOURCE_GROUP>' -var='scanner_subscription_id=<SCANNER_SUBSCRIPTION_ID>' -var='worker_plane_component_name=<WORKER_PLANE_COMPONENT_NAME>' -var='worker_plane_region=<WORKER_PLANE_REGION>' -var='worker_plane_vnet_cidr=["<WORKER_PLANE_VNET_CIDR>"]' -var='worker_plane_vnet_subnet_address_range=["<WORKER_PLANE_VNET_SUBNET_ADDRESS_RANGE>"]' -var='worker_plane_vnet_subnet_postgres_address_range=["<WORKER_PLANE_VNET_SUBNET_POSTGRES_ADDRESS_RANGE>"]' -var='outbound_ips=["<IP_1>","<IP_2>","<IP_3>","<IP_4>"]'`Replace the placeholders with the actual values for your:
  - `<CONTROL_PLANE_VNET_CIDR>`: The CIDR block for the control plane VNet.
  - `<RESOURCE_GROUP>`: The name of the resource group for the worker plane.
  - `<SCANNER_SUBSCRIPTION_ID>`: The ID of the scanner subscription.
  - `<WORKER_PLANE_COMPONENT_NAME>`: The name of the worker plane component.
  - `<WORKER_PLANE_REGION>`: The region for the worker plane (e.g. centralus).
  - `<WORKER_PLANE_VNET_CIDR>`: The CIDR block for the worker plane VNet.
  - `<WORKER_PLANE_VNET_SUBNET_ADDRESS_RANGE>`: The address range for the worker plane VNet subnet.
  - `<WORKER_PLANE_VNET_SUBNET_POSTGRES_ADDRESS_RANGE>`: The address range for the worker plane VNet subnet for Postgres.
  - `<IP_#>`: The AI Security IP address that needs to be placed on the allowlist, such as `[ "``35.164.218.12``", "``34.208.206.171``", "``52.42.215.70``", "``35.84.226.159``", "``52.40.209.233``", "``54.191.175.18``"]`

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
2. Go to the **Virtual networks** page, and click **Create**.
3. On the **Create virtual network** page, on the **Basics** tab:
  1. **Subscription**: Select the orchestrator subscription from the drop-down menu.
  2. **Resource group**: Select the resource group from the drop-down menu.
  3. **Virtual network name**: Enter a name for the virtual network.
  4. **Region**: Select the primary region where the orchestrator is going to be deployed.
4. Click **Next**.
5. On the **Security** tab, select **Virtual network encryption** if the virtual machines used for scanning have network acceleration enabled.
6. Click **Next**.
7. On the **IP addresses** tab, enter the subnet address space, preferably`/24`.
8. Click the **Edit**icon for the subnet.
9. On the**Edit subnet** page, go to the **Security** section and complete the following:
  1. Click **Create new** to add a new **NAT Gateway**.
  2. Enter the **Name**, **Public IP address**, and **Public IP prefix**, then click **OK**.
  3. Click **Create new** to add a new **Network security group**.
  4. Provide a name for the **Network security group**, then click **OK**.
  5. In the **Service Endpoints** section, add the following services:
    - Microsoft.KeyVault
    - Microsoft.Sql
    - Microsoft.Storage.Global
  6. In the **Network Policy for Private Endpoints** section, select **Disabled**, then click **Save**.
10. Click **Next**.
11. Add tags for the **virtual network**.
12. Click **Next**.
13. Click **Create** on the **Review** page. The control plane VNet is created.

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
2. Go to the **Virtual networks** page, and click **Create**.
3. On the **Create virtual network** page, on the **Basics** tab:
  1. **Subscription**: Select the orchestrator subscription from the drop-down menu.
  2. **Resource group**: Select the resource group from the drop-down menu.
  3. **Virtual network name**: Provide a name for the virtual network.
  4. **Region**: Select the region where the data stores are located.
4. Click **Next**.
5. On the **Security** tab, select **Virtual network encryption** if the virtual machines used for scanning have **Network acceleration** enabled.
6. Click **Next**.
7. On the **IP addresses** tab, enter the subnet address space, preferably `/20`.
8. Click the **Edit**icon for the default subnet.
9. On the **Edit Subnet**page, go to the **Security** section and complete the following:
  1. Click **Create new** to add a new **NAT Gateway**.
  2. Enter the **Name**, **Public IP address**, and **Public IP prefix**, then click **OK**.
  3. Click **Create new** to add a new **Network security group**.
  4. Provide a name for the **Network security group**, then click **OK**.
  5. In the **Service Endpoints** section, add the following services:
    - Microsoft.KeyVault
    - Microsoft.Sql
    - Microsoft.Storage.Global
  6. In the **Network Policy for Private Endpoints** section, select **Disabled**, then click **Save**.
10. To enable the scanning for Azure PostgreSQL Server, you must configure a network security group for Azure PostgreSQL Server, and then create a delegated subnet:
  1. On the **IP addresses** tab, click **Add a subnet**.
  2. On the **Add a subnet** page, enter the **Name**, and select the required **Network security group** for the subnet.
  3. In the **Subnet Delegation** section, from the **Delegate subnet to a service** drop-down menu, select **Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers**, then click **Add**.
11. Click **Next**.
12. Add tags for the **virtual network**.
13. Click **Next**.
14. Click **Create** on the **Review** page. The worker plane VNet is created. Repeat the steps for other regions where data stores need to be scanned.

Add the following inbound and outbound security rules for the control plane network security group. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/manage-network-security-group?tabs=network-security-group-portal#security-rule-settings).

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
2. Go to the **Network security groups** page.
3. Select the **control plane network security group** you created while configuring the control plane.
4. Add the following rules: The following outbound rules are required if [Microsoft Information Protection](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/selecting-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope) labeling is enabled:
  - Deny all inbound communication to the orchestrator
  - Allow inbound communication from the control plane to the worker plane
  - Deny all outbound communication from the orchestrator with lesser priority
  - Allow outbound communication from the orchestrator to the scanner
  - Allow outbound communication from the orchestrator to AI Security
  - Allow outbound communication from the orchestrator to Azure cloud
  - Allow outbound communication from the orchestrator to Microsoft Information Protection
  - Allow outbound communication from the orchestrator to Microsoft Entra ID
  - Allow outbound communication from the orchestrator to Azure Front Door Frontend
  - Allow outbound communication from the orchestrator to Azure Front Door FirstParty
  - Allow outbound communication from the orchestrator to Outlook domain MIP

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-gcp-network","lastmod":"2026-08-06T21:06Z","nid":"1541997"} -->
## Configuring the GCP Network

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-gcp-network
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Custom Network Configuration > Configuring the GCP Network
- Last modified: 2026-08-06T21:06Z
- Summary: How to configure the GCP network and allow DSPM to scan data in the GCP resources.

AI Security requires a specific network configuration to be able to access the GCP services, scan the resources, compute, and report the findings. You must configure a custom network in your organization by creating the following virtual private cloud (VPC) in the [orchestrator project](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-gcp-organization):

- **Control Plane VPC**: Create this VPC only in the primary region where the orchestrator is going to run.
- **Worker Plane VPC**: Create this VPC in all the regions where the resources exist. For example, if the GCP projects are stored in East US and Central US regions, create the worker plane VPC in both regions.

Ensure that both control and worker plane VPC do not have overlapping Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR).

You can configure the GCP network manually or deploy the predefined templates:

- 1. Create the control plane VPC and associated resources.
- 2. Configure the control plane network firewall rules.
- 3. Create the worker plane VPC and associated resources.
- 4. Configure the worker plane network firewall rules.
- 5. Set up private service access in the worker plane VPC.
- 6. Peer the control and worker plane VPCs.
- 7. Configure Cloud NAT gateway resources.

A Cloud NAT resource is required to allow VMs in a VPC to connect to other VPC resources and outbound internet connections. The Cloud NAT Gateway is a region-specific and network-specific resource that must be created for each combination. For the primary region where data stores are to be scanned, two Cloud NAT gateways need to be created, one for the control plane VPC and one for the worker plane VPC.

To set up control plane and worker plane Cloud NAT resources in the orchestrator project:

1. Go to [Network Services](https://console.cloud.google.com/net-services/) in the Google Cloud console and select **Cloud NAT**.
2. Click **CREATE CLOUD NAT GATEWAY**.
3. On the **Create Cloud NAT gateway** page:
  1. **Gateway name**: Enter a name for the Control Plane NAT Gateway.
  2. **NAT type**: Set the NAT type to **Public**.
  3. In the **Select Cloud Router** options:
    1. **Network**: Select the Control Plane VPC Network.
    2. **Region**: Select the region as the Control VPC network.
    3. **Cloud Router**: Select **CREATE NEW ROUTER**.
    4. In the **Create a router** drawer, provide a name for the control plane router and retain the default configurations.
    5. Click **CREATE**. See image.
  4. In the **Cloud NAT mapping**, for **Source endpoint type**, select the **VM instance, GKE nodes, Serverless**. Retain the default configurations.
  5. Click **Create**. See image.
  6. Repeat the steps for the Worker Plane Cloud NAT Gateway, for each region where data stores are present, selecting the Worker Plane VPC Network in **Cloud Router** options.

[Image: Create Cloud NAT gateway page with required values to configure the NAT gateway.]

[Image: Create a router pane pane.]

After the control and worker plane VPCs are created, they need to be peered so that the control and worker planes can communicate.

To peer the control and worker plane VPCs:

1. Go to the **VPC networks** page, and select the created control plane VPC network.
2. On the **VPC network details** page, select the **VPC NETWORK PEERING** tab.
3. Click **ADD PEERING**.
4. On the **Create peering connection** page:
  1. Provide a name for the peering connection.
  2. In the **Peered VPC network** dropdown, select the worker plane VPC in the orchestrator project. Retain the default selections for the remaining configurations.
5. Click **CREATE**. The peering status in the control plane VPC is **Inactive**. See image.
6. Repeat the steps for the worker plane VPC, selecting the control plane VPC in the **Peered VPC network** drop-down menu.

After successful configuration of the peering, the peering status is updated to **Active** for both the control plane VPC and worker plane VPC.

[Image: Create peering connection with required values]

After the worker plane VPC is created, set up private service access in the worker plane VPC. This is used for scanning GCP Cloud SQL instances.

To set up private access in the worker plane VPC:

1. Select the worker plane VPC network.
2. Select the **Private Services Access** tab. See image.
3. Select the **ALLOCATED IP RANGES FOR SERVICES** tab.
4. Click **ALLOCATE IP RANGE** and enter the following values:
  1. **Name**: Enter `private-service-access-ip-range`.
  2. **IP range**: Select **Automatic**.
  3. **Prefix length**: Enter `16`.
5. Click **ALLOCATE**. See image.
6. Select the **PRIVATE CONNECTIONS TO SERVICES** tab.
7. Click **CREATE CONNECTION** and enter the following values:
  1. **Connected service producer**: Select **Google Cloud Platform**.
  2. **Assigned allocation**: Select the IP Range created in the previous step.
  3. Click **OK**.
8. Click **CONNECT**. See image.

After the private service access is configured, Google adds peering from the worker plane VPC to servicenetworking.

[Image: Create a private connection page with  the required values to configure.]

[Image: Allocate an internal IP range page with the required values to configure.]

[Image: Private Services Access page to setup private service access for worker plane.]

After creating the worker plane VPC network, edit the created VPC to configure the firewall rules.

- To add a rule to deny outbound communication to the orchestrator:
  1. Go to the **VPC networks** page, and select the created worker plane VPC network.
  2. Select the **Firewalls** tab, and click **Add Firewall Rule**. The **Create a firewall rule** window appears.
  3. In the **Create a firewall rule** window, provide the following values in the respective fields to deny all outbound communication to the orchestrator: See image.
    1. **Name**: Enter `deny-all-outbound-rule`.
    2. **Priority**: Enter `1000`.
    3. **Direction**: Select **Egress**.
    4. **Action on match**: Select **Deny**.
    5. **Targets**: Select **All Instances in the network**.
    6. **Destination filter**: Select **IPv4 ranges**.
    7. **Destination IPv4 ranges**: Enter `0.0.0.0/0`.
  4. Click **Create** to save the rule.
- To add a rule to allow inbound communication from the orchestrator to the scanner VPC:
  1. Go to the **VPC networks** page, and select the created control plane VPC network.
  2. Select the **Firewalls** tab, and click **Add Firewall Rule**. The **Create a firewall rule** window appears.
  3. In the **Create a firewall rule** window, provide the following values in the respective fields to deny all outbound communication to the orchestrator: See image.
    1. **Name**: Enter `allow-orchestrator-outbound-rule`.
    2. **Priority**: Enter `0`.
    3. **Direction**: Select **Ingress**.
    4. **Action on match**: Select **Allow**.
    5. **Targets**: Select **All Instances in the network**.
    6. **Destination filter**: Select **IPv4 ranges**.
    7. **Destination IPv4 ranges**: Enter `0.0.0.0/0`.
    8. **Protocols and ports**: Select **Specified protocols and ports**.
      1. **TCP**: Select the checkbox.
      2. **Ports**: Enter `443`.
  4. Click **Create** to save the rule.
- To add a rule to allow outbound communication from the scanner to AI Security:
  1. Go to the **VPC networks** page, and select the created control plane VPC network.
  2. Select the **Firewalls** tab, and click **Add Firewall Rule**. The **Create a firewall rule** window appears.
  3. In the **Create a firewall rule** window, provide the following values in the respective fields to deny all outbound communication to the orchestrator: See image.
    1. **Name**: Enter `allow-https-outbound-rule`.
    2. **Priority**: Enter `1`.
    3. **Direction**: Select **Egress**.
    4. **Action on match**: Select **Allow**.
    5. **Targets**: Select **All Instances in the network**.
    6. **Destination filter**: Select **IPv4 ranges**.
    7. **Destination IPv4 ranges**: Enter `0.0.0.0/0`.
    8. **Protocols and ports**: Select **Specified protocols and ports**.
      1. **TCP**: Select the checkbox.
      2. **Ports**: Enter `443`.
  4. Click **Create** to save the rule.
- To add a rule to allow outbound communication from the scanner to GCP Cloud SQL instances: The worker plane firewall rules are configured.
  1. Go to the **VPC networks** page, and select the created control plane VPC network.
  2. Select the **Firewalls** tab, and click **Add Firewall Rule**. The **Create a firewall rule** window appears.
  3. In the **Create a firewall rule** window, provide the following values in the respective fields to deny all outbound communication to the orchestrator: See image.
    1. **Name**: Enter `allow-db-outbound-rule`.
    2. **Priority**: Enter `2`.
    3. **Direction**: Select **Egress**.
    4. **Action on match**: Select **Allow**.
    5. **Targets**: Select **All Instances in the network**.
    6. **Destination filter**: Select **IPv4 ranges**.
    7. **Destination IPv4 ranges**: Enter `0.0.0.0/0`.
    8. **Protocols and ports**: Select **Specified protocols and ports**.
      1. **TCP**: Select the checkbox.
      2. **Ports**: Enter `3306, 5432, 1433`.
  4. Click **Create** to save the rule.

[Image: Create a worker plane firewall rule with the values provided to allow outbound communication from the scanner to GCP Cloud SQL Instances.]

[Image: Create a worker plane firewall rule with the values provided to allow outbound communication from the scanner to DSPM.]

[Image: Create a worker plane firewall rule with the values provided to allow inbound communication from the orchestrator to scanner vpc.]

[Image: Create a worker plane firewall rule with the values provided to deny all outbound communication]

2. On the **Create a VPC network** page: See image.
  1. **Name**: Enter a name for the VPC network.
  2. **Subnet creation mode**. Select **Custom**.
  3. **Subnets**: Click **ADD SUBNET** and provide a name for the subnet. To add multiple subnets in different regions, click **ADD SUBNET** and repeat these steps for each additional subnet as required.

The VPC and subnet for the worker plane are created.

After creating the worker plane VPC, create and configure the Cloud NAT gateway resources for the new subnet and region in the worker plane.

    1. **Name**: Enter `deny-all-outbound-rule`.

  4. Click **Create** to save the rule.

  4. Click **Create** to save the rule.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-aws-cloud-storage","lastmod":"2026-06-05T21:06Z","nid":"1540274"} -->
## Configuring Scan Rule for AWS Cloud Storage

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-aws-cloud-storage
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Scan Rules for AWS > Configuring Scan Rule for AWS Cloud Storage
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to configure the scan rule for AWS cloud storage resources in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can configure the scan rule to scan Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud storage resources such as S3 buckets. AI Security scans the S3 buckets for any sensitive data.

- You can configure the scan rule after onboarding the AWS accounts. To learn more, see [About Cloud Accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts).
- AI Security automatically excludes the active [CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-aws-cloudtrail)and VPC flow log buckets from sensitive data scans even if they match the scan criteria.
- AI Security also excludes AWS workloads that were created using the AWS Marketplace from scanning.

To configure a scan rule for AWS cloud storages, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

- 1. Provide the general information.
- 2. Select the cloud and resource type.
- 3. Select the accounts that must be scanned.
- 4. Exclude S3 buckets and prefixes (Optional).
- 5. Select the scan type.
- 6. Select the scan scope.
- 7. Review and complete the configuration.

1. Go to **Administration** > **Scan Settings**.
2. Select the **Scan Rules**tab. If you are configuring the scan rule for the first time, the following page appears: See image.
3. Click **Add Scan Rule**. See image. The **General Information** page appears.
4. On the **General Information**page: See image.
  1. **Scan Rule Name**: Enter a unique and descriptive name for the scan rule.
  2. **Scan Rule Description (Optional)**: Enter a description for the scan rule (maximum is 500 characters).
5. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Select Cloud and Resource Type** page:
  - For **Cloud Type**, select **AWS**.
  - For **Resource Type**, select **Cloud Storage**.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Select Resources to Scan** page, choose one of the following options:
  - **Scan All Resources**: Scan all the cloud storage resources across all onboarded accounts. See image.
  - **Scan Specific Resources**: Select the checkbox for the specific accounts and regions that must be scanned. See image.
    1. **Select Specific Accounts and Regions**: Select the checkbox for specific accounts and regions that must be scanned. See image.
    2. **Scan S3 Buckets**: Specify the S3 buckets that must be scanned. You can either select the names from the list or specify the tags.
      - **Select from the List**: Select the checkbox for the S3 buckets that must be scanned. If you choose **Manual**, then you need to enter the names.
      - **Select by Tag**: Specify the tags in key-value pairs. All the S3 buckets that match the tag are scanned. Click **Add More** to add multiple key-value pairs. If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security scans all buckets that match at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses `OR` logic, and a bucket is included if it matches any of the key-value pairs.
2. **Enable Malware Scanning**: Enable this option if the resources must be scanned for malware. This option is disabled by default. See image.
3. Click **Next**.

On the **Exclude S3 Buckets and Prefixes (Optional)** page, you can specify the S3 buckets and prefixes that must be excluded from the scan.

If a full scan is already initiated or completed, the bucket or folder is excluded in the next incremental scan.

1. Enter the name of the bucket, or include the folder name followed by a forward slash (/). For example, to exclude a folder named `reports` within a bucket named `my-bucket`, enter `my-bucket/reports/`. Additionally, you can use wildcards with the S3 bucket names instead of relying on tags. Based on the wildcard, DSPM excludes all the matching S3 buckets from scanning. This is applicable to both existing S3 buckets and the ones that might be added in the future.
2. **Exclude S3 Buckets By Tags**: Select the checkbox and enter the key-value pairs of the S3 buckets that must be excluded from scanning. This option is disabled by default. Click **Add More** to add multiple key-value pairs. If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security excludes any bucket that matches at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses `OR` logic, and a bucket is excluded if it matches any of the key-value pairs.
3. **Exclude S3 Bucket Names Using Wildcards**: Select the checkbox and enter the wildcard expressions to exclude buckets by name using wildcards. For example, `*logs*` — excludes any bucket name that contains the word `logs`. See image.
4. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Scan Type** page, choose one of the following options: AI Security cannot detect files that are deleted in the AWS console. See image.
  - **Full Scan**: Scans all objects in the S3 buckets.
  - **Full + Incremental Scan**: Scans all objects, including those that are newly added or modified since the previous scan.
    - Select one of the scan durations: **1 Day**, **1 Week**, **1 Month**, **Continuous**, **Custom Duration**. If you select **Custom Duration**, enter the number of days to define the scan window.
  - **Incremental Scan**: Scans only the files that are newly added or modified since the previous scan.
    - Select one of the scan durations: **1 Day**, **1 Week**, **1 Month**, **Continuous**, **Custom Duration**. If you select **Custom Duration**, enter the number of days to define the scan window.
  - **Historical Scan**: Scans files based on a specified look back period.
    - **Lookback Period**: Enter the number of days (1 to 365 days) to scan historical data.
  - **Historical + Incremental Scan**: Scans files based on a specified lookback period and scan files that are newly added or modified since the previous scan.
    - **Lookback Period**: Enter the number of days (1 to 365 days) to scan historical data.
    - **Duration**: Specify the number of days for incremental scanning.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the**Scan Scope**page, choose a scan scope from the drop-down menu to set up your scan rule. To learn more about configuring and creating a scan scope, see [Configuring Scan Scope](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-scope). See image.
2. Click **Next**.

[Image: The Scan Scope page with dropdown menu for selecting scan scope.]

1. Review the scan rule. Click the **Edit** icon to change any values, if required. See image.
2. Click **Finish**.

## Configuring Scan Rule for AWS ECR Repositories

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-aws-ecr-repositories
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Scan Rules for AWS > Configuring Scan Rule for AWS ECR Repositories
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to configure the scan rule for AWS ECR container image repositories in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can configure the scan rule to discover vulnerabilities and software packages within your container images stored in AWS Elastic Container Registry (ECR). AI Security scans the ECR for any sensitive data.

Before you configure a scan rule, ensure you have updated your AWS onboarding templates to include the necessary IAM permissions for ECR scanning. To learn more, see [IAM Roles and Permissions for AWS](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/iam-roles-and-permissions-aws).

To configure a scan rule for AWS ECR container image repositories, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

- 1. Provide the general information.
- 2. Select the cloud and resource type.
- 3. Select the accounts that must be scanned.
- 4. Exclude ECR repositories (Optional).
- 5. Set up the scan schedule.
- 6. Review and complete the configuration.

1. Go to **Administration** > **Scan Settings**.
2. Select the **Scan Rules**tab. If you are configuring the scan rule for the first time, the following page appears: See image.
3. Click **Add Scan Rule**. See image. The **General Information** page appears.
4. On the **General Information**page: See image.
  1. **Scan Rule Name**: Enter a unique and descriptive name for the scan rule.
  2. **Scan Rule Description (Optional)**: Enter a description for the scan rule (maximum is 500 characters).
5. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Select Cloud and Resource Type** page:
  - For **Cloud Type**, select **AWS**.
  - For **Resource Type**, select **Container Image Repositories**.
2. Click **Next**.

[Image: The initial scan rule configuration page with no scan rule configured and + Add Scan Rule button.]

[Image: The Scan Settings page with an annotation around the Add New button.]

[Image: General Information page to set the scan rule name and an optional description field.]

1. On the **Select the Resources to Scan** page, choose one of the following options: If you chose **Scan All Resources**, or**Scan Specific Resources**, you can optionally exclude specific ECR repositories from the scan.
  - **Scan All Resources**: Scans all discovered ECR repositories across all onboarded accounts. See image.
  - **Scan Specific Resources**: Scan only specific resources. When you select this option, select the checkbox for the repositories that must be scanned. See image.
    1. **Select Specific Accounts and Regions**: Select the checkbox for specific accounts and regions that must be scanned.
    2. **Scan Specific Repositories**: Specify the ECR repositories that must be scanned. You can either select the names from the list or specify the tags.
      - **Select from the Lis**t: Select the checkbox for the ECR repositories that must be scanned. If you choose **Manual**, then you need to enter the names.
      - **Select by Tags**: Specify the tags in key-value pairs. All the ECR repositories that match the tag are scanned. Click **Add More** to add multiple key-value pairs. If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security scans all accounts that match at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses `OR` logic, and a account is included if it matches any of the key-value pairs.
2. In the **Scan by Last Pulled** option, select a timeframe to only scan images that have been pulled within that period.

On the **Exclude ECR Repositories (Optional)** page, you can specify the ECR repositories that must be excluded from the scan.

If a full scan is already initiated or completed, the ECR repositories are excluded in the next incremental scan.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-azure-acr-repositories","lastmod":"2026-08-11T07:06Z","nid":"1541564"} -->
## Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Container Registry (ACR) Repositories

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-azure-acr-repositories
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Scan Rules for Azure > Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Container Registry (ACR) Repositories
- Last modified: 2026-08-11T07:06Z
- Summary: How to configure the scan rule for Azure ECR container image repositories in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can configure the scan rule to discover vulnerabilities and software packages within your container images stored in Azure Container Registry (ACR). AI Security detects vulnerabilities, AI Models, AI Packages, and MCP servers.

Before you configure a scan rule, ensure you have enabled the Azure Container Registry service within the product's **Manage Services** settings. This tells the system that you want it to discover and scan container registries in your Azure environment. To learn more, see [Managing Services](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-services). You must also ensure you have executed the latest Azure onboarding templates that include the necessary IAM permissions for ACR scanning. To learn more, see [IAM Roles and Permissions for Azure](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/iam-roles-and-permissions-microsoft-azure).

To enable scanning of a private Azure Container Registry (ACR) from a scanner instance, two network-level configurations are required:

- VNet Peering (Bidirectional): The customer must establish a VNet peering between the scanner VNet and the VNet where the private ACR is deployed. Without peering, scanner traffic cannot reach the address space where the ACR private endpoint lives.
- Private DNS Zone VNet Link: The customer must link the scanner VNet to the Private DNS Zone where the ACR private endpoint DNS records are registered— this ensures the scanner can resolve the ACR hostname to its private IP.

If the ACR has IP network rules configured, the scanner's outbound IPs must be explicitly whitelisted.

To configure a scan rule for ACR container image repositories, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

- 1. Provide the general information.
- 2. Select the cloud and resource type.
- 3. Select the subscriptions that must be scanned.
- 4. Exclude ACR repositories (Optional).
- 5. Set up the scan schedule.
- 6. Review and complete the configuration.

1. Go to **Administration** > **Scan Settings**.
2. Select the **Scan Rules**tab.
3. Click **Add Scan Rule**. See image. The **General Information** page appears.
4. On the **General Information**page: See image.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-azure-blob-storage","lastmod":"2026-06-05T21:06Z","nid":"1540301"} -->
## Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Blob Storage

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-azure-blob-storage
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Scan Rules for Azure > Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Blob Storage
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to configure the scan rule for Azure Blob Containers in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can configure the scan rule to scan Azure blob storage resources. AI Security scans the blob containers for any sensitive data.

You can configure the scan rule after onboarding the Azure accounts. To learn more, see [About Cloud Accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts).

To configure a scan rule for Azure blob storage, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

- 1. Provide the general information.
- 2. Select the cloud and resource type.
- 3. Select the accounts that must be scanned.
- 4. Exclude storage account containers and prefixes (Optional).
- 5. Select the scan type.
- 6. Select the scan scope.
- 7. Review and complete the configuration.

Enable the scan rule on the [Scan Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings) page to initiate scheduled or on-demand scans.

1. Go to **Administration** > **Scan Settings**.
2. Select the **Scan Rules**tab. If you are configuring the scan rule for the first time, the following page appears: See image.
3. Click **Add Scan Rule**. See image. The **General Information** page appears.
4. On the **General Information**page: See image.
  1. **Scan Rule Name**: Enter a unique and descriptive name for the scan rule.
  2. **Scan Rule Description (Optional)**: Enter a description for the scan rule (maximum is 500 characters).
5. Click **Next**.

[Image: The initial scan rule configuration page with no scan rule configured and + Add Scan Rule button.]

[Image: General Information page to set the scan rule name and an optional description field.]

1. On the **Select Cloud and Resource Type** page:
  - For **Cloud Type**, select **Azure**.
  - For **Resource Category**, select **Cloud Storage**.
  - For **Resource Type**, select **Blob Containers**.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Select Resources to Scan** page, choose one of the following options: If you select any of the above options, you can optionally exclude specific databases from the scan.
  - **Scan All Resources**: Scans all the subscriptions or storage accounts. See image.
  - **Scan Specific Resources**: Scan only specific resources. When you select this option, select the checkbox for the resources that must be scanned. See image.
    1. **Select Specific Subscriptions and Regions**: Select the checkbox for specific subscriptions and regions that must be scanned.
    2. **Scan Specific Storage Account**: Specify the storage accounts that must be scanned.
      - **Select from the List**: Select the checkbox for the accounts or subscriptions that must be scanned from the list.
      - **Select by Tags**: Enter the key-value pairs for the accounts or subscriptions. Click **Add More** to add multiple key-value pairs. If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security scans all accounts or subscriptions that match at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses `OR` logic, and a account or subscription is included, if it matches any of the key-value pairs.
    3. **Scan Blob Containers**: Select the checkbox for the blob containers that must be scanned from the list. If you choose **Manual**, enter the blob container names and prefixes separated by commas.
2. **Enable Malware Scanning**: Enable this option if the resources must be scanned for malware. This option is disabled by default. See image.
3. Click **Next**.

On the **Exclude Storage Account Containers and Prefixes (Optional)** page, you can specify the storage account containers and prefixes that must be excluded from the scan.

If a full scan is already initiated or completed, the bucket or folder is excluded in the next incremental scan.

1. Enter the name of the blob containers, or include the folder name followed by a forward slash (/). For example, to exclude a folder named `myblobcontainer` within the storage account `https://storagename.blob.core.windows.net/`, enter `https://storagename.blob.core.windows.net/myblobcontainer`. Additionally, you can use wildcards with the storage account names instead of relying on tags. Based on the wildcard, DSPM excludes all the matching storage account containers from scanning. This is applicable to both existing storage accounts and the ones that might be added in the future.
2. **Exclude Subscriptions & Storage Accounts By Tags**: Enable this option and enter the key-value pairs of the subscriptions or storage accounts that must be excluded from scanning. This option is disabled by default. Click **Add More** to add multiple key-value pairs. If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security excludes any accounts or subscriptions that matches at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses `OR` logic, and an account or subscription is excluded, if it matches any of the key-value pairs.
3. **Exclude Azure Blob Containers with Wildcards**: Select the checkbox and enter the wildcard expressions to exclude blob containers by name using wildcards. For example, `*logs*` excludes any blob name that contains the word `logs`. See image.
4. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Scan Type** page choose one of the following options: AI Security cannot detect files that are deleted in Azure. See image.
  1. **Full Scan**: Scans all objects on the on-premises file server.
  2. **Full + Incremental Scan**: Scans all objects, including those that are newly added or modified since the previous scan.
    1. Select one of the scan durations: **1 Day**, **1 Week**, **1 Month**, **Continuous**, **Custom Duration**. If you select **Custom Duration**, enter the number of days to define the scan window.
  3. **Incremental Scan**: Scans only those files that are newly added or modified since the previous scan.
    1. Select one of the scan durations: **1 Day**, **1 Week**, **1 Month**, **Continuous**, **Custom Duration**. If you select **Custom Duration**, enter the number of days to define the scan window.
  4. **Historical Scan**: Scans files based on a specified look back period.
    1. **Lookback Period**: Enter the number of days (1 to 365 days) to scan historical data.
  5. **Historical + Incremental Scan**: Scans files based on a specified lookback period and scan files that are newly added or modified since the previous scan.
    1. **Lookback Period**: Enter the number of days (1 to 365 days) to scan historical data.
    2. **Duration**: Specify the number of days for incremental scanning.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Scan Scope** page, choose a scan scope from the drop-down menu to set up your scan rule. To learn more about configuring and creating a scan scope, see [Configuring Scan Scope](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-scope). See image.
2. Click **Next**.

[Image: The Scan Scope page with drop-down menu for selecting scan scope.]

1. Review the scan rule. Click the **Edit** icon to change any values, if required. See image.
2. Click **Finish**.

[Image: The Scan Settings page with an annotation around the Add New button.]

[Image: The Select Resources to Scan page with Scan All Subscriptions & Storage Accounts option is selected.]

[Image: The Select Resources to Scan page with Scan Specific Subscription & Storage option selected.]

[Image: Exclude storage account containers from scanning]

[Image: Enable malware scanning option is enabled with the toggle button.]

[Image: The scan type selection page with the available options.]

[Image: The scan settings review page displays the configured scan settings before completing the scan configuration.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Configuring Scan Rule for Azure-Managed Databases

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-azure-managed-databases
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Scan Rules for Azure > Configuring Scan Rule for Azure-Managed Databases
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to configure the scan rule for Azure databases in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can configure the scan rule to scan Azure SQL databases and Azure-Managed PostgreSQL Flexible servers. AI Security scans the databases for any sensitive data and vulnerabilities.

Before configuring the scan, ensure your Azure SQL database has a Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) policy for the Key Vault.
AI Security does not provide support for scanning Azure SQL databases that are encrypted with a Customer-Managed Key (CMK) without the RBAC policy.

You can configure the scan rules after onboarding the Azure accounts. To learn more, see [About Cloud Accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts).

To configure a scan rule for Azure-managed databases, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

- 1. Provide the general information.
- 2. Select the cloud and resource type.
- 3. Select the accounts that must be scanned.
- 4. Exclude database servers (Optional).
- 5. Select the scan type.
- 6. Set up the scan schedule.
- 7. Select the scan scope.
- 8. Review and complete the configuration.

After completing the scan, AI Security deletes the restored servers, databases, and File System (FS) Analyzer to reduce the cost for customers.

1. Go to **Administration** > **Scan Settings**.
2. Select the **Scan Rules**tab. If you are configuring the scan rule for the first time, the following page appears: See image.
3. Click **Add Scan Rule**. See image. The **General Information** page appears.
4. On the **General Information**page: See image.
  1. **Scan Rule Name**: Enter a unique and descriptive name for the scan rule.
  2. **Scan Rule Description (Optional)**: Enter a description for the scan rule (maximum is 500 characters).
5. Click **Next**.

[Image: The initial scan rule configuration page with no scan rule configured and + Add Scan Rule button.]

[Image: General Information page to set the scan rule name and an optional description field.]

1. On the **Select Cloud and Resource Type** page:
  - For **Cloud Type**, select **Azure**.
  - For **Resource Category**, select **Database**.
  - For **Resource Type**, select **Managed Database**.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Select Resources to Scan** page, choose one of the following options: You can optionally exclude specific databases from the scan.
  - **Scan All Resources**: Scan all the supported database resources across all onboarded accounts. See image.
  - **Scan Specific Resources**: Select the checkbox for the specific resources that must be scanned.
    1. **Select Specific Subscriptions and Regions**: Select the checkbox for specific subscriptions and regions that must be scanned.
    2. **Scan Specific Database Servers**: Specify the databases that must be scanned. When you select this option, select the checkbox for the account that must be excluded from the scan. See image.
      - **Select from the List**: Select the checkbox for the instances that must be scanned from the list. If you choose **Manual**, enter the database names separated by commas.
      - **Select by Tags**: Enter the key-value pairs for the database servers. All the database servers that match the tag are scanned. Click **Add More** to add multiple key-value pairs. If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security scans all databases that match at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses `OR` logic, and a database is included if it matches any of the key-value pairs.
2. Click **Next**.

On the **Exclude Database Servers (Optional)** page, you can specify the database servers that must be excluded from the scan.

If a full scan is already initiated or completed, the databases are excluded in the next incremental scan.

1. Enter the database server names separated by commas.
2. **Exclude Database Servers By Tags**: Enable this option and enter the key-value pairs of the database servers that must be excluded from scanning. This option is disabled by default. Click **Add More** to add multiple key-value pairs. If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security excludes any database that matches at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses `OR` logic, and a database is excluded if it matches any of the key-value pairs. See image.
3. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Scan Type** page, you can choose to perform one of the following scans: AI Security cannot detect files that are deleted in the AWS console. See image.
  - **Data Sampling Scan**: Scan a sample of recent data in the database.
  - **Full Scan**: A complete scan of all databases across all onboarded accounts.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Scan Schedule** page, select the scan frequency: See image.
  - **On Demand**(Default): Scan the data manually when needed.
  - **Daily**: Scan the data daily.
  - **Weekly**: Scan the data once a week. Select the day from the drop-down menu.
  - **Monthly**: Scan the data once a month.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Scan Scope** page, choose a scan scope from the drop-down menu to set up your scan rule. To learn more about configuring and creating a scan scope, see [Configuring Scan Scope](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-scope). See image.
2. Click **Next**.

[Image: The scan type selection page with data sampling scan, and full scan options.]

[Image: The Scan Scope page with dropdown menu for selecting scan scope.]

1. Review the scan rule. Click the **Edit** icon to change any values, if needed. See image.
2. Click **Finish**.

[Image: The Scan Settings page with an annotation around the Add New button.]

[Image: The Select Resources to Scan page with Scan All Subscriptions option is selected.]

[Image: The Select Resources to Scan page with Scan specific instances option selected, showing the fields to enter key-value pair.]

[Image: The Database Servers screen to exclude resources from scanning.]

## Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Virtual Machines

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-azure-virtual-machines
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Scan Rules for Azure > Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Virtual Machines
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to configure the scan rule for Azure virtual machines in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can configure the scan rule to scan virtual machines (VMs) in your Azure cloud accounts. AI Security scans the databases for any sensitive data and vulnerabilities.

You can configure the scan rule after onboarding the Azure accounts. To learn more, see [About Cloud Accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts).

The following systems are excluded from scanning:

- VMs encrypted using ADE.
- Windows desktop VMs running with Windows version 10 or 11.
- Windows Server 2012 VMs.
- Azure VMs created using unmanaged disks (`.vhd` from storage account).
- Storage accounts with public network access disabled.

To configure a scan rule for Azure virtual machines, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

- 1. Provide the general information.
- 2. Select the cloud and resource type.
- 3. Select the accounts that must be scanned.
- 4. Exclude virtual machines (Optional).
- 5. Set up the scan schedule.
- 6. Select the scan scope.
- 7. Review and complete the configuration.

1. Go to **Administration** > **Scan Settings**.
2. Select the **Scan Rules**tab. If you are configuring the scan rule for the first time, the following page appears: See image.
3. Click **Add Scan Rule**. See image. The **General Information** page appears.
4. On the **General Information**page: See image.
  1. **Scan Rule Name**: Enter a unique and descriptive name for the scan rule.
  2. **Scan Rule Description (Optional)**: Enter a description for the scan rule (maximum is 500 characters).
5. Click **Next**.

[Image: The initial scan rule configuration page with no scan rule configured and + Add Scan Rule button.]

[Image: General Information page to set the scan rule name and an optional description field.]

1. On the **Select Cloud and Resource Type** page:
  - For **Cloud Type**: Select **Azure**.
  - For **Resource Type**: Select **Virtual Machine**.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Select Resources to Scan** page, select one of the following options: You can optionally exclude some VMs from the scan.
  - **Scan All Resources**: Scans all the virtual machines across all the onboarded Azure accounts. See image.
  - **Scan Specific Resources:**Scan only specific subscriptions. When you select this option, select the checkbox for the subscriptions that must be scanned. See image.
    1. **Select Specific Subscriptions and Regions**: Scan only specific subscriptions. When you select this option, select the checkbox for the subscriptions that must be scanned.
    2. **Scan Specific Instances**: Specify the virtual machines that must be scanned.
      - **Select from the List**: Select the checkbox for the virtual machines that must be scanned from the list. If you choose **Manual**, enter the instance IDs separated by commas.
      - **Select by Tags**: Enter the key-value pairs for the instances. All the instances that match the tag are scanned. Click **Add More** to add multiple key-value pairs. If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security scans all instances that match at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses `OR` logic, and a instance is included if it matches any of the key-value pairs.
2. **Enable Malware Scanning**: Enable this option if the resources must be scanned for malware. This option is disabled by default. See image.
3. Click **Next**.

On the **Exclude Virtual Machines (Optional)** page, you can specify the VMs that must be excluded from the scan.

1. Enter the instance IDs separated by commas.
2. **Exclude Virtual Machines By Tags**: Enable this option and enter the key-value pairs of the VMs that must be excluded from scanning. This option is disabled by default. Click **Add More** to add multiple key-value pairs. If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security excludes any VMs that matches at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses `OR` logic, and a VM is excluded if it matches any of the key-value pairs.
3. **Exclude Operating System Directories Files from Scanning**: Disable this option if you want to scan the OS directories. This option is enabled by default. The following directories are excluded from the scan: See image.
  - Linux
  - Windows
  - Packages
4. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Scan Schedule** page, select the scan frequency: See image.
  - **On Demand**(Default): Scan the data manually when needed.
  - **Daily**: Scan the data daily.
  - **Weekly**: Scan the data once a week. Select the day from the drop-down menu.
  - **Monthly**: Scan the data once a month.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Scan Scope** page, choose a scan scope from the drop-down menu to set up your scan rule. To learn more about configuring and creating a scan scope, see [Configuring Scan Scope](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-scope). See image.
2. Click **Next**.

2. Click **Finish**.

## Configuring Scan Rule for GitHub

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-rule-github
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Scan Rules for SaaS > Configuring Scan Rule for GitHub
- Last modified: 2026-08-29T07:06Z
- Summary: How to configure the scan rule for GitHub resources in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can configure the scan rule to scan GitHub resources and repositories after onboarding the GitHub repositories. To learn more, see [Onboarding GitHub Tenant](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-github-tenant).

To configure a scan rule for GitHub repositories, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

- 1. Provide the general information.
- 2. Select the cloud and resource type.
- 3. Select the repositories that must be scanned.
- 4. Exclude repositories
- 5. Select the scan type.
- 6. Select the scan schedule.
- 7. Review and complete the configuration.

The scan rule must be enabled on the Overview page to initiate the scan.

1. Go to **Administration** > **Scan Settings**.
2. Select the **Scan Rules**tab.
3. Click **Add Scan Rule**. See image. The **General Information** page appears.
4. On the **General Information**page: See image.
  1. **Scan Rule Name**: Enter a unique and descriptive name for the scan rule.
  2. **Scan Rule Description (Optional)**: Enter a description for the scan rule (maximum is 500 characters).
5. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Select Cloud and Resource Type** page: See image.
  - For **Cloud Type**, select **SaaS**.
  - For **Service Type**, select **GitHub**.
2. Click **Next**.

1. On the **Select Repositories** page, select the repositories from GitHub that you want to include in the scan rule. See image.
2. Click **Next**.

On the **Exclusions** page, you can specify the paths in the repositories that must be excluded from the scan.

Define the path exclusion rules per repository.

1. Select the repositories you would like to set an exclusion for the scan rule.
2. Set rules: To set the rules, do the following:
  - **Path field**: Enter the file path or pattern you want to exclude. For example, src/**/*.ts excludes all TypeScript files inside the src folder and its subfolders.
  - **Regex toggle (</> Regex):** Switch to Regex mode if you need more advanced pattern matching instead of glob patterns.
3. Click **Add** to add the entered path rule to the exclusion list. See image.
4. Click **Next**.

On the **Scan Type** page, choose how scans are triggered and what type of scan to run.

1. Select **Scheduled Full Scan**to run a complete scan of all files across every selected repository on a recurring schedule is performed. If you do not select this option, recurring scans are not scheduled for the selected repositories, and you are taken directly to the Review page. See image.
2. Click **Next**.

On the **Scan Schedule** page, choose one of the following options:

- **Daily:** To scan the data every day.
- **Weekly:** To scan the data every week.
- **Monthly:** To scan the data once a month.
- **On Demand:**To scan the data on demand.

See image.

1. Review the scan rule. Click the **Edit** icon to change any values, if required. See image.
2. Click **Finish**.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-scope","lastmod":"2026-06-05T21:06Z","nid":"1540704"} -->
## Configuring Scan Scope

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/configuring-scan-scope
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Managing Scan Scope > Configuring Scan Scope
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to configure the scan scope for NoSQL Datastores in AI Security Admin Portal.

Scan scope allows you to select specific DLP engines that must be used to detect and classify sensitive data in specific file types. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is used to scan and identify sensitive data in image files and also images embedded within files. AI Security uses only the specified DLP engines to scan the resources for sensitive data. AI Security

## Creating Scan Scope

To create a new scan scope, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

1. Go to **Administration**> **Scan Settings**.
2. Select the **Scan Scope** tab.
3. On the [Scan Scope](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings#scan_scope) page, click **Create Scan Scope**.
4. On the **General Information** page: See image.
  - **Engine Scope Name**: Enter a descriptive name for your scan scope.
  - **Engine Scope Description**: Provide a detailed explanation of what the scan scope covers.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Select Criteria** page: See image.
  - **DLP Engine**: Choose DLP engines for the scan scope. Choose all for a comprehensive scan or specific DLP engines to focus on specific DLP engines.
  - **Specific DLP Engines**: Choose the DLP engines that must be included in the scan scope. This option is enabled only if you select specific DLP engines to scan. To learn more, see [About Data Classification Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-data-sensitivity). A DLP engine must be enabled so you can select it while configuring the scan scope. A DLP engine that is not enabled appears grayed out and cannot be selected.; If you disable a DLP engine that is currently selected in a scan scope, it is displayed as grayed out with a partial selection indicator. The scanner does not evaluate this DLP engine, even if it is still partially selected.; When a DLP engine is deleted, it is automatically removed from all existing scan scopes.
  - **File Type**: Choose the file types that must be included in the scan scope.
  - AI Security uses OCR to scan and identify sensitive data in image files (e.g., `.png`, `.jpeg`, `.tiff`, `.bmp`, `.gif`) and also images that are embedded within documents (e.g., `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.pptx`).
  - **Machine Learning Document Scan**: Enable if you want to use machine learning-powered document scanning. File type filters and machine learning document scans are optimized for cloud storage and VM resources.
7. Click **Next**.
8. On the **Summary** page, review the configured details. Click the **Edit** icon to modify the scan scope, if required. To learn more, see [Editing or Deleting Scan Scopes](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/editing-or-deleting-scan-scopes). See image.
9. Click **Finish**.

You can apply the scan scope while configuring the scan settings.

[Image: Scan Scope Summary]
