## IAM Roles and Permissions for GCP

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/iam-roles-and-permissions-gcp
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > GCP Cloud Accounts > IAM Roles and Permissions for GCP
- Last modified: 2026-08-06T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about the roles created and permissions assigned while onboarding GCP organizations.

As part of the onboarding process, you need to deploy AI Security templates in the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project. These templates create service accounts and access management (IAM) roles that AI Security requires to connect to the GCP project, discover the resources, and scan data. Each role has permissions for various services and actions, such as resource discovery, data scanning, etc.

## IAM Roles

AI Security creates the following IAM roles and service accounts to access the GCP projects:

- Discovery Service Account
- Orchestrator Service Account
- Scanner Service Account
- Target Role

The service account with this role is used to perform scan-related tasks on data stores. The service account is assigned the following Managed Roles and associated permissions:

- Storage Object Viewer
- Cloud KMS CryptoKey Encrypter or Decrypter
- Service Usage Consumer

| Permission | Scope | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `storage.managedFolders.list` | Monitored Projects | To get managed folders of buckets |
| `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` | Monitored Projects | To decrypt resources for scanning |
| `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt` | Monitored Projects | To encrypt resources for scanning |
| `cloudsql.backupRuns.create` | Monitored Projects | To create latest cloud SQL backup |
| `cloudsql.backupRuns.delete` | Monitored Projects | To delete cloud SQL backups |
| `cloudsql.backupRuns.get` | Monitored Projects | To get latest cloud SQL backup |
| `cloudsql.backupRuns.list` | Monitored Projects | To list latest cloud SQL backups |
| `cloudsql.instances.get` | Monitored Projects | To get cloud SQL instances |

The following permissions are required to scan GCP BigQuery projects:

| Permission | Scope | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bigquery.datasets.get | Monitored Projects | To read the metadata of BigQuery datasets |
| bigquery.datasets.getIamPolicy | Monitored Projects | To check the access permissions configured for datasets |
| bigquery.jobs.create | Monitored Projects | To run BigQuery jobs |
| bigquery.models.getData | Monitored Projects | To read data from BigQuery ML models for scanning |
| bigquery.models.getMetadata | Monitored Projects | To read metadata of BigQuery ML models |
| bigquery.models.list | Monitored Projects | To list BigQuery ML models in a dataset |
| bigquery.routines.get | Monitored Projects | To read the routine definitions |
| bigquery.routines.list | Monitored Projects | To list routines in a dataset |
| bigquery.tables.get | Monitored Projects | To read the metadata and schema of BigQuery tables |
| bigquery.tables.getData | Monitored Projects | To read the contents of BigQuery tables for scanning |
| bigquery.tables.getIamPolicy | Monitored Projects | To check the access permissions configured for tables |
| bigquery.tables.list | Monitored Projects | To list tables within a BigQuery dataset |

This service account is used by the scanner instance to perform scan-related tasks. The service account is assigned the following Managed Roles, which provide the necessary permissions:

- Storage Object Viewer
- Cloud KMS CryptoKey Encrypter or Decrypter
- Viewer
- Logs View Accessor
- Service Usage Consumer
- Service Account User
- Service Account Token Creator

| Permission | Scope | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `logging.logEntries.list` | Monitored Projects | To list log entries from log views |
| `secretmanager.versions.access` | Monitored Projects | To access Zscaler AI Security secret version |

This service account is used by the orchestrator instance to perform scan and management operations. The service account is assigned the following Managed Roles, which provide the necessary permissions:

- Viewer
- Service Usage Consumer
- Service Account User
- Cloud KMS CryptoKey Encrypter or Decrypter
- Service Account Token Creator

| Permission | Scope | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `compute.disks.use` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security scanner instance disk |
| `compute.instances.attachDisk` | Orchestrator Project | To attach Zscaler AI Security scanner instance disk |
| `compute.instances.detachDisk` | Orchestrator Project | To detach Zscaler AI Security scanner instance disk |
| `compute.instances.delete` | Orchestrator Project | To delete Zscaler AI Security scanner instance |
| `compute.instanceGroups.update` | Orchestrator Project | To update Zscaler AI Security instance group manager |
| `compute.autoscalers.update` | Orchestrator Project | To update Zscaler AI Security instance group manager |
| `secretmanager.versions.access` | Orchestrator Project | To access Zscaler AI Security secret version |
| `compute.subnetworks.use` | Orchestrator Project | To attach Zscaler AI Security scanner instance to its subnetwork |
| `compute.instances.setMetadata` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security scanner instance |
| `compute.instances.setLabels` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security scanner instance |
| `compute.instances.setMachineType` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security scanner instance |
| `compute.instances.setName` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security scanner instance |
| `compute.instances.setServiceAccount` | Orchestrator Project | To assign Zscaler AI Security scanner instance service account |
| `cloudsql.instances.get` | Orchestrator Project | To get the restored cloud SQL instance details |
| `cloudsql.instances.list` | Orchestrator Project | To list the restored cloud SQL instances |
| `cloudsql.instances.delete` | Orchestrator Project | To delete the restored cloud SQL instances |
| `resourcemanager.projects.get` | Orchestrator Project | To retrieve the project details |
| `cloudsql.backupRuns.get` | Orchestrator Project | To get restored latest cloud SQL instance backup |
| `cloudsql.instances.restoreBackup` | Orchestrator Project | To restore latest cloud SQL backup |
| `cloudsql.users.update` | Orchestrator Project | To update restored cloud SQL user |
| `secretmanager.secrets.delete` | Orchestrator Project | To delete Zscaler AI Security secret |
| `secretmanager.secrets.update` | Orchestrator Project | To update Zscaler AI Security secret |
| `secretmanager.versions.add` | Orchestrator Project | To add Zscaler AI Security secret version |
| `compute.instances.create` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security scanner instance |
| `compute.disks.create` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security scanner instance disk |
| `cloudsql.instances.create` | Orchestrator Project | To create the restored cloud SQL instance |
| `secretmanager.secrets.create` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security secret |
| `cloudsql.users.create` | Orchestrator Project | To create restored cloud SQL user |
| `logging.sinks.get` | GCP Organisation | To update Zscaler AI Security org log sink for buckets incremental scans |
| `logging.sinks.list` | GCP Organisation | To update Zscaler AI Security org log sink for buckets incremental scans |
| `logging.sinks.update` | GCP Organisation | To update Zscaler AI Security org log sink for buckets incremental scans |

This service account is used by AI Security to discover resources in the GCP projects and to instruct Local Scanner Platform to perform scan-related instructions. The service account is assigned the following Managed Roles, which provide the necessary permissions:

- Viewer
- Organization Policy Viewer
- Folder Viewer
- Service Usage Consumer
- Service Account User
- Security Reviewer
- Cloud Asset Viewer

| Permission | Scope | Purpose |

| `storage.buckets.get` | Monitored Projects | To get storage buckets metadata |
| `storage.managedfolders.get` | Monitored Projects | To get managed folders metadata |
| `storage.managedfolders.list` | Monitored Projects | To list the managed folders |
| `storage.buckets.getIamPolicy` | Monitored Projects | To get the storage bucket's IAM policy metadata |
| `storage.managedfolders.getIamPolicy` | Monitored Projects | To get the managed folder's IAM policy |
| `cloudasset.assets.searchAllIamPolicies` | Monitored Projects/Organisation | To get GCP resources IAM policies |
| `compute.autoscalers.update` | Orchestrator Project | To update the Zscaler AI Security instance group manager scaling |
| `compute.instanceGroupManagers.use` | Orchestrator Project | To update the Zscaler AI Security instance group manager scaling |
| `compute.instanceGroupManagers.update` | Orchestrator Project | To update the Zscaler AI Security instance group manager scaling |
| `compute.subnetworks.use` | Orchestrator Project | To attach Zscaler AI Security instance to subnetworks |
| `compute.instances.setMetadata` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security instance |
| `compute.instances.delete` | Orchestrator Project | To terminate Zscaler AI Security instance |
| `compute.instances.setLabels` | Orchestrator Project | To create Zscaler AI Security instance |

| `compute.disks.create` | Orchestrator Project | To create Disks for Zscaler AI Security instance |
| `compute.disks.setLabels` | Orchestrator Project | To create Disks for Zscaler AI Security instance |
| `compute.instanceTemplates.delete` | Orchestrator Project | To delete Zscaler AI Security instance template |

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/iam-roles-and-permissions-microsoft-azure","lastmod":"2026-07-14T08:44Z","nid":"1540254"} -->
## IAM Roles and Permissions for Microsoft Azure

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/iam-roles-and-permissions-microsoft-azure
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > IAM Roles and Permissions for Microsoft Azure
- Last modified: 2026-07-14T08:44Z
- Summary: Information about the roles created and permissions assigned while onboarding Azure subscriptions.

As part of the [onboarding](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant) process, you need to deploy the AI Security templates in the Microsoft Entra tenant. These templates create a service principal (enterprise application), custom roles, and managed identities in Microsoft Entra ID. AI Security requires these roles to connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant, discover the resources, and collect metadata.

## IAM Roles

AI Security creates the following IAM roles to access the Azure subscriptions:

- Resource Discovery Role
- AI Security Access Role
- Target Role
- Orchestrator Role
- Scanner Role
- Custom Network Configuration Role
- Encryption Role
- Custom Role (AI Agent)

This role is used by the Local Scanner Platform to perform the CMK encryption related tasks on instances.

| Permission | Scope | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/read` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To list the keys in a specified vault |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/unwrap/action` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To unwrap a symmetric key with a Key Vault key |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/wrap/action` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To wrap a symmetric key with a Key Vault key |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/read` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To list the keys in a specified vault |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/decrypt/action` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To decrypt ciphertext with a key |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/encrypt/action` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To encrypt plaintext with a key |

AI Security requires the resource discovery role to identify resources within the onboarded subscriptions. This role is assigned at the management group level and has the following permissions:

| Permission | Scope | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `*/read` | Management group | Actions | To allow read permissions to read the metadata of Azure resources |
| `Microsoft.Insights/DiagnosticSettings/read` | Management group | Actions | To discover diagnostic settings |
| `Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes/values/read` | Management group | Actions | To read activity logs |
| `Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/read` | Management group | Actions | To discover Azure resource groups |
| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/read` | Management group | Actions | To discover Azure blob containers |
| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action` | Management group | Actions | To discover Azure storage account keys |

AI Security requires the access role to send data scan requests to the storage account queues that are used by the orchestrator subscription. The role is assigned at the AI Security resource group level and has the following permissions:

| Permission | Scope | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To read virtual machines |
| `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets/deallocate/action` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To deallocate virtual machine scale set |
| `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets/virtualMachines/delete` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To delete virtual machine in a virtual machine scale set |
| `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create or update virtual machine scale set |

The orchestrator subscription requires the target role to scan the data stores. The role is assigned at the monitoring scope or target subscriptions level and has the following permissions:

| Permission | Scope | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `*/read` | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To allow read permissions to read the metadata of Azure resources |
| `Microsoft.Compute/disks/beginGetAccess/action` | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To get the SAS URI of the disk |
| `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/write` | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To restore the PostgreSQL Flexible Server into the Orchestrator subscription |
| `Microsoft.Insights/DiagnosticSettings/write` | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To create a diagnostic setting for Azure storage accounts |
| `Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases/write` | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To restore the SQL server into the Orchestrator subscription |
| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action` | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To read Azure storage account keys |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/read` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To list the keys in a specified vault |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/unwrap/action` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To unwrap a symmetric key with a Key Vault key |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/wrap/action` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To wrap a symmetric key with a Key Vault key |
| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/*/read` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To read blobs from containers |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/getSecret/action` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To get the value of a secret This permission is conditional and only required if Custom Network is used with Unmanaged DB Scanning. |
| `Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries/pull/read` | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To pull or get images from a container registry. |
| `Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries/catalog/read` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To list repositories in a container registry. |
| `Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries/repositories/metadata/read` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To get the metadata of a specific repository for a container registry. |
| `Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries/repositories/content/read` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To pull or get images from a container registry. |

To configure a custom network in your organization, the orchestrator requires the following roles and permissions at the subscription level, to establish a connection between the custom network components, the scanner instance, and SQL database.

These permissions are conditional and only required if Custom Network is selected.

| Permission | Scope | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/join/action` | Orchestrator Subscription | Actions | To join the Network Security Group of the Custom Network mode |
| `Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/join/action` | Orchestrator Subscription | Actions | To join the subnet of the Custom Network |
| `Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/joinViaServiceEndpoint/action` | Orchestrator Subscription | Actions | To join the SQL database to a subnet of the Custom Network |

The scanner role is used by the scanner instances that are launched in the orchestrator subscription to perform data scanning. The role is assigned at the AI Security resource group level and has the following permissions:

| Permission | Scope | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `*/read` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To allow read permissions to read the metadata of Azure resources |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/getSecret/action` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To get the value of a secret |
| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/*/read` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To read blobs from containers |

The orchestrator instance requires this role to scan the data. The role is assigned at the AI Security resource group level and has the following permissions:

| Permission | Scope | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `*/read` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To allow read permissions to read the metadata of Azure resources |
| `Microsoft.Compute/disks/beginGetAccess/action` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To get the SAS URI of the disk |
| `Microsoft.Compute/disks/delete` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To delete the disk |
| `Microsoft.Compute/disks/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create the disk |
| `Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/delete` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To delete the snapshot |
| `Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create a snapshot |
| `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/delete` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To delete the virtual machine |
| `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create virtual machine extension This permission is conditional and only required if Custom Network is selected. |
| `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create a virtual machine for scanning |
| `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets/read` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To read the properties of virtual machine scale sets |
| `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets/virtualMachines/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To update the properties of a virtual machine in a VM scale sets |
| `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/delete` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To delete the PostgreSQL flexible server used for scanning |
| `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/PrivateEndpointConnectionsApproval/action` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To determine if the user is allowed to approve a private endpoint connection |
| `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/read` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To read the properties of the PostgreSQL flexible server |
| `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create the PostgreSQL flexible server for scanning |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/versions/read` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To list the versions of a specified key, or read the specified version of a key |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create a new secret |
| `Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/assign/action` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To assign the user-managed identity to scanner-related instances |
| `Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/join/action` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To join the scanner network security group |
| `Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/delete` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To delete the private endpoint created for scanning |
| `Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create the private endpoint for scanning |
| `Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/join/action` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To join the scanner virtual network |
| `Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/joinViaServiceEndpoint/action` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To join SQL database to scanner subnet |
| `Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases/delete` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To delete the SQL server database created for scanning |
| `Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create the SQL server database for scanning |
| `Microsoft.Sql/servers/delete` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To delete the SQL server for scanning |
| `Microsoft.Sql/servers/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create the SQL server for scanning |
| `Microsoft.Sql/servers/virtualNetworkRules/delete` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To delete a virtual network rule added for scanning |
| `Microsoft.Sql/servers/virtualNetworkRules/write` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To create a virtual network rule for scanning |
| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To discover Azure storage account keys |
| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/queueServices/queues/read` | AI Security resource group | Actions | To read AI Security queues |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/read` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To list the keys in a specified vault |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/unwrap/action` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To unwrap a symmetric key with a Key Vault key |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/wrap/action` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To wrap a symmetric key with a Key Vault key |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/delete` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To delete a secret created for scanning |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/getSecret/action` | AI Security resource group | DataActions | To get the value of a secret |

| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/fileServices/fileshares/files/write` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To write MIP labeled files |
| `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/fileServices/writeFileBackupSemantics/action` | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To write file backup semantics privilege |

### API Permissions

The following API permissions are required for MIP labeling:

| Application | Application Permission | Scope | Type | Purpose |

| Azure Rights Management Services | `Content.Writer` | Orchestrator Managed Identity | Application | To create protected content |

| Microsoft Graph | `InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All` | Orchestrator Managed Identity | Application | To read all published labels and label policies for an organization |

The custom role is required to collect data from AI services. Assign this role to the Tree Discovery service principal, created by the [Tree Discovery template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-tree-discovery-template), for each subscription.

- This role is required only when [AI service](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-services) data collection is enabled.

## Integrating AI Security with Cloud Storage Services

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-ai-security-cloud-storage-services
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > External Integrations > Cloud Storage Services > Integrating AI Security with Cloud Storage Services
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on integrating AI Security with various cloud storage services.

Cloud Storage is a service that allows you to store and organize data. You can granularly control access to this data and use it for data analysis, auditing, threat detection, etc., based on your organization's security and compliance requirements.

AI Security can be integrated with cloud storage solutions, such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3), Amazon Security Lake, and Azure Blob Storage services to store and manage your data logs. The integration enables AI Security to send the alert data logs to these cloud storage services.

Only users with the administrator role can configure cloud storage integrations.

You can integrate AI Security with the following cloud storage services:

- [Amazon S3](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-amazon-s3)
- [Azure Blob Storage](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-azure-blob-storage)
- [Amazon Security Lake](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-amazon-security-lake)
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-ai-security-servicenow","lastmod":"2026-08-09T23:28Z","nid":"1541827"} -->
## Integrating AI Security with ServiceNow

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-ai-security-servicenow
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > External Integrations > ITSM Tools > Integrating AI Security with ServiceNow
- Last modified: 2026-08-09T23:28Z
- Summary: How to integrate AI Security with ServiceNow and send issue notifications.

AI Security discovers and monitors AI resources across your cloud environments, including models, agents, data stores, workloads, and guardrails. The ServiceNow integration lets you push these discovered assets and their associated security issues into ServiceNow, so your IT, security, and risk teams can manage AI resources within the same governance and compliance workflows they already use.

Ensure that your ServiceNow instance is online.

## Prerequisites

Ensure you do the following before you integrate AI Security with ServiceNow:

- 1. Create a ServiceNow User.
- 2. Create an Inbound Integration.

## Integrating with ServiceNow

To integrate AI Security with ServiceNow:

1. Go to **Administration > External Integrations**.
2. Under **ITSM Integrations**, click **Add**. See image.
3. In the **Integration Details** section, do the following:
  1. **Integration Name:** Enter a unique name for the integration.
  2. **IT Service:** Select **ServiceNow**. See image.
  3. Click **Next**.
4. In the **ITSM Details** section, do the following:
  1. **ServiceNow Hostname:**Enter the ServiceNow hostname.
  2. **Authentication Method:** OAuth 2.0 is selected by default.
  3. **Client ID:** Enter the Client ID created in the prerequisites section.
  4. **Client Secret:** Enter the Client ID created in the prerequisites section.
  5. Click **Test Connection** to validate the ServiceNow connection. A confirmation message appears if the connection is successful. If not, then check the previous steps and try again.
  6. Click **Next**. See image.
5. In the **AI Infrastructure & Issues** section, do the following:
  1. Select one of the following:
    - **AI Assets types:**Tosync asset types such as Agents, Data stores, MCP servers, Guardrails, Models, Workloads, Software Libraries, Code Repositories and Identities with ServiceNow.
    - **Select All:**To sync all available asset types.
  2. **Issues:** Enable the **Issues** toggle to push findings to ServiceNow.
  3. Select the method to determine how the discovered issues must be routed:
    - **Create Ticket:** Push issues to the ServiceNow Import Set (staging) table.
    - **Import Set Table:** Push issues directly to the ServiceNow Incident table.
  4. Click **Next**.
6. In the **Import Set Tables**section, do the following:
  1. **Table Prefix:** Enter a table prefix for the import set tables to be created in ServiceNow and click **Check Tables**.
  2. **Generated Table Names:** Displays a preview of the Import Set table names that are created in your ServiceNow instance, based on the prefix you entered.
  3. **Provision Tables:** Download the creation script to run it in ServiceNow.
    1. Click **Download Script** to download the JavaScript setup script.
    2. Open the downloaded script file and copy all the content.
    3. Log in to your **ServiceNow** instance and open the JavaScript console.
    4. Paste the copied script into the console and click **Run Script**.
    5. The script automatically creates the required import set tables and the necessary roles. See image.
  4. Click **Validate**to validate the setup. See image.
7. Return to the AI Security Admin Portal platform and click **Check Tables**. Ensure that the user account configured for the inbound integration has the required ServiceNow roles to access the tables. Table validation may fail even if the tables exist, if the user lacks sufficient permissions.
8. Verify that the tables are successfully created, a green indicator confirms the setup is complete.
9. Click **Save**to finalize the integration. After saving, the integration appears on the **Integrations** page. Allow up to an hour for the data to be pushed into the ServiceNow tables.

To create a ServiceNow user, do the following:

1. Log in to your **ServiceNow**instance.
2. Navigate to **User Administration > Users**.
3. Click**New.**
4. Enter all the relevant fields to create a new user and click **Submit**.
5. To assign roles to the created user, go to **User Administration** **> Users**.
6. Select the user that you would like to assign the role to.
7. Add the following roles to the user:
  - import_admin
  - import_set_loader
  - import_transformer See image.
8. Click **Save**.

To create an inbound integration, do the following:

1. Navigate to **Inbound Integrations** in your **ServiceNow**instance.
2. Click **New Integration**. See image.
3. Select **OAuth – Client Credential Grant** as the authentication type. See image.
4. In the **New record** page, enter the following details for the connection:
  1. **Name:** Enter a name for the record.
  2. **Provider name:** Select the provider name from the drop-down menu.
  3. **OAuth application user:** Enter the user name you created in Create a ServiceNow User step.
  4. **Client ID:** Copy the generated Client ID to a secure location. These credentials are required to complete the integration.
  5. **Client Secret:** Copy the generated Client secret to a secure location. These credentials are required to complete the integration.
5. In the **Configure auth scopes** section, enter:
  1. **Auth scope:**Select the auth scope from the drop-down menu.
  2. Limit Authorization to the following APIs:
    - Table API
    - Import Set API
  3. Enable **Allow access only to APIs in selected scope**.
6. Click **Save**.

[Image: Configure ServiceNow details in the ITSM Details section.]

[Image: Enter a Table Prefix for the import set tables to be created in ServiceNow.]

[Image: Setup Complete Message on the ServiceNow.]

[Image: Select roles from the collection column to add to the roles list]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-amazon-s3","lastmod":"2026-06-05T21:06Z","nid":"1540166"} -->
## Integrating with Amazon S3

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-amazon-s3
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > External Integrations > Cloud Storage Services > Integrating with Amazon S3
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to integrate AI Security with Amazon S3 to send alert details to the cloud storage service.

You can integrate AI Security with Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). This integration enables AI Security to send the alert data logs of your cloud resources to the Amazon S3 buckets for storage.

Only users with the administrator role can configure a cloud storage integration.

## Integrating with Amazon S3

To integrate AI Security with Amazon S3:

1. Go to **Administration** >**External Integrations**.
2. Click **Add** for cloud storage integration. See image.
3. On the **Add Cloud Storage Integration** page, for **Integrations Details**:
  1. For **Integration Name**, enter a unique name for the integration.
  2. For **Cloud Storage**, select **Amazon S3 Bucket**.
4. Click **Next**.
5. Under **Cloud Storage**, complete the following steps to set up the permissions required by AI Security to access the Amazon S3 bucket. See image.
  1. For **Amazon S3 Bucket Name**, enter the bucket name where the data must be stored.
  2. Click the **Copy** icon to copy the **S3 Bucket policy**. The policy authorizes AI Security to access the S3 bucket. You need to paste this policy in the AWS console.
6. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/s3).
  1. Access the required bucket where you want to apply the bucket policy.
  2. Select **Permissions**.
  3. Under**Bucket policy**, click **Edit**.
  4. On the **Edit bucket policy** page, paste the **S3 bucket policy** you copied earlier, then click **Save changes**. See image.
7. In the AI Security Admin Portal, under **Cloud Storage**, enter the **Folder Location**of the bucket.
8. Before testing the connection, check the encryption type that is applied to the S3 bucket.
  1. On the [AWS Management Console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/s3), select the **Properties** tab, then scroll down to **Default encryption**.
  2. Select **Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)** as the encryption key type for the connection to be successful and eventually for seamless data transfer. If you select AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS), then the connection fails. See image.
9. Click **Test Connection** to check if the connection is established between AI Security and Amazon S3 service. A message is displayed to indicate the connection is successful.
10. Click **Next**.
11. Review the integration summary. Click the **Edit** icon if you want to make any changes. See image.
12. Click **Finish**.

You can see the integration details on the **Integrations** page. The initial status is shown as Pending because data is not yet sent to the Amazon S3 bucket. You must first configure and associate the [Issue rules](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-issues) with this integration for AI Security to be able to send the data logs. After AI Security sends the data logs to the Amazon S3 Bucket, then the status changes to Success.

## Integrating with Amazon Security Lake

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-amazon-security-lake
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > External Integrations > Cloud Storage Services > Integrating with Amazon Security Lake
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to integrate AI Security with Amazon Security Lake and send alert details.

You can integrate AI Security with the Amazon Security Lake service to export and store the alert data in a dedicated Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) bucket that is pre-configured as part of the Amazon Security Lake setup.

Amazon Security Lake is a data lake for security logs, built into the customer’s account. The data lake is backed by an Amazon S3 bucket and organizes data as a set of Lake Formation tables. Amazon Security Lake is designed to optimize the cost of storing and querying massive security logs. Amazon Security Lake uses the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) as the selected format for the alert information and requires the Parquet file format for the stored alerts. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://aws.amazon.com/security-lake/).

## Prerequisites

Complete the following steps before exporting the alert data to Amazon Security Lake:

- 1. Configure the Amazon Security Lake service.
- 2. Configure the custom source.
- 3. Collect the S3 Bucket details.

## Integrating AI Security with Amazon Security Lake

To configure the Amazon Security Lake integration:

1. Go to **Administration**> **External Integrations**.
2. Click **Add** for cloud storage integration.
3. On the **Add Cloud Storage Integration** page:
  - For **Integration Name**, enter a unique name for the integration.
  - For **Cloud Storage**, select **Amazon Security Lake**.
4. Click **Next**.
5. On the **Cloud Storage** page:
  - **AI Security AWS Account**: Copy the AI Security AWS Account ID and paste it in the **Account ID** field while creating the custom source on the Amazon Security Lake console.
  - **External ID**: Copy the External ID and paste it in the **External ID** field while creating the custom source on the Amazon Security Lake console.
  - **IAM Role**: Enter the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) ARN role that you copied after creating the custom source. This role allows the AI Security AWS account to write data to Security Lake.
  - **Amazon S3 Bucket Name**: Provide the Amazon S3 bucket name.
  - **Bucket Region**: Select the bucket region from the drop-down menu. You should have these details from the Prerequisites step.
  - **Folder Location**: Provide the folder path for the S3 bucket set for Amazon Security Lake. You should have these details from the Prerequisites step.
6. Click **Test Connection** to verify the connection between AI Security and the AWS service. The test connection validates that the S3 bucket exists. A message is displayed that the connection is successful.
7. Click **Next**.
8. Review the integration summary. Click the **Edit** icon if you want to make any changes. See image.
9. Click **Finish**.

You can see the integration details on the Integrations page. The initial status shows as Pending because data is not yet sent to the Amazon Security Lake. After you configure and associate the alert rules with this integration, and when AI Security starts sending the alert data to Amazon Security Lake, the status changes to Success.

## Partitioning

Partitioning is a technique for organizing datasets, so they can be queried efficiently. AI Security alerts are exported in OCSF format to Amazon Security Lake and are stored in Parquet files. The Parquet format is a column-based data format.

The files are limited by size. A new file is generated and posted whenever the file size reaches 256 MB or after 5 minutes. The files are stored under the root path created for the custom source. The folder structure is: `region=<awsregion>/accountid=<cloudaccountid>/eventDay=<YYYYMMDD>`.

New folders are generated to host new alert files.

## OCSF Mapping

OCSF includes an open specification for the normalization of security telemetry across a wide range of security products and services, as well as open-source tools that provide support for using the OCSF schema. To learn more, refer to the [GitHub page on OCSF](https://github.com/ocsf/).

- Cloud alert data logs written to OCSF

## Troubleshooting

Zscaler recommends the following resolutions for issues that you might encounter while integrating and using AI Security with Amazon Security Lake.

| **Issue** | **Resolution** |
| --- | --- |
| The AI Security alert data is available in the Amazon Security Lake S3 bucket, but the Glue Crawler fails to parse the data into Amazon Security Lake. | This issue typically occurs when the custom source that is created for the integration is using the wrong event class. Make sure you create the custom source with the `Security Finding` event class. |
| Amazon Security Lake integration object on the AI Security Integrations page shows a Failed status. | This indicates that AI Security does not have the permission to access the Amazon Security Lake S3 bucket. While integrating AI Security with Amazon Security Lake, make sure you have applied the required policy to grant AI Security access to the S3 bucket. |
| New alerts are present in the AI Security Admin Portal but are not exported into Amazon Security Lake. | Make sure you've configured the alert rule notification and check the scope of the alert rule. |

Make sure you have a configured Amazon Security Lake service that is connected to an S3 bucket in your AWS account. To learn more, refer to the [Amazon Security Lake documentation](https://aws.amazon.com/security-lake/).

Zscaler is regarded as a source integration for Amazon Security Lake. To enable the integration, you must generate a custom source in Amazon Security Lake. To learn more, refer to the [Amazon Security Lake documentation](https://aws.amazon.com/security-lake/).

1. Sign in to your AWS account.
2. Open the [Security Lake console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/securitylake/).
3. From the Security Lake left-side navigation, select **customized sources**.
4. Scroll down to the **Customized source details** section:
  - **Data source name**: Provide a name for this custom source. This name determines the path in the S3 bucket to which the alert data is written. Amazon Security Lake generates a new folder for each custom source.
  - **Event class**: Make sure you use the `Security_Finding` event class.
  - **Region**: Select the region from the drop-down menu. The custom source is created in the region where the AWS console is connected. You need to specify this region while setting up the Security Lake integration in the AI Security Admin Portal.
  - **Account ID**: Enter the account ID that you copied from the **Cloud Storage** page in the AI Security Admin Portal.
  - **External ID**: Enter the external ID that you copied from the **Cloud Storage** page in the AI Security Admin Portal. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user_externalid.html). The **AWS Account ID** and **External ID** are identifiers of the custom source (AI Security) that writes logs and events to the data lake. See image.
5. Click **Create**. The Amazon Security Lake custom source is created.
6. On the **Customized sources** page, search for the custom source you created.
7. Copy the ARN IAM role. You need to provide this value while setting up the Security Lake integration in the AI Security Admin Portal. See image.

Make sure you have the following information for setting up the AI Security integration:

- The Amazon Security Lake S3 region.
- The S3 bucket name (e.g., aws-security-data-lake-us-east-2-o-4g8wg3sx9z).
- The folder prefix for the custom source path on the S3 bucket (e.g., /ext/dspm-security-alerts).

## Integrating with Azure Blob Storage

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/integrating-azure-blob-storage
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > External Integrations > Cloud Storage Services > Integrating with Azure Blob Storage
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to integrate AI Security with Azure Blob Storage and send alert details.

You can integrate AI Security with your Azure Blob Storage. This integration enables AI Security to send the issue data logs of your cloud resources to the Azure Blob Storage containers for storage and data analysis by external tools.

Only users with the administrator role can configure a cloud storage integration.

## Integrating with Azure Blob Storage

To configure the Azure Blob Storage integration:

1. Go to **Administration** >**External Integrations**.
2. On the **Integrations** page, click **Add**. See image.
3. On the **Add Integration** page:
  1. For **Integration Name**, enter a unique name.
  2. For **Cloud Storage**, select **Azure Blob Storage**.
4. Click **Next**.
5. Under **Cloud Storage**, complete the following steps to provide AI Security with write permissions on Azure Blob Storage.
  1. Copy the connection string from the Azure portal.
  2. For **Azure Storage Account Connection String**, paste the connection string you copied from the Azure portal.
  3. (Optional) **Container Location**: Enter the location of the storage container. It is mandatory to first create a folder in your Azure Blob Storage and then add the name.
  4. Click **Test Connection** to verify the connection between AI Security and the Azure Blob Storage. A message is displayed indicating the connection is verified.
6. Click **Next**.
7. Review the integration summary. Click the **Edit** icon if you want to make any changes. See image.
8. Click **Finish**.

You can see the integration details on the **Integrations** page. The initial status is shown as Pending because data is not yet sent to the Azure Blob Storage. You must configure and associate the [issue rules](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-issues) with this integration for AI Security to be able to send the data logs. When AI Security sends the data logs to the Blob Storage, then the status changes to Success.

1. Log in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
2. Go to your storage account.
3. Under **Security**>**Networking**, select **Access Key**.
4. Click **Show Keys** to view your access keys and connection strings. A connection string includes the authorization information required for AI Security to access data in your Azure Storage account. To learn more, refer to the [Azure Blob Storage documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-keys-manage?tabs=azure-portal).
5. Copy the entire connection string for the relevant access key.

[Image: Review the integration]

## Issue Status

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/issue-status
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Monitoring & Investigation > Issues > Issue Status
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about AI Security alert statuses in the AI Security Admin Portal.

When a policy violation is detected in your cloud resources, AI Security generates issues and notifies recipients to take action. These generated issues are displayed on the [Issues page](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-issues). Issues that are initially generated are in Open status. When these issues are evaluated and addressed, the status transitions to Resolved, Closed, or Snoozed.

AI Security issues can have the following status:

| Issue Status | Description | Example Scenarios | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open | The new issues generated for a policy violation or resolved issues for which policy violation is detected again. | A [policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-posture-policies) violation is detected.; The policy violation is detected again within 180 days of resolving the issue. | An open issue moves to the resolved, closed, or snoozed state based on the latest policy findings, [manual actions](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-issues) (resolve, snooze, unsnooze, or reset), or issue filter (ignore issue filter).; When a data store is removed from the [scan settings](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings), the issues remain open based on the posture assessment of the data store.; An automatically resolved issue is reopened if the violation is detected within 180 days of resolving the issue. The Issue Status Reason in an individual issue's page describes the reason why the issue is reopened.; AI Security generates a new issue if the policy violation is detected again after 180 days. |
| Closed | The issues that are no longer valid. | The [cloud account](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts) is offboarded.; The cloud account is deleted from the CSP.; The policy is edited, disabled, or deleted.; The data store is deleted.; The data store that was removed earlier is not added back to the scan settings. | A closed issue is the final state of an issue (i.e., it does not move to any other state).; The issue graph for a closed issue is frozen and the nodes are unclickable.; The Sensitive Data tab in an individual issue's page is hidden.; The closed issue is deleted from the AI Security Admin Portal after 180 days. |
| Resolved | The policy violation detected in the data store is fixed. | The issue is manually resolved in the AI Security Admin Portal.; The policy violation is manually remediated.; The policy violation is resolved in the CSP. | An automatically resolved issue moves to the open state if the issue is detected within 180 days of resolving the issue. AI Security generates a new issue if the policy violation is detected again after 180 days.; A manually resolved issue remains in the resolved state until you reset it. When you reset the issue, the issue status is updated based on the latest policy findings.; A resolved issue moves to the closed state if the data store, policy, or cloud account is deleted.; The issue graph for a resolved issue is frozen, and the nodes are unclickable.; The Sensitive Data tab in an individual issue's page is hidden. |
| Snoozed | Issues of low priority that are paused for a specific duration. | The issue is manually snoozed to pause notification for a specified duration. | A snoozed issue remains snoozed even if the policy violation is resolved in the CSP.; If you unsnooze an issue or if the snooze period expires, the issue status changes to open or resolved based on the latest policy findings.; If the data store or policy is deleted when the issue is snoozed, the issue moves to the closed state irrespective of the snooze period.; If the policy violation is resolved in the CSP, the issue graph freezes, and the nodes become unclickable. |
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Managing AI Model Scan Integrations

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-ai-model-scan-integrations
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Model Scan Management > Managing AI Model Scan Integrations
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to register, edit, or delete an AI model scan integration in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The AI Security AI model scanner is a command-line tool used to scan machine learning models for security risks before deployment. To use the AI model scanner, you must first add an integration and generate an API key in the AI Security Admin Portal. This API key authenticates the model scanner and allows it to send the scan results back to AI Security for analysis.

On the **Administration** > [**Model Scan Management**](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scanning-ai-models) page, you can:

- Add an Integration and Generate an API Key
- Download the AI Model Scanner

## Edit an Integration

To edit an integration and regenerate the API key if it has been exposed, lost, or for periodic credential rotation:

1. Go to **Administration** > **Model Scan Management**.
2. On the [Integration Registration](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scanning-ai-models) tab, click **Actions** (**⋮**), and select **Edit** for the required integration. See image. The **Edit Integration** window appears.
3. In the **Edit Integration** window: See image.
  - **Integration Name**: Update the integration name if needed.
  - Click **Regenerate Key** to generate a new API key. A new API key is generated. The regenerated API key invalidates the existing API key. Copy the new API key, store it in a secure location, and update all environments or scripts where the old API key was used.

## Delete an Integration

To delete an integration:

1. Go to **Administration** > **Model Scan Management**.
2. On the [Integration Registration](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scanning-ai-models) tab, click **Actions** (**⋮**), and select **Delete**for the required integration. See image. The **Delete Integration** confirmation window appears.
3. In the **Delete Integration** confirmation window, read the message, and then enter `CONFIRM` in the text box. See image.
4. Click **Delete**.

The registered integration is deleted from the AI Security Admin Portal.

1. Select the [Integration Registration](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scanning-ai-models) tab and click **Add Integration**. See image. The **Add Integration** drawer appears.
2. In the **Add Integration** drawer: This API key is required to authenticate the scanner and is not recoverable. Copy the API key and store it in a secure location. See image.
  1. **Integration Name**: Enter a name for the integration.
  2. Click **Save**.
  3. Under **API Key Management**, click **Generate Key**. An API key is generated and displayed.

[Image: Model Scan Management page showing the list of integrations and an annotation for Add Integration button]

[Image: Add Integration drawer with the details filled and generated API key]

1. Select the [Scanner Download](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scanning-ai-models) tab.
2. Click the **Download** icon for the scanner binary appropriate for your operating system and save the file in your local folder. Use the downloaded scanner binary to configure the AI model scanner.

See image.

[Image: Model Scan Management page with Scanner Download tab selected, displaying available model scanner to download.]

[Image: Model Scan Management page showing the list of integrations and an annotation for Edit button]

[Image: The Edit Integration drawer showing the options to update the integration details.]

[Image: Model Scan Management page showing the list of integrations and an annotation for Delete option]

[Image: Delete Integration pop-up window for confirming the delete action.]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-issues","lastmod":"2026-06-05T21:06Z","nid":"1540787"} -->
## Managing Issues

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-issues
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Monitoring & Investigation > Issues > Managing Issues
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to manage AI Security issues in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can resolve, snooze, unsnooze, or reset the issues as required.

## Resolving Issues

AI Security generates [issues](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-issues) for any [policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-ai-posture-policies)violations or misconfigurations that are detected in your cloud resources. You might want to manually resolve issues that are not critical or do not pose any issues.

- To resolve an issue, you must be assigned either an administrator role or a custom role with the **Resolve Issues** permission. If you have the **Resolve Issues** permission, you are automatically assigned permissions to reset manually resolved issues.
- When you manually resolve an issue, the issue is resolved only in the AI Security Admin Portal and the policy violation persists in the cloud service provider (CSP). The issue remains in the resolved state until you reset it.

To resolve a single issue or multiple issues:

1. Go to **Administration**> **Issues**> **Issues**.
2. Select the **All Issues** tab, and resolve the issue on the Issues page or an individual issue's details page:
  - Issues Page
3. In the **Resolve Issue** window, enter the reason for resolving the issue.
4. Click **Resolve**. See image. A message appears indicating that the issues are successfully resolved.

## Snoozing Issues

When you do not want to take any action for an issue at the moment, or you do not want to be notified for an issue, you can manually snooze the issue and specify the duration. When you snooze an issue, the issue notifications are paused and not shared with the recipients or [third-party integrations](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-external-integrations) within the specified snooze period.

- To snooze an issue, you must be assigned either an administrator role or a custom role with the **Snooze Issues** permission. If you have the **Snooze Issues** permission, you are automatically assigned permissions to reset snoozed issues.
- A snoozed issue remains snoozed for the specified duration if the issue is resolved in the CSP or if the resource or policy is deleted.

To snooze a single issue or multiple issues:

1. Go to **AI Infrastructure**> **Issues**> **Issues View**.
2. Snooze the issue on the Issues View page:
  - Issues Page
3. In the **Snooze Issue** window:
  - **Reason for Snooze**: Enter the reason for snoozing the issue.
  - **Snooze End Date**: Select the duration until when you want to snooze the issue. By default, the issue is snoozed for 1 day.
4. Click **Snooze**. See image. A message appears indicating that the issues are snoozed.

## Unsnoozing Issues

If you've accidentally snoozed an issue, or you want to start receiving notifications for a snoozed issue, you can unsnooze it. When you unsnooze an issue, the status of the issue is updated based on the latest policy findings.

To unsnooze a single issue or multiple issues:

1. Go to **AI Infrastructure**> **Issues**> **Issues View**.
2. Select the **All Issues** tab, and unsnooze the issue on the Issues page:
  - Issues View Page
3. In the **Unsnooze Issue** window, click **Unsnooze**. See image. A message appears indicating that the issues are unsnoozed.

## Resetting Issues

If you've accidentally resolved an issue, you can reset the issue. When you reset an issue, the status of the issue is updated based on the latest policy findings.

To reset a single issue or multiple issues:

1. Go to **AI Infrastructure**> **Issues**> **Issues View**.
2. Select the **All Issues** tab, and reset the issue on the Issues page or an individual issue's page:
  - Issues Page
3. In the **Reset Issue** window, click **Reset**. See image. A message appears indicating that the issues are reset based on the latest policy findings.

- Locate the required snoozed issue, click the **Actions** () icon, then select **Unsnooze**. See image.
- To unsnooze multiple snoozed issues, select the corresponding checkboxes. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Unsnooze**. See image.

Click the **Issue ID** of the snoozed issue to view that individual issue's page. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Unsnooze**.

- Locate the required issue, click the **Actions** () icon, then select **Snooze**. See image.
- To snooze multiple issues, select the corresponding checkboxes. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Snooze**. See image.

Click the **Issue ID** to view that individual issue's page. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Snooze**.

- Locate the required issue, click the **Actions** () icon, then select **Resolve**. See image.
- To resolve multiple issues, select the corresponding checkboxes. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Resolve**. See image.

- Locate the required resolved issue, click the **Actions** () icon, then select **Reset**. See image.
- To reset multiple resolved issues, select the corresponding checkboxes. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Reset**. See image.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-monitoring-scope-aws","lastmod":"2026-06-29T21:06Z","nid":"1539931"} -->
## Managing Monitoring Scope for AWS

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-monitoring-scope-aws
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Organization > Managing Monitoring Scope for AWS
- Last modified: 2026-06-29T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to manage the monitoring scope for AWS in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The monitoring scope refers to the AWS target accounts that are [onboarded](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization). When new accounts are added to your organization, you can onboard them to AI Security for monitoring data stores. You can add new accounts to the monitoring scope, but you cannot remove the existing target accounts.

Additionally, you can enable autodetection at the organization or organizational unit (OU) level. The autodetection feature enables AI Security to automatically detect and onboard any new accounts added to the organization or OU in the future. This eliminates the need to manually onboard new accounts to AI Security.

## Prerequisites

You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the AI Security Admin Portal.

## Managing Monitoring Scope

To add new accounts to the monitoring scope:

1. Go to **Administration**> **Account Onboarding**.
2. Select the organization for which you want to add new target accounts.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Monitoring & Autodetection** from the drop-down menu.
  1. On the **Add to Monitoring Scope** page, select the accounts that you want to be monitored. Enable **Autodetection** at the organization or OU level so AI Security can automatically detect and onboard any new accounts that are added in the future. Click **Next**. You must activate automatic deployment in AWS to automatically deploy stack instances for newly added account in the future.
  2. On the **Assign Business Units** page, change the [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-business-units) for the OU if required, then click **Next**.
  3. On the **Apply Changes** page, download the monitoring scope template and run it in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
    - Template Type
    - Monitoring Scope
    - Autodetection
4. Click **Done**. The new target accounts are added to the monitoring scope. You can view all the organization's onboarded accounts in the [Accounts tab](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-onboarded-account-details).

Select the **CloudFormation**or **Terraform**template.

- Run the CloudFormation template
- Run the Terraform template

- i. Download the monitoring scope template.
- ii. Update the StackSet.

Click **Monitoring Scope** to download the template as a ZIP file and extract it to your local system. The ZIP file contains two files:

- A CSV file that contains a list of target accounts that needs to be scanned.
- A YAML file that contains the policies and permissions required for AI Security to connect to the AWS organization.

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) root account and go to **CloudFormation**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **StackSets**.
3. Identify the StackSet created for monitoring scope while [onboarding the organization](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization) and click **StackSet name**.
4. Under **Actions**, click **Edit StackSet details**.
5. On the **Choose a template** page:
  - **Prerequisite - Prepare template**: Select **Replace current template**.
  - **Specify template**: Select **Upload a template file**.
  - **Upload a template file**: Click **Choose file**, browse your folder and select the YAML file downloaded from the AI Security Admin Portal, then click **Open**.
6. Click **Next**.
7. On the **Specify StackSet Details** page, click **Next**.
8. On the **Configure StackSet options** page, click **Next**.
9. On the **Set deployment options** page:
  - Select **Deploy to accounts**and then select **Deploy stacks in accounts**.
  - **Account numbers**: Add the new account numbers or upload the CSV file downloaded from the AI Security Admin Portal.
  - **Specify regions:**Select the regions that contain the data stores that you want to scan.
  - **Region concurrency**: Select **Sequential** to deploy the StackSets in a sequential order as specified in the **Specify regions**.
10. Click **Next**.
11. On the **Review** page, review the StackSet details and then select the **I acknowledge** checkbox to acknowledge AWS CloudFormation's creation of IAM resources with custom names.
12. Click **Submit**. On the **Operations** tab, you can see the status of the StackSet execution. On the **Stack Instances** tab, you can view the stack instances created for each account and region. To complete the StackSet execution, all the individual stack instances must be deployed successfully.

- i. Download the monitoring scope template.
- ii. Copy the access keys of the target account.
- iii. Update and run the Terraform files.

Click **Monitoring Scope** to download the Terraform template as a ZIP file and extract it to your local system. The ZIP file contains the following files:

- A CSV file containing the list of target accounts that you want to be monitored.
- Multiple Terraform files that contains policies and permissions required for the AI Security to connect to the AWS organization.
- A README file that contains the instructions to run the template.

The access keys provide AI Security with administrator access to the target account from the AWS CLI.

1. Sign in to the AWS access portal and select the target account.
2. Click **Access keys**.
3. Select the required tab (macOS/Linux, Windows, PowerShell) based on your operating system.
4. Under **Option 1: Set AWS environment variables**, click **Copy**and save the access keys.

1. Update the downloaded Terraform files:
  - In the `parameters.auto.tfvars` file, under **regions**, enter the primary region of the target account.
  - In the `backend.tf` file, add the name of the storage services where you want to store the Terraform state files. For example:
    - **bucket**: Enter the name of the S3 bucket of the target account.
    - **region**: Enter the primary region of the target account.
    - **dynamoDB_table**: Enter the name of the dynamoDB table in the primary region of the target account.
2. Open the Command prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
3. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform files.
4. Paste the access keys you copied earlier and press `Enter`.
5. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the Terraform working directory: `terraform init`See image.
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`
  3. To run the Terraform script: `terraform apply`Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes`and press `Enter`.

Review the list of OUs that you selected for autodetection.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-monitoring-scope-gcp","lastmod":"2026-08-06T21:06Z","nid":"1539958"} -->
## Managing Monitoring Scope for GCP

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-monitoring-scope-gcp
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > GCP Cloud Accounts > Managing Monitoring Scope for GCP
- Last modified: 2026-08-06T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to manage the monitoring scope for GCP in the AI Security Admin Portal.

The monitoring scope refers to the GCP projects that are [onboarded](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-gcp-organization). When new projects are created in your GCP organization, you can onboard and add new projects to the monitoring scope.

You can also enable autodetection, which allows AI Security to automatically detect and onboard any new projects added in the future. This eliminates the need to manually onboard new projects to AI Security.

## Prerequisites

Be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/predefined-ai-security-roles-and-permissions) or any role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the AI Security Admin Portal.

## Managing Monitoring Scope

To add new projects to the monitoring scope:

1. Go to **Administration >** **Account Onboarding**.
2. Select the cloud account to which you want to add new target projects.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Monitoring & Autodetection** from the drop-down menu.
  1. On the **Add to Monitoring Scope** page, select the projects that you want to be monitored. Enable **Autodetection** so AI Security can automatically detect and onboard any new subscriptions that are added in the future. Click **Next**. After a project has been added to the monitoring scope, you cannot remove it from the monitoring scope. If you want to stop monitoring a project, you need to delete the project from the AI Security organization. To learn more, see[Deleting an Onboarded Account](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deleting-onboarded-account).
  2. On the **Assign Business Units** page, change the [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-business-units) for the management group if required, then click **Next**.
  3. On the **Apply Changes** page:
    - Monitoring Scope
    - Autodetection
  4. Click **Done**.

The new projects are added to the monitoring scope. You can view all the organization's onboarded projects on the [Projects tab](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-onboarding-status).

The onboarding template includes policies and permissions to create custom roles in the GCP organization. This template provides AI Security with the permissions to access the organization.

- i. In the AI Security Admin Portal.
- ii. On the Local System

Click **GCP Onboarding** to download the template as a ZIP file.

Update and run the template in the gcloud using the CLI app:

1. Extract the downloaded ZIP file to a local directory on your system.
2. Locate the `backend.tf` file within the extracted folder and open it in a text editor.
3. Update the file by adding the name of the storage bucket and a preferred prefix where you would like to store the Terraform state files, and then, save and close the `backend.tf` file.
4. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app on your local system.
5. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform file.
6. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the working directory and apply the Terraform configuration: `terraform init`
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`For **Enter a value**, enter the regions where you want AI Security to monitor and scan data in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]`ai-security creates resources required for data scanning only in these specified regions.
  3. To run the Terraform script: `terraform apply`For **Enter a value**, enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]`For **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes` and then press `Enter`.

Review the list of folders that you selected for autodetection.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-orchestrator-network","lastmod":"2026-06-01T21:06Z","nid":"1540258"} -->
## Managing Orchestrator Network

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-orchestrator-network
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Custom Network Configuration > Managing Orchestrator Network
- Last modified: 2026-06-01T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to update the orchestrator and network details in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can modify the orchestrator network details when an existing orchestrator network is being decommissioned, deleted, or if an incorrect network was selected during onboarding. After changing the orchestrator network, you must rerun the orchestrator template to update the deployment. AI Security validates the template deployment and updates the [orchestrator status](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/viewing-orchestrator-status) accordingly.

This option is available only when the AI Security Connection Status is failed for the custom network configuration type.

## Prerequisites

You must be assigned either an Administrator role or a custom role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the AI Security Admin Portal.

## Modifying the Orchestrator Network

To modify the orchestrator network configuration:

1. Go to **Administration**> **Account Onboarding**.
2. Select the cloud account.
3. From the **Manage** drop-down menu, select **Managing Orchestrator Networks**.
4. On the **Manage Orchestrator Networks** page, update the orchestrator network:
  - AWS
  - Azure
5. Click **Done**.

After the templates are deployed, the regions are updated in the AI Security Admin Portal and subsequent data scans are performed on the resources in the selected regions.

1. **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select a region where you want to deploy the orchestrator template.
2. **Subnet ARN**: Enter the subnet where the scanner instances must be launched.
3. **Security Group ID**: Enter the identifier (ID) of the security group that controls network traffic to and from the instances.
4. Click **Next**.
5. On the **Apply Changes** page, [download and run the orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant).

1. **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select a region where you want to deploy the orchestrator template.
2. **Subnet ID**: Enter the subnet where the scanner instances must be launched.
3. **Network Security Group ID**: Enter the identifier (ID) of the security group that controls network traffic to and from the instances.
4. **Storage Account Name**: Enter a unique name for the storage account. This storage account is used to store the activity logs of the target subscriptions and is created while deploying the [onboarding template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant). AI Security validates the uniqueness of the storage account name. If the name is already registered with [Microsoft.Storage](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant#reg-microsoft-storage), AI Security displays an error message. The storage account name must not exceed 16 characters.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Apply Changes** page, [download and run the orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant). If you are using a new subnet from a different VNet, run the following command before deploying the new template: `terraform destroy -target module.scale_set.azurerm_linux_virtual_machine_scale_set.orchestrator_scale_set`
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-policies","lastmod":"2026-06-10T21:06Z","nid":"1540863"} -->
## Managing Policies

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/managing-policies
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > AI Posture Policies & Data Classification > AI Posture Policies > Managing Policies
- Last modified: 2026-06-10T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to enable, disable, edit, delete, or clone policies in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can enable, disable, edit, delete, change policy severity, or clone a policy as required.

- Enabling or Disabling a Single Policy
- Enabling or Disabling Bulk Policies
- Editing a Policy
- Deleting a Policy
- Cloning a Policy
- Changing Policy Severity

You can enable or disable an individual policy or multiple policies as required.

New issues are not generated for disabled policies. However, the status of the existing issues remains unchanged.

To enable or disable a single policy:

1. Go to **Policies & Controls > AI Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, do any of the following:
  - Click the **Actions** icon for the required policy, then select **Enable** or **Disable**. See image.
  - Select the checkbox for the required policy. Select **Enable** or **Disable** from the **Actions** drop-down menu that appears on the page. See image.
3. In the **Enable Policy** or **Disable Policy** window, select the checkbox to confirm that you want to proceed. See image.
4. Click **Enable** or **Disable**.

To enable or disable bulk security policies:

1. Go to **Policies & Controls > AI Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, select the checkboxes for the required policies. The **Actions** drop-down appears on the page. See image.
3. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Enable** or **Disable**.
4. In the **Enable Policy** or **Disable Policy** window, select the checkbox to confirm that you want to proceed. See image.
5. Click **Enable** or **Disable**.

Editing a custom AI posture policy might have an impact on the issues that AI Security generates. If you edit any custom policy, such as the policy title or remediation procedure, the new information is displayed on the [Issues page](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-issues) and the dashboard. If you edit the custom policy query logic, AI Security determines that the custom policy has changed and closes all existing issues, and generates new issues based on the updated custom policy query logic.

You can edit or delete only the custom policies. Predefined policies cannot be edited or deleted.

To edit a custom AI posture policy:

1. Go to **Policies & Controls > AI Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, click the **Actions** icon for the required custom policy.
3. Click **Edit**. You are directed to the **Query Builder** page.
4. On the **Query Builder** page, [edit the query](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/creating-custom-policies)as required.
5. When you are done editing the query, click **Test Run**. The query results are displayed in the **Policy Test Result** window. See image.
6. Click **Accept and Proceed**.
7. On the **Remediation Procedure** page, click **Add Remediation Procedure**.
8. Enter the remediation steps in Markdown format, then click **Save**. If you've already added the remediation procedure, then click the **Edit** icon to modify the text, if required. See image.
9. Click **Next**.
10. On the **Severity and Description** page, edit any of the values as required. See image.
11. Click **Save Changes**.

When you delete a custom policy, all issues previously generated by the policy are closed.

To delete a custom AI posture policy:

1. Go to **Policies & Controls > AI Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, click the **Actions** icon for the required custom policy. See image.
3. Read the confirmation message, then click **Delete**. See image.

[Image: The query result]

[Image: Add the remediation steps]

[Image: Select the Delete option]

[Image: Confirm to delete a policy]

You can clone a predefined or an existing custom policy by reusing its query structure and modifying some parameters, as required, to create another custom policy.

To clone a policy:

1. Go to **Policies & Controls > AI Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, click the **Actions** icon () and select the **Clone** option for the required policy. See image. You cannot clone policies that are temporarily hidden.
3. In the **Duplicate Policy** window, select the checkbox to confirm that you want to proceed, then click **Clone**. See image. You are directed to the **Query Builder** page.
4. On the **Query Builder** page, add additional predicates to the query if required. See image.
5. Continue with the remaining steps to [create the policy](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/creating-custom-policies). The new policy is created and displayed on the **Policy** page.

[Image: Clone a policy]

[Image: Confirmation message]
