You can change the severity of an AI posture policy as required. When you change the policy severity, it impacts the issue risk level that is triggered for any findings by this policy.

You cannot edit, delete, or change the severity level for predefined policies.

To change the policy severity:

1. Go to **Policies & Controls > AI Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, select the checkbox of the required policy. See image.
3. Click the **Actions** drop-down menu and select **Change Severity**. See image.
4. In the **Change Policy Severity** window, select one of the following options from the **Policy Severity** drop-down menu: See image.
  - Critical
  - High
  - Medium
  - Low
5. Click the **I understand the consequences and want to proceed** checkbox.
6. Click **Change**. You have now successfully changed the policy severity.

After [onboarding a cloud account](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts), you can select the services that must be scanned by AI Security. AI Security permissions are restricted to monitor and scan the data only in the selected services.

- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Vulnerability Scanning > Managing Vulnerabilities in AWS Accounts
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about vulnerability scanning of AWS accounts in the AI Security Admin Portal.

AI Security scans your Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud accounts to detect vulnerabilities.

Vulnerability scanning is supported for both AWS-managed and customer-managed encryption. However, to support AWS-managed encryption, at least one customer-managed key should be present in the region.

- Europe(Frankfurt) eu-central-1
- Europe(Ireland) eu-west-1

AI Security scans your Microsoft Azure cloud accounts to detect vulnerabilities.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization","lastmod":"2026-08-20T04:54Z","nid":"1539734"} -->
## Onboarding an AWS Organization

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Organization > Onboarding an AWS Organization
- Last modified: 2026-08-20T04:54Z
- Summary: Information on how to onboard an AWS organization in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can onboard an AWS organization and its associated accounts. AI Security monitors and [scans](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings) the [data stores](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/supported-data-stores-file-types-and-regions) (e.g., S3, EC2 instances, RDS instances and clusters) in the onboarded accounts to identify sensitive data and vulnerabilities.

## Onboarding Workflow

The onboarding process is illustrated in the following image:

## Prerequisites

Before onboarding an AWS organization, ensure you have completed the following:

- Identify an AWS account as the orchestrator account. The AI Security template is deployed in this account to scan the data in the target accounts.
- Identify the target AWS accounts that need to be monitored and protected. AI Security defines these target accounts as monitoring scope.
- You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with Add Accounts permissions in the AI Security Admin Portal.
- Configure[CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-aws-cloudtrail) for management and data events. This allows AI Security to perform incremental [data scans](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings) on S3 buckets. To enable data event for S3 buckets:
  1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **CloudTrail**.
  2. Under **Trails**, click the name of the CloudTrail that must be used to store data events.
  3. Under **Data events**, click **Edit**.
  4. For **All current and future S3 buckets**, select the **Write** checkbox.
  5. Click **Save changes**.
- Identify the template type you want to use:
  - CloudFormation Template
  - Terraform Template

## Onboarding an AWS Organization

To onboard an AWS organization:

1. [Provide AWS organization details.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-organization-details)
2. [Deploy the tree discovery template.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-aws-tree-discovery-template)
3. [Select the network configuration, orchestrator account, monitoring scope, and business unit.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/selecting-aws-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope)
4. [Deploy the orchestrator and monitoring scope templates.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope-templates)

To use the CloudFormation template:

- Understand the following AWS concepts:
  - **Stacks**: A collection of AWS resources that can be managed as a single unit. They are required to run the AI Security templates. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacks.html).
  - **StackSets**: An entity that allows you to create, update, or delete stacks across multiple AWS accounts and regions using a CloudFormation template. StackSets are required to run the AI Security templates. It also allows you to add a new region to an existing StackSet (e.g., add secondary regions for orchestrator setup). To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stackinstances-create.html).
  - **Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles**: IAM roles are entities that assign specific permissions to allow trusted identities to perform actions in AWS. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html).
  - **Subnet**: A subnet is a range of IP addresses in your VPC that can be connected to the internet, other VPCs, or data centers. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/how-it-works.html).
- Create the following IAM roles in the orchestrator account to establish a trust relationship between the orchestrator account and target accounts. The IAM roles are required to create stacks and StackSets that are used to deploy the AI Security template in the AWS organization.
  - AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole
  - AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole
- Create the AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole IAM role on all the target accounts with a trust relationship with the root account and the AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole role. This is required to deploy the AI Security templates on the target accounts via the root account.
- Ensure that each AWS region has at least two default subnets in the default virtual private clouds (VPC). AI Security creates subnets to launch AWS cloud resources (e.g., EC2 instances, S3 buckets) in specific subnets.

To use the Terraform template:

- Install the following on your local system:
  - Terraform CLI to run the Terraform templates.
  - AWS CLI 2.22 version or later to connect to the AWS organization. For instructions on installing or updating AWS CLI, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html).
- Identify the storage services in the primary region of the orchestrator account to store the Terraform state files. You can use an existing storage service or create a new one. For example:
  - AWS S3 Bucket
  - DynamoDB Table

To create an AWS S3 bucket:

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **S3**.
2. Click **Create bucket**.
3. Under **Bucket name**, enter a unique name to the S3 bucket.
4. Click **Create bucket**.

To create a DynamoDB table:

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **DynamoDB**.
2. Click **Create table**.
3. On the **Table details** page:
  - **Table name**: Enter a unique name to the table.
  - **Partition key**: Enter **LockID**.
4. Click **Create table**.

This IAM role with admin permissions creates a trust relationship with the CloudFormation service.

To create the AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole role:

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **IAM**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Roles**.
3. Click **Create Role**.
4. In the **Select trusted entity** page:
  - **Trusted entity type**: Select the **AWS account** tile.
  - **An AWS account**: Select **This account (<root account ID>).**
5. Click **Next**.
6. In the **Add permissions**page, select the **AdministratorAccess** policy from the table and click **Next**.
7. In the **Name, review, and create**page, under **Role name**, enter the role name as **AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole**.
8. Click **Create role**.
9. On the **Permissions** tab, click **Add permissions** and then select **Create inline policy** from the drop-down menu.
  1. On the **Specify permissions** page, under **Policy editor**, select **JSON**.
  2. Copy the following JSON text and paste it in the **Policy editor** text box. `{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Action": [ "sts:AssumeRole" ], "Resource": [ "arn:aws:iam::*:role/AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole" ], "Effect": "Allow" } ] }`
10. Click **Next**.
11. On the **Review and create** page, under **Policy name**, enter `AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationPolicy`.
12. Click **Create policy**.

This IAM role creates a trust relationship with the administrator account and the AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole IAM role.

To create the AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole role:

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **IAM**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Roles**.
3. Click **Create Role**.
4. In the **Select trusted entity** page:
  - **Trusted entity type**: Select the **AWS account** tile.
  - **An AWS account**: Select **This account (<root account ID>)**.
5. Click **Next**.
6. In the **Add permissions**page, select **AdministratorAccess**and **SystemAdministrator** policy from the table and click **Next**.
7. In the **Name, review, and create**page, under **Role name**, enter the role name as **AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole**.
8. Click **Create role**.
9. On the **Permissions** tab, click **Add permissions** and then select **Create inline policy**to provide additional permissions from the drop-down menu.
  1. On the **Specify permissions** page, under **Policy editor**, select **JSON**.
  2. Copy the following JSON text and paste it in the **Policy editor** text box. `{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "cloudformation:*" ], "Resource": "*" } ] }`
  3. Click **Next**.
  4. On the **Review and create** page, under **Policy name**, enter `ScannerCFT`.
  5. Click **Create policy**.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-gcp-organization","lastmod":"2026-07-30T09:34Z","nid":"1539955"} -->
## Onboarding a GCP Organization

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-gcp-organization
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > GCP Cloud Accounts > Onboarding a GCP Organization
- Last modified: 2026-07-30T09:34Z
- Summary: Information about how to onboard a GCP organization in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can onboard a Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account and its associated projects to AI Security. AI Security monitors and scans the Cloud Storage buckets in the onboarded projects to identify sensitive data, misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, and more.

## Prerequisites

Before onboarding the GCP organization, ensure you have completed the following:

- You must have Super Admin access to the Google Admin console.
- You must have a GCP [Organization Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/predefined-ai-security-roles-and-permissions) and an owner role.
- Install the following tools:
  - gcloud CLI to connect to the Google Cloud project and deploy the template using gcloud CLI. To learn more, refer to the [Google Cloud documentation](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install).
  - Terraform CLI v1.7.5 or later to run the Terraform on a Windows system. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/terraform/quickstart-configure).
- Enable debug logging (optional but recommended for troubleshooting). Click to view the instructions.
- Create a custom role in the Google Admin console to assign permissions to user, group, and domain resources. This is an optional step. If skipped, AI Security cannot gain read-only access to this resource data. Click to view the instructions.
- Override the service account key creation policy. Click to view the instructions.
- Identify a GCP project that has the required roles and which is linked to a billing account to deploy the orchestrator template.
- Enable the required GCP APIs in the selected GCP project. Click to view the list of required APIs.

## OAuth Scopes

Zscaler AI Security leverages the following OAuth scopes for API authentication:

- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.readonly
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.readonly
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.member.readonly
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.domain.readonly

Run the following commands to enable the debug logs:

- PowerShell `$env:TF_LOG="TRACE" $env:TF_LOG_PATH="<filepath>filename.log"`
- Bash `export TF_LOG="TRACE" $ export TF_LOG_PATH="<filepath>filename.log"`

By default, the `disable service account key` creation policy prevents you from creating a service account key. Override the `disable service account key`creation policy for the project where you want to create the service account.

1. Sign in to the Google Cloud console and go to [Organization policies](https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/orgpolicies).
2. Select the organization from the project picker.
3. Search for `Disable service account key creation` and click **Disable service account key creation**.
4. On the **Policy for Disable service account key creation** page, click **MANAGE POLICY**.
5. Under the **Policy source** section, select **Override parent's policy**.
6. Under the **Rules** section, click **ADD A RULE**.
7. In the **New rule** window, under the **Enforcement** section, select **Off**.
8. Click **Done**.
9. Click **SET POLICY** to apply the changes.

Ensure the status of `Disable service account key creation` policy is set to **Not enforced**.

1. Run the following command on Google Cloud Shell or gcloud CLI: `gcloud organizations describe <ORG_ID>`Replace `<ORG_ID>` with your organization ID, which is required to get the `directoryCustomerId`.
2. Copy the `directoryCustomerId` value from the output.
3. Go to the [Google Admin SDK Directory](https://developers.google.com/admin-sdk/directory/reference/rest/v1/roles/insert).
4. Click the **API** tag in the right panel and paste the copied `directoryCustomerId` into the **customer** string.
5. Copy the following request provided and paste it into the **Request body** field. `{ "roleName": "role_name", "rolePrivileges": [ { "privilegeName": "DOMAIN_MANAGEMENT", "serviceId": "00haapch16h1ysv" }, { "privilegeName": "GROUPS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00haapch16h1ysv" }, { "privilegeName": "USERS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00haapch16h1ysv" } ] }`Replace `role_name` with a desired name for the new role.
6. Click **Execute**. You are prompted to log in again. You can see the JSON output that includes the newly created role. `{ "kind": "admin#directory#role", "etag": "\"0A0Bc2deFgHi\"", "roleId": "4123456782", "roleName": "role_name", "roleDescription": "", "rolePrivileges": [ { "privilegeName": "DOMAIN_MANAGEMENT", "serviceId": "00abcdef16g1hij" } , { "privilegeName": "GROUPS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00abcdef16g1hij" } , { "privilegeName": "USERS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00abcdef16g1hij" } ], "isSystemRole": false, "isSuperAdminRole": false }`
7. Sign in to the [Google Admin console](https://admin.google.com/ac/roles), search for the newly created role, then click **View privileges** to see the assigned permissions. The following roles are created and permissions are assigned:
  | Role | Permission | Description |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | User | Read | To collect the user data |
  | Group | Read | To collect the group and member data |
  | Domain Management | Read | To collect domain resources |

| API | Description | Project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| admin.googleapis.com | Discover Google Workspace account resources | Tree Discovery, Target |
| cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com | Discover Google Cloud Platform resource containers | Tree Discovery, Target |
| cloudasset.googleapis.com | Discover the history and inventory of Google Cloud resources | Tree Discovery, Target |
| monitoring.googleapis.com | Discover cloud monitoring data and configurations | Tree Discovery, Target |
| orgpolicy.googleapis.com | Discover governance rules on GCP resources | Tree Discovery, Target |
| apikeys.googleapis.com | Manage and use API keys for Google Cloud services and APIs | Tree Discovery, Target |
| bigquery.googleapis.com | Discover and classify sensitive data in BigQuery tables | Tree Discovery, Target |
| serviceusage.googleapis.com | Consume quota for a project | Tree Discovery, Orchestrator, Target |
| iam.googleapis.com | Discover identity and access control for Google Cloud resources | Tree Discovery, Orchestrator, Target |
| networkmanagement.googleapis.com | Check connections between virtual private cloud (VPC) network and AI Security. It is required for BYON | Orchestrator |
| logging.googleapis.com | Discover logs resources and perform logging operations | Orchestrator |
| secretmanager.googleapis.com | Discover secret manager resources and perform operations | Orchestrator |
| servicenetworking.googleapis.com | Enable private connections between the virtual private cloud (VPC) network and AI Security | Orchestrator |
| cloudkms.googleapis.com | Discover KMS resources and perform KMS-related operations | Orchestrator, Target |
| storage.googleapis.com | Discover storage resources and read data from storage | Orchestrator, Target |
| sqladmin.googleapis.com | Manage Cloud SQL instances | Orchestrator, Target |
| compute.googleapis.com | Discover compute resources and perform compute-related operations This is required to enable notebooks.googleapis.com and compute resources on the target project. | Orchestrator, Target To enable this API, the project must be linked to billing. |
| aiplatform.googleapis.com | Interact with Google's unified artificial intelligence and machine learning platform for AI Security to scan the AI models for vulnerabilities | Target |
| notebooks.googleapis.com | Manage Vertex AI resources | Target compute.googleapis.com must be enabled on the target project to enable notebooks.googleapis.com. |

Run the following commands in the gcloud CLI:

- To set your project ID: `gcloud config set project <PROJECT_ID>`Replace <PROJECT_ID> with your project ID, which is required to authenticate your API requests and associate them with the correct project.
- To enable the required API: `gcloud services enable <API_SERVICE_NAME>`Replace <API_SERVICE_NAME> with the API you want to enable. For example, if your project ID is `812345678902`, you can enable the `admin.googleapis.com` API by running: `gcloud config set project 812345678902``gcloud services enable admin.googleapis.com`

## Onboarding a GCP Organization

To onboard a GCP account:

- 1. Provide the GCP account details.
- 2. Deploy the tree discovery template.
- 3. Select the orchestrator project, monitoring scope, and business units.
- 4. (Optional) Configure custom tags or evidence.
- 5. Grant permissions and deploy the onboarding template.

After completing the onboarding process, you can [configure the scan settings](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-settings-gcp-cloud-storage).

The account details are required for AI Security to generate a tree discovery template that is used to connect to the GCP project.

1. Go to **Administration** > **Account Onboarding**.
2. Click **Add New**.
3. Under **Select Cloud Type**, select **Google Cloud**.
4. Click **Next**.
5. In the **Organization Details** section:
  - **Integration Alias**: Enter a user-friendly name for the organization that you want to onboard.
  - **Organization Name**: Enter the organization name that contains the GCP project. This organization name will be validated with the Organization ID on the GCP console. After validation, the verified name is synced with AI Security.
  - **Organization ID**: Enter the organization ID.
  - **Role Name**: Enter a unique name for the role that is created in the project.
  - **Project ID**: Enter the project ID where you want to create the service account and roles. You can get the organization ID, organization name, and project ID from the [Google Cloud console](https://console.cloud.google.com/).
  - **Service Account**: Enter a unique name for the service account. The role and service account names must contain only alphabetic characters, numbers, hyphens ("-"), and underscores ("_").
  - **Notification Emails** (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded tenant. You can add up to 30 email addresses to receive notifications about the issues. You can also add email addresses after completing the onboarding process.
6. Click **Apply**to continue, or click **Reset** if you want to change the details. If all the details are accurate, you are directed to the Connect to the Organization section.

Download and deploy the tree discovery template on the project to create a role that provides read-only access to AI Security, for collecting the metadata for various services and network discoveries. This template contains policies and permissions to create a service principal, a [resource discovery role](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/predefined-ai-security-roles-and-permissions) with the required permissions, and managed identities.

- a. Download and modify the tree discovery template.
- b. Deploy the tree discovery template.
- c. Initialize the tree discovery template.
- d. (Optional) Add a service account.
- e. Validate the deployment in AI Security.

1. In the Zscaler Admin Console, under the **Connect to the Organization** section, click **Tree Discovery** to download the template as a ZIP file and extract it to a folder on your system.
2. Locate the `backend.tf` file in the folder and open it in a text editor.
3. Add the name of the storage bucket and a preferred prefix where you want to store the Terraform state files, then save and close the `backend.tf` file.

Use any of the following methods:

- Google Cloud Shell (Recommended)
- gcloud CLI

Run the following commands to initialize the template. This is required to manage your infrastructure resources.

1. To initialize the Terraform configuration: `terraform init`
2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`
3. To apply the Terraform script: `terraform apply`When you run the `terraform plan` or `terraform apply` command, Terraform verifies that all the required APIs are enabled. If any API is missing, an error message is displayed prompting you to enable the APIs and then continue with the verification. To avoid this situation, enable the required APIs in your project. To learn more, see Enable APIs.
4. The command returns a JSON output that includes the project ID, private key ID, private key, client email address, and other credentials for AI Security to connect with the GCP organization.
5. Copy the JSON data, including the `client email` to a text file. While adding a service account, you need to provide the email ID to validate the template deployment.

1. Sign in to the [Google Admin console](https://admin.google.com/).
2. Go to **Menu** > **Account** > **Admin roles**.
3. Locate the role you created as part of the prerequisites, click the **Actions**drop-down menu, and select **Assign admin**.
4. Click **Assign service accounts**.
5. In the **Add service accounts** window, enter the `client_email` that you copied from the JSON file.
6. Click **ADD** to add the service account to the service accounts list, then click **ASSIGN ROLE** to proceed.

1. In the **Connect to the Organization** section, under **Generated JSON**, paste the JSON output generated with the Terraform apply command.
2. Click **Validate**.

AI Security verifies the JSON data and validates the template deployment. If the validation is successful, you are directed to the Orchestrator & Monitoring Scope section.

1. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app on your local system.
2. Run the following command to connect to the Google Cloud console: `gcloud auth application-default login`You are directed to a browser to authorize access to the Google Auth Library. Log in to your GCP account to confirm authorization and close it after granting access. After successful authorization, the Google Cloud SDK displays a confirmation message, indicating that your credentials are saved to a file.
3. Change the current working directory to the folder containing the modified Terraform file from your system.
4. Run the commands to initialize the template.

1. Sign in to the [Google Cloud console](http://console.cloud.google.com/).
2. On the **Project Selector**, select the Google Cloud project where you want to apply the Terraform configuration.
3. Click **Activate Cloud Shell** at the top. This launches a session in the bottom pane. It can take a few seconds for the session to initialize.
4. From the **More** menu, click **Upload**, then select the **Folder** option. Click **Choose Folder** to select the folder containing the modified Terraform file from your system, and click the **Upload** button.
5. Run the commands to initialize the template.

After validating the [tree discovery template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-gcp-organization#connect-org), select the network configuration, orchestrator, and monitoring scope.

Under **Orchestrator & Monitoring Scope**:

- Select the network configuration.
- Configure the Orchestrator.
- Set the Monitoring Scope.

To modify the configuration for Orchestrator or Monitoring Scope, click **Reset**.

After successfully configuring the projects, you are directed to the Additional Configuration section.

You can choose any of the following network configurations:

- **Zscaler**: Use Zscaler resources to deploy the orchestrator and monitoring scope.
- **Custom**: Use your organization's resources to deploy the orchestrator and monitoring scope.

- By default, the custom configuration is selected.
- Changing the network configuration resets the existing configurations.

To configure the orchestrator, click **Configure Orchestrator**.

The orchestrator configuration depends on the network configuration you chose earlier.

- If you select the Zscaler network configuration
- If you select the custom network configuration

1. On the **Configure Orchestrator Project** page:
  - Select an orchestrator project on which you want to deploy the AI Security orchestrator template.
  - **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select the region where you want to deploy the orchestrator project.
  - **VPC Selflink**: Enter the selflink of the VPC network where you want to deploy the orchestrator. The VPC selflink is the unique identifier for your VPC network in the selected region.
  - **Subnet Selflink**: Enter the selflink of the subnet within the selected VPC where you want to deploy the orchestrator. The subnet selflink identifies the specific subnet network that is used for deployment.
  - **Log Bucket Name**: Enter a unique name for the log bucket. This log bucket stores the target projects' activity logs. The log bucket is created while deploying the onboarding template. The name must be unique, otherwise, AI Security shows an error message. AI Security automatically excludes Google Cloud Storage buckets used for storing logs.
2. Click **Next**.
3. On the **Configure Regions for monitoring and scanner's configuration** page:
  1. **VPC Selflink**: Enter the selflink of the VPC network where you want to deploy the scanner instances.
  2. Choose the regions that AI Security must monitor and enter the **Subnet Selflink** for each selected region. AI Security creates and deploys resources required for scanning only in the selected regions.
4. Click **Done**.

1. On the **Configure Orchestrator Project** page:

The name must be unique, otherwise, AI Security shows an error message. AI Security automatically excludes Google Cloud Storage buckets used for storing logs.

1. Click **Set Monitoring Scope**.

In the **Additional Configuration** section, you can configure custom tags and evidence storage. Click **Skip This Step** to configure the additional details after completing the onboarding process and go to Grant Permissions section.

- Custom Tags

You can configure custom tags while onboarding or skip this step and configure it after completing the onboarding process.

Custom tags are assigned to the resources created by AI Security that enable you to distinguish resources in the organization.

To add custom tags:

4. Click **Done**.

ai-security discovers files and tables containing sensitive data and generates snippets of evidence data to investigate and validate the findings. You can choose an existing bucket or add a new one to store these evidence snippets.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-github-tenant","lastmod":"2026-08-15T07:06Z","nid":"1541396"} -->
## Onboarding GitHub Tenant

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-github-tenant
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Code Repository Onboarding > Onboarding GitHub Tenant
- Last modified: 2026-08-15T07:06Z
- Summary: Information about adding GitHub tenant and select repositories in the AI Security Admin Portal.

Onboarding a GitHub tenant to AI Security Admin Portal connects your organization’s GitHub environment (enterprise, organizations, and repositories) to the AI Security Admin Portal. This connection enables AI Security to discover, assess, and help you govern AI-related activity and risks across your codebase and developer workflows. The system checks for new repositories twice daily, at 12:00 AM and 12:00 PM UTC.

The supported agentic frameworks are CrewAI, n8n, OpenAI Agents, Langchain, and Pydantic AI.

To onboard a GitHub tenant, do the following:

1. Go to **Administration**> **Account Onboarding**.
2. Click + **Add New**. The **Start Onboarding** window appears.
3. Select **Code Repository**. See image.
4. In the **Select Code Repository** window, select the **GitHub** tile. See image. The **Add GitHub Tenant** window appears.
5. In the **Integration Alias**field, enter a user-friendly name to identify this integration.
6. Click **Authorize with GitHub.** See image. You are redirected to the GitHub account you are currently logged into.
7. Select the GitHub organizations you want to configure. See image.
8. Install and authorize the Zscaler GitHub integration app. You are prompted to install the integration app so that it can read metadata of GitHub and read files from your repository for scanning.
9. Choose the repository access scope from the following: See image.
  1. **All repositories**: All current and future repositories owned by the resource owner. This also includes public repositories.
  2. **Only select repositories**: Select one or more repositories. This also includes public repositories.
10. Click **Save**.
11. Return to the [Account Onboarding](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-account-onboarding) page to verify onboarding.

[Image: Select Code Repository in the Start Onboarding Window.]

[Image: Select GitHub as the Code Repository for Onboarding.]

[Image: Enter details in the Add GitHub Tenant Details page.]

[Image: Install the Zscaler AI Security app on the selected repositories.]

[Image: Select the GitHub organizations you want to configure the Zscaler app for.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-copilot-studio-tenant","lastmod":"2026-08-29T07:06Z","nid":"1541053"} -->
## Onboarding Microsoft Copilot Studio Tenant

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-copilot-studio-tenant
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > SaaS Platforms Onboarding > Microsoft Copilot Studio > Onboarding Microsoft Copilot Studio Tenant
- Last modified: 2026-08-29T07:06Z
- Summary: Information about adding Microsoft Copilot Studio tenant details in the AI Security Admin Portal.

Microsoft Copilot Studio onboarding in AI Security lets you quickly connect your Microsoft tenant so AI Security can discover and inventory Copilot Studio–related AI assets and surface security relevant findings in a centralized view. Using Account Onboarding, you authorize access to your Copilot Studio environment, assign a friendly tenant alias for identification, and complete the integration so AI Security can begin discovering agents and associated resources for monitoring and investigation.

## Prerequisites

Before onboarding a Microsoft Copilot Studio tenant, ensure you have completed the following:

1. Registered an app in the Azure Portal
2. Power Platform Admin Portal Setup
3. Created a Power Automate Flow

## Onboarding Microsoft Copilot Studio Tenant

To onboard a Microsoft Copilot Studio Tenant, do the following:

1. Go to **Administration**> **Account Onboarding**.
2. Click **Add New**. The **Start Onboarding** window appears.
3. Select **SaaS Platforms**.
4. Under **Select SaaS Platform**, click the**Microsoft Copilot Studio** tile. The **Add Microsoft Copilot Studio Tenant** window appears.
5. In the **Tenant Details** drawer:
  - **Tenant Alias:**Enter a unique name for the tenant as registered in the Azure Portal.
  - **Tenant ID:** Enter the Microsoft Entra tenant ID.
  - **Tenant Name**: Enter the name of the tenant that you want to onboard.
  - **Configuration Details:**
    - **Authentication Type:**Select one of the following from the drop-down menu.
      - Client Secret
      - Client Certificate
  - **Power Platform Environment URL:** Enter the environment URL available in the **Details**section of your environment in the [Power Platform admin center](https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com/manage/environments).
  - **Power Platform Environment ID:**Enter the environment ID available in the **Details** section of your environment in the [Power Platform admin center](https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com/manage/environments).
  - **Power Platform Region:**Enter the region name available in the **Details** section of your environment in the [Power Platform admin center](https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com/manage/environments).
  - **Business Units:**Select the business unit from the drop-down menu.
  - **Flow URL:**Enter the flow URL that is generated in Power Automate Flow.
  - Click **Add**to add multiple flows.
6. Click **Save**. See image.

The tenant is onboarded and is displayed on the [Account Onboarding](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-account-onboarding) page.

[Image: The onboarded tenant is visible in the Configured Integrations table.]

To register an app in the Azure Portal, do the following:

- 1. Create an app in Entra ID
- 2. Add a Client Secret or Client Certificate
- 3. Add API Permissions
- 4. Configure token

To create an app in Entra ID:

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com).
2. Go to **App Registrations**.
3. Click **+ New registration**. See image.
4. In the **Register an application** page:
  1. **Name:** Enter a unique name for the application.
  2. **Supported account types:** Retain the default selection.
5. Click **Register**. See image.

The application is registered and details are displayed on the **Overview**page. Copy the **Application (client) ID** details and ensure you have saved the details. The client ID is required while updating the Configuration Details in the AI Security Admin Portal.

See image.

To add API Permissions:

1. In the **All applications** tab, click the newly created application.
2. In the left-side navigation, go to **Manage >** **API permissions**.
3. Click + **Add a permission.**
4. In the**Request API Permissions**drawer,select **Microsoft Graph** >**Application Permissions**. See image.
5. Search and add all the six required permissions from **Microsoft Graph** (one by one). The list of permissions are:
  - Application.Read.All
  - AuditLog.Read.All
  - Directory.Read.All
  - LicenseAssignment.Read.All
  - User.Read.All
  - User.Read (by default)
6. After all permissions are added, click **Add permissions**.
7. In the **Configured permissions** section, click **Grant admin consent for <your Azure tenant name>.**
8. Verify all permissions show a **Granted**status (green checkmarks). See image.

To configure token (Optional claims):

1. Go to **Token configuration**.
2. In the **Optional claims** section, click **Add optional claim**.
3. In the **Add optional claim** drawer, select the **Token type** as **Access**.
4. Select the **aud** Claim and click **Add**. See image.

To add an application user and assign security role:

1. Go to the [Power Platform Admin Center](https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com/manage/environments).
2. In the left navigation, locate **Manage > Environments**.
3. Select the environment you want to onboard. See image.
4. Under **Access** > **S2S apps,**click **See All.** See image.
5. Click + **New app user.**
6. In the **Create a new app user** drawer, click**Add an app**. See image.
7. In the **Add an app from Microsoft Entra ID**, search for the application by the name registered in Create an app registration. See image.
8. Select the app and click **Add**.
9. Select the **Business Unit ID**. See image.
10. Under **Security Roles**, click **Edit** and assign the **Service Reader** role.
11. Click **Save** to confirm the role assignment.
12. Click **Create**. See image.
13. Verify that the **Service Reader** role appears under the app user's permissions. See image.

To create a flow URL:

- 1. Create an Instant Cloud Flow
- 2. Add Get Connection as Admin Action

To create an instant cloud flow:

1. Navigate to the **Power Automate flow** URL, e.g., https://make.powerautomate.com/environments/<env id>/flows.
2. Click **New Flow** > **Instant cloud flow**. See image.
3. In the **Build an instant cloud flow window**, enter a flow name.
4. In the **Choose how to trigger this flow** section, select the trigger as **When an HTTP request is received**.
5. Click **Create**. See image.
6. Click the **manual** trigger node.
7. In the **Parameters**tab, select **Specific user from my tenant**in the **Who can trigger the flow** field. See image.
8. Go to your Enterprise App, click **Overview > Managed Applications**, andcopy the **Object ID** of the application, and paste it into the **Allowed users** field in the flow. See image.

The Power Automate flow must be created in the same environment where you are onboarding to ensure that the connection details are discovered correctly.

To add Get Connections as an Admin action:

1. Click **+**to add a new step and action to the flow.
2. In the **Add an action** window, under the **Power Apps for Admins**section, locate and select the **Get Connections as Admin** option. See image. The **Get Connection as Admin** step is added.
3. Enter the **Environment ID** fetched from **Manage > Environments > Details** in the **Power Platform Admin Center**. See image.
4. To configure the **Response**step, search and add **Response** from the **Request** section. See image.
5. Copy the response body from the **Get Connections as Admin**output. See image.
6. Paste it into the response body field. See image.
7. Click **Save** to save the flow. A flow URL is generated.
8. Get the **Flow URL**from the Manual node. See image.
9. Click **Save**to save the flow.

Enter the following information:

- **Client ID**: The Application (client) ID you copied and saved from the **Overview**page in the Azure portal.
- **Client Secret**: The client secret created for the app registration.

[Image: Enter all the Client Secret fields.]

- Client secret
- Certificate

1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) or [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), click the newly created application.
2. In the left-side navigation, go to **Manage**> **Certificates & secrets**.
3. In the **Client secrets** tab, click **+ New client secret**.
4. In the **Add a client secret** drawer:
  - **Description**: Enter a description for the client secret.
  - **Expires**: Select the expiration time from the drop-down menu. By default, 180 days (6 months) is selected.
5. Click **Add**. See image. The client secret is generated and displayed. See image.
6. Copy the secret immediately and save it for later use.

1. Run any of the following commands in a CLI application:
  1. To generate an encrypted file
  2. To generate an unencrypted file
2. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) or [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), click the newly created application.
3. In the left-side navigation, go to **Manage**> **Certificates & secrets**.
4. In the **Certificates**tab, click **Upload certificate**.
5. In the **Upload certificate** drawer:
  - **Upload a certificate**: Upload the CER certificate file from your local folder.
  - **Description**: Enter a description.
6. Click **Add**.

1. To generate a private key (in 2048 bits) and save it to a specific file: `openssl genrsa -out <filename> 2048`
2. To generate a self-signed X.509 certificate using an existing private key that is valid for 365 days: `openssl req -new -x509 -key <filename>.key -out <filename>.crt -days 365 -subj "/CN=<filename>"`
3. To export the password for the newly created certificate: `openssl pkcs12 -export -out <filename>.pfx -inkey <filename>.key -in <filename>.crt`After you run the command, the following prompt appears: `Enter Export Password: Enter the export password`
4. To convert the CRT file type to CER and upload to the Azure portal or Microsoft Entra admin center: `openssl x509 -in <filename>.crt -out <filename>.cer -outform DER`
5. To create a PEM file from the CER file and upload it to the AI Security Admin Portal: `cat <filename>.key <filename>.crt > file.pem`

1. To generate a certificate and a corresponding RSA private key: `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -days 365 \ -keyout private.key \ -out certificate.crt \ -subj "/CN=my-sp-cert-password" \ -passout pass:*<password>*`
2. To combine the private key and certificate into a single PEM file: `cat private.key certificate.crt > combined.pem`

Enter the following information:

- **Client ID**: The Application (client) ID you copied and saved from the **Overview**page in the Azure portal.
- **Client Password**: The export password for the certificate.
- **Certificate File**: Upload the certificate file (PEM file) from your local folder or drag and drop the file.

## Onboarding a Microsoft Entra Tenant or Management Group

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant-or-management-group
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > Onboarding a Microsoft Entra Tenant or Management Group
- Last modified: 2026-06-25T07:12Z
- Summary: Information about how to onboard a Micorosft Azure tenant to AI Security Admin Portal.

You can onboard a Microsoft Entra tenant or management group and their associated subscriptions. AI Security monitors and [scans](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings) the data stores (e.g., databases, virtual machines, storage accounts) in the onboarded subscriptions to identify sensitive data, misconfigurations, and vulnerabilities.

## Prerequisites

Make sure the following prerequisites are met:

- In the Microsoft Entra Tenant
- On Your Local System
- In the AI Security Admin Portal

## Onboarding a Microsoft Entra Tenant

To onboard a Microsoft Entra tenant:

1. [Provide Microsoft Entra tenant details.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-microsoft-entra-tenant-details)
2. [Deploy the tree discovery template.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-tree-discovery-template)
3. [Select the orchestrator subscription and monitoring scope.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/selecting-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope)
4. [Deploy the onboarding template.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-azure-onboarding-template)

- **Orchestrator subscription**: Identify an [orchestrator](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-cloud-accounts) subscription on which the AI Security's orchestrator template is deployed to scan the data stores.
- Roles and permissions
- **Virtual machine instance type**: Ensure that you have the Standard_D2s_v3 virtual machine instance type in the region where the orchestrator template must be deployed. This is required to run the orchestrator instance.
- **Access management**: Enable Access management for Azure resources. This is required to manage access to all subscriptions and management groups in the tenant. Management group is a container for Azure subscriptions. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview). See instructions.
- **Microsoft Storage Resource Provider**: Register the Microsoft Azure Storage Resource Provider (Microsoft.Storage) in the subscription within which the orchestrator template is deployed. This is required for AI Security to validate the storage account created while onboarding. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/authorization-resource-provider). See instructions.
- **Storage containers**: Identify the storage containers where Terraform state files must be stored. The state files are required to manage resources created by the AI Security Terraform templates and to [upgrade to new templates](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-roles-and-templates). You can also create the following new storage containers to store the state files: Ensure to store the state files safely to upgrade to new templates. If the state files are lost or accidentally deleted, purge the resources, download and rerun the onboarding templates. See instructions.
  - Resource Group
  - Storage Account
  - Storage Account Container

Resource groups are logical containers that comprises a group of Azure resources. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/manage-resource-groups-portal).

To create a resource group:

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Resource groups**.
2. Click **+Create**.
3. On the **Basics** tab:
  1. **Subscription**: Select the orchestrator subscription from the drop-down menu.
  2. **Resource group**: Enter a unique name for the resource group.
  3. **Region**: Select a region where the resource group must be created.
4. Click **Review + create**.

Storage accounts store data objects such as files, queues, tables, and Terraform state files. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview).

To create a storage account:

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Storage account**.
2. Click **+Create**.
3. On the **Basics** tab:
  1. **Subscription**: Select your Azure subscription.
  2. **Resource group**: Select the resource group that you created.
  3. **Storage account name**: Enter a unique name for the storage account.
  4. **Region**: Select location where the storage account must be created.
4. Click **Review + create**.

A storage account container is a set of blobs similar to a directory in a file system. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blobs-introduction).

To create a storage account container:

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Storage account**.
2. Locate the storage account you created and click the storage account.
3. In the left-side navigation, under **Data storage**, select **Containers**.
4. Click **+Container**.
5. In the **New container** drawer:
  1. **Name**: Enter a unique name for the container.
  2. **Anonymous access level**: Select the access level for the container.
6. Click **Create**.

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Subscriptions**.
2. Click the **Subscription name** on which you want to deploy the orchestrator template.
3. In the left-side navigation, go to **Settings** > **Resource providers**.
4. Search for **Microsoft.Storage**, click the ellipsis and select **Register**.

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Microsoft Entra ID**.
2. In the left-side navigation, go to **Manage > Properties.**
3. Under **Access management for Azure resources**, click the toggle to **Yes**.

- Install the latest versions of Terraform and Azure CLIs to run the templates. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/install-azure-cli).
- Zscaler recommends you to enable the debug logs feature to identify issues encountered while onboarding. To enable debug logs, run the following commands:
  - PowerShell `$env:TF_LOG="TRACE" $env:TF_LOG_PATH="<filepath>filename.log"`
  - Bash `export TF_LOG="TRACE" $ export TF_LOG_PATH="<filepath>filename.log"`

You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with Add Accounts permissions in the AI Security Admin Portal.

1. Delete the following resource groups from the Azure portal:
  - z-ais-{integration-id}-auth-plane-rg
  - z-ais-{integration-id}-worker-plane-rg
  - z-ais-{integration-id}-control-plane-rg
2. Purge key vaults:
  1. Go to **Key vaults** and select **Manage deleted vaults**.
  2. Select the subscription where the resource groups were created.
  3. Select key vaults with the following format: `z-ais-{integration-id}-secrets`
  4. Click **Purge**.
3. Delete the following roles from the orchestrator subscriptions: You can find the role name from the **Roles and Templates** tab.
  - <role_name>-access-role
  - <role_name>-analyzer-role
  - <role_name>-orchestrator-role
4. Delete <role_name>-target-role from all the target subscriptions.
5. Delete **Read organization tree**role from the management group.
6. Delete **Key vault reader** assignment from AI Security Service principal in the management group.
7. Delete root level assignment in the management group by running the following command: `az role assignment delete --assignee "Service principal Application ID" --role "Management Group Reader" --scope "/'`
8. Delete the service principal created:
  1. Go to **Microsoft Entra ID**.
  2. In the left-side navigation, go to **Manage** > **App registrations**.
  3. Select **All applications**.
  4. Search for and delete the service principal.
9. From the **Roles and Templates** tab, download the Tree Discovery template, add new backend details, and run the template.
10. From the **Roles and Templates** tab, download the Azure Onboarding template, add new backend details, and run the template.

You must have the following roles and permissions:

| Onboarding Type | Role | Access Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tenant or Management group | Global Administrator | Root |
| Key Vault Administrator | Orchestrator subscription |  |
| Tenant | User Access Administrator | Root |
| Management group | Contributor | Orchestrator subscription |
| User Access Administrator | Management group |  |

The Key Vault Administrator role is required to perform operations on a key vault that stores secrets such as passwords, certificates, etc. and all objects in it. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-guide?tabs=azure-cli).

To assign the Key Vault Administrator role:

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Management groups**.
2. Select **Tenant Root Group**. This is the root management group that includes management groups and subscriptions of the Microsoft Entra tenant.
3. In the left-side navigation, select **Access control (IAM)**.
4. Click **Add** and then select **Add role assignment** from the drop-down menu.
5. In the **Add role assignment** page: A message appears indicating that the role was assigned to the selected member successfully.
  1. On the **Role** tab, select **Key Vault Administrator**from the table and click **Next**.
  2. On the **Members** tab, click **+Select members**.
    1. Locate the member you want to assign the role to and select the member name.
    2. Click **Select**.
  3. Click **Next**.
  4. On the **Conditions** tab, add any condition as required and click **Next**.
  5. Click **Review+assign**.

| Environment | Terraform Version | Azure CLI Version | PowerShell or Bash Version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mac | v1.10.3 | 2.65.0 | version 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin23) |
| Cloud Shell - Bash | v1.9.5 | 2.65.0 | version 5.1.8(1)-release (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) |
| Cloud Shell - PowerShell | v1.9.5 | 2.65.0 | 7.4.5 |
| Windows - Command line | v1.7.5 | 2.67.0 | NA |
| Windows - PowerShell | v1.9.8 | 2.67.0 | 7.4.6 |
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-standalone-aws-account","lastmod":"2026-06-15T07:09Z","nid":"1539940"} -->
## Onboarding a Standalone AWS Account

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-standalone-aws-account
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Account > Onboarding a Standalone AWS Account
- Last modified: 2026-06-15T07:09Z
- Summary: Information about how to onboard a standalone AWS account in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can onboard a standalone AWS account for AI Security to monitor and [scan](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings) the [data stores](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/supported-data-stores-file-types-and-regions) (e.g., S3, EC2 instances) to identify sensitive data, misconfigurations, and vulnerabilities.

## Onboarding Workflow

The onboarding workflow is as follows:

1. Provide the orchestrator account details, select the network configuration, and configure the regions where you want to deploy the local scanner. AI Security uses these details to generate a template in both CloudFormation and Terraform format.
2. Deploy the template on the orchestrator account. The template creates roles that provide AI Security with read-only permissions to access the account.
3. Add the target accounts that must be monitored and deploy the templates.

## Prerequisites

Before onboarding an AWS account, ensure you have completed the following:

- You must be assigned an Administrator role to onboard the AWS account.
- Identify an AWS account as the orchestrator account. The AI Security template is deployed in this account to scan the data in the target accounts.
- Configure[CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/understanding-aws-cloudtrail) for management and data events. This allows AI Security to perform incremental [data scans](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings) on S3 buckets. To enable data events for S3 buckets:
  1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **CloudTrail**.
  2. Under **Trails**, click the name of the CloudTrail that must be used to store data events.
  3. Under **Data events**, click **Edit**.
  4. For **All current and future S3 buckets**, select the **Write** checkbox.
  5. Click **Save changes**.
- You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/predefined-ai-security-roles-and-permissions) or any role with Add Accounts permissions in the Zscaler Admin Console.
- Select the [CloudFormation](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization#cfttemplate) or [Terraform Template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-aws-organization#tftemplate).

## Onboarding an AWS Account

To onboard an AWS account:

1. [Add orchestrator details and configure regions.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-orchestrator-details-and-configuring-regions)
2. [Deploy the orchestrator template.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-orchestrator-template)
3. [Add the target account and deploy the templates.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/adding-account-details-and-deploying-templates)
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/resetting-orchestrator-monitoring-scope","lastmod":"2026-06-01T21:06Z","nid":"1540255"} -->
## Resetting Orchestrator & Monitoring Scope

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/resetting-orchestrator-monitoring-scope
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > Resetting Orchestrator & Monitoring Scope
- Last modified: 2026-06-01T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about how to reset the orchestrator and monitoring scope.

If you want to reset the orchestrator or monitoring scope subscriptions after deploying the onboarding template, run the `terraform destroy` command to purge the template and delete any resource that was created.

To reset the configured subscriptions:

1. Select **Orchestrator & Monitoring Scope** and click **Reset**.
2. In the **Reset Configured Subscription** window, click **Confirm**.
3. [Configure new subscriptions.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/selecting-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope)
4. [Deploy the onboarding template.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-azure-onboarding-template)
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/resolving-configuration-issues-microsoft-azure","lastmod":"2026-06-24T21:06Z","nid":"1540253"} -->
## Resolving Configuration Issues for Microsoft Azure

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/resolving-configuration-issues-microsoft-azure
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > Resolving Configuration Issues for Microsoft Azure
- Last modified: 2026-06-24T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on the issues encountered while onboarding and troubleshooting for Microsoft Azure.

You might encounter any of the following error messages while onboarding:

| Error Messages or Issues | Resolution Steps |
| --- | --- |
| In the CLI app: `Role not found`; `Error: loading Role Definition List: could not find role <role name>`; ``Account in pending state from long time`` | Rerun the template. |
| In the AI Security Admin Portal: Admin consent has not been granted to the necessary APIs. Please provide consent to the necessary APIs. | [Grant API permissions to the service principal](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-tree-discovery-template#step2azureportal). |
| In the CLI app: ``Planning failed. Terraform encountered an error while generating this plan.``; ``Invalid value for input variable`` | Enter at least one [region](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/supported-data-stores-file-types-and-regions#azure-region) where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region 1", "region 2"]` |
| In the CLI app: ``User Assigned Identity (Subscription: <"ID"> \| Resource Group Name: <"name"> \| Name: <"managed-identity">) was not found`` | Delete the resource group and rerun the template. To delete the resource group: Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Resource groups**.; Search for and click the resource group.; Click **Delete resource group**.; On the **Delete a resource group** page:Review the resource group and dependent resources.; Copy the resource group name.; **Enter resource group name to confirm deletion**: Paste the resource group name. |
| In the CLI app: ``Error acquiring the state lock``; ``Error message: state blob is already locked \| Lock Info: <lock ID>`` | Run `terraform force-unlock <ID>` |
| In the CLI app: ``Error: authorization.RoleAssignmentsClient#Create: Failure responding to request: StatusCode=400 -- Original Error: autorest/azure: Service returned an error.``; ``Status=400 Code="RoleAssignmentLimitExceeded"``; ``No more role assignments can be created`` | The limit for role assignment is exceeded. Delete any custom role to accommodate new requests. To delete custom roles: Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Management groups**.; Click **Tenant Root Group**.; In the left-side navigation, click **Access control (IAM)**.; Select the **Roles** tab.; Click the **ellipsis** icon and select **Delete**. |
| In the CLI app: ``Error: Provider produced inconsistent result after apply``; ``When applying changes to <managed identity details>`` | Run the `terraform destroy` command to purge the template.; [Download and deploy the Azure onboarding template.](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-azure-onboarding-template) In the `backend.tf` file, ensure to use a different container. |
| In the CLI app: ``Error: local-exec provisioner error``; ``Error running command 'az role assignment create --assignee <Subscription ID> --role``; ``(AuthorizationFailed) The client <username> with object ID <object ID> does not have authorization to perform action or the scope is invalid`` | [Ensure that you have enabled access management for Azure resources for your ID](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant#entratenant-prereq). |
| In the CLI app: ``Error: deleting Subnet (Subscription: <"ID"> \| Resource Group Name: <"name"> \| Virtual Network Name \| Subnet Name)``; ``network.SubnetsClient#Delete: Failure sending request: StatusCode=400``; ``Subnet <Subnet name> is in use by </subscriptions/subscription ID/resourceGroups/Z-AIS-RG/providers/Microsoft.Network/networkInterfaces/.../> cannot be deleted`` | Delete resources manually in Azure portal. To delete the resources: Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Resource groups**.; Search for and click the resource group.; Click **Delete resource group**.; On the **Delete a resource group** page:Review the resource group and dependent resources.; Copy the resource group name.; **Enter resource group name to confirm deletion**: Paste the resource group name. |
| In the CLI app: ``Error: deleting Network Security Group <"ID"> (Resource Group name): network.SecurityGroupsClient#Delete: Failure sending request: StatusCode=400``; ``Error: Code="InUseNetworkSecurityGroupCannotBeDeleted``; ``Network security group cannot be deleted because it is in use by the following resources: <Resource details>`` | Delete resources manually in Azure portal. To delete the resources: Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Resource groups**.; Search for and click the resource group.; Click **Delete resource group**.; On the **Delete a resource group** page:Review the resource group and dependent resources.; Copy the resource group name.; **Enter resource group name to confirm deletion**: Paste the resource group name. |

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/running-demand-scan","lastmod":"2026-06-05T21:06Z","nid":"1540313"} -->
## Running an On-Demand Scan

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/running-demand-scan
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Administration > Scan Rules > Managing Scan Rules > Running an On-Demand Scan
- Last modified: 2026-06-05T21:06Z
- Summary: How to perform an on-demand scan of virtual machines or databases in the AI Security Admin Portal.

You can use the On-Demand scan option to run a scan instantly on the database or virtual machine. The On-Demand scan overrides the scheduled scan. To learn more, see [About Scan Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-scan-settings).

To run an On-Demand scan, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

1. Go to **Administration** > **Scan Settings**.
2. Select the **Scan Rules** tab.
3. Click the **Actions** icon () for the scan rule you want to run. See image.
4. Select the **On-Demand Scan** option. The **On-Demand Scan** confirmation window appears.
5. Read the message that appears, then click **Confirm**. See image.

[Image: Scan rule page with an annotation for On-Demand Scan action.]

[Image: Confirmation window to confirm the on-demand scan.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/selecting-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope","lastmod":"2026-06-18T21:06Z","nid":"1540184"} -->
## Selecting the Orchestrator and Monitoring Scope

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/selecting-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Account Onboarding > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > Selecting the Orchestrator and Monitoring Scope
- Last modified: 2026-06-18T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to select the orchestrator and monitoring scope in the AI Security Admin Portal.

After deploying the [tree discovery template](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-tree-discovery-template) when [onboarding a Microsoft Entra tenant](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/onboarding-microsoft-entra-tenant), select orchestrator and monitoring scope.

Under the **Orchestrator & Monitoring Scope** section:

- 1. Configure the orchestrator.
- 2. Set the monitoring scope.

To modify the configured accounts, click **Reset**.

When you have configured the network and scopes successfully, you are directed to the Additional Configuration section.

In the **Additional Configuration** section, you can configure custom tags and evidence storage. Click **Skip This Step**to configure the additional details after completing the onboarding process and go to [Deploy Orchestrator](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-orchestrator-template) section.

- Custom Tags
- Evidence Storage

After the configuration is completed, you are directed to the [Grant Permissions](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/deploying-azure-onboarding-template) section to deploy the templates.

AI Security discovers files and tables containing sensitive data and generates snippets of evidence data to investigate and validate the findings. You can choose an existing storage account container or add a new one to store these evidence snippets.

The storage account container cannot be changed after it is added.

To add evidence storage:

1. Click **Add Evidence Storage**.
2. On the **Evidence Configuration** page, select one of the following storage types:
  - Custom Managed Container
  - Zscaler Managed Container

You can use an existing storage account container to configure evidence data. AI Security uploads the snippet of evidence data into the specified container.

- **Storage Account Resource ID**: The resource ID of the storage account.
- **Container Name**: The name of the container.
- **Key Vault Resource ID**: The resource ID of the key vault. This key vault is used to encrypt the evidence data in the container.

AI Security creates a storage container in the orchestrator account to upload the snippet of evidence data.

Custom tags are attached to resources created by AI Security for easy identification.

To add custom tags:

1. Click **Add Custom Tags**.
2. On the **Add Custom Tags** page, enter a key and value pair for the tag. Ensure to follow the guidelines while entering key-value pairs for custom tags.
3. Click **Add More**, and enter key-value pairs to add more tags.
4. Click **Done**.

You can add up to 15 tags to Private DNS zone resources. If only numerical values are included in the tag, they do not count towards the 15-tag limit, allowing for additional tags to be added.

For Managed Identity, only predefined tags are added.

To configure the orchestrator, click **Configure Orchestrator**.

1. On the **Configure an Orchestrator Subscription** page, select a subscription to deploy the orchestrator template, then provide the following details:
  - **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select the region.
  - **Subnet ID**: Enter the subnet where the orchestrator instances must be launched.
  - **Network Security Group ID**: Enter the network security group for the orchestrator instance.
  - **Storage Account Name**: Enter a unique name for the storage account. This storage account is created while deploying the onboarding template and is used to store the activity logs of the target subscriptions. AI Security validates the uniqueness of the storage account name if Microsoft.Storage is registered. If the storage account name already exists, AI Security displays an error message. The storage account name cannot exceed 16 characters.
  - Select the **Deploy private endpoint for secure communication** checkbox to establish a private connection between AI Security and Azure resources. This restricts communication over public IP addresses. You can also establish or remove the private connection after onboarding the tenant. On the **Overview**page, select **Manage Private Endpoint** from the **Manage**drop-down menu, and then select or deselect the checkbox.
2. Click **Next**.
3. On the **Select which services to monitor** page, select the services that AI Security must monitor. By default, all the services are selected. AI Security permissions are restricted to monitor and scan the data only in the selected services. Select the **Leverage MIP Label** checkbox to allow AI Security to apply Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) sensitivity labels to Azure File Share. AI Security automatically excludes Azure Storage accounts used for storing logs.
4. On the **Configure Regions for monitoring and scanner's configuration** page: Remember the regionsthat you selected as you need to specify them while deploying the orchestrator template.
  1. For **Storage account**, specify whether you want to create storage accounts for each region or provide your own existing storage account details. If you want to use your own existing storage account for scanning logs, disable this option and provide storage account details for each region. When enabled, AI Security follows the standard workflow by creating the storage account for scan logs. This option is available only if **Storage** was selected on the Select which services to monitor page.
  2. Choose the regions that AI Security must monitor and enter the following details for each selected region. AI Security creates and deploys resources required for scanning only in the selected regions.
    - **Subnet ID**: Enter the subnet where the scanner instances must be launched.
    - **Network Security Group ID**: Enter the network security group for the scanner instance.
    - **Postgres Delegated Subnet ID**: (Optional) Enter the Postgres subnet ID for the scanner instance. This option is available only if **Database** was selected on the Select which services to monitor page.
    - **Storage Account Resource ID**: Enter the storage account name or account resource ID where you want to store the scanning logs.
5. Click **Done**.

1. Click **Set Monitoring Scope**.
2. On the **Configure Monitoring Scope** page:
  - Select the target subscriptions that AI Security must monitor.
  - Select the management group if all subscriptions must be scanned.
  - Select **Autodetection** at the management group level if you want AI Security to automatically include and scan new subscriptions that are added to the management group in the future. This eliminates the need to manually onboard new subscriptions.
3. Click **Next.**
4. On the **Assign Business Units** page, assign a [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/about-business-units) to the management group. All the subscriptions within the management group are mapped to the selected business unit. The default business unit is assigned to the management group. You can change the business unit for the management group if required, after completing the onboarding process.
5. Click **Done**.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/ai-asset-mgmt/signing-ai-security-admin-portal","lastmod":"2026-05-26T00:36Z","nid":"1540851"} -->
## Signing in to the AI Security Admin Portal

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/ai-asset-mgmt/signing-ai-security-admin-portal
- Product: AI Asset Management
- Path: AI Asset Management Help > Getting Started > Signing in to the AI Security Admin Portal
- Last modified: 2026-05-26T00:36Z
- Summary: How to sign in to and navigate the AI Security Admin Portal.

## Prerequisites

- An active Authentication Service user account (username and password).
- AI Security entitlement enabled for your user account to access the Zscaler AI Security Admin Portal.

You can access the AI Security Admin Portal in the following ways:

1. Login via AI Security URL
2. Login via Authentication Service Portal URL
3. Login via Experience Center

1. Open the **AI Security Admin Portal** (URL: https://ai-console.zscaler.com/dashboard).
2. You are redirected to the **Authentication Service** login page.
3. Enter your username and password.
4. After authentication, you are redirected back to the **AI Security Portal**.

1. Open the **Authentication Service Portal** (URL: https://<tenant>.zslogin.net/portal). The subdomain and domain may vary by tenant.
2. Enter your username and password.
3. From the portal, select **AI Security** to proceed.

1. Log in to the **Experience Center** (URL: https://console.zscaler.com).
2. Go to **Administration**> **Identity** > **Authentication Service**. In the **Authentication Service Portal**, click **AI Security**. You are redirected to the **AI Security Portal**.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->
